News.title: Posh beauty brand launches luxury dog range from £40 perfume to £80 wellness pack – and some items are already sold out
News.content:
Next

THESE could be the pawfect presents for your pampered pooch — part of a luxury range created especially for man’s best friend by posh beauty brand Rituals.

As well as alcohol-free perfume for £40, there are shampoos, paw treatments, grooming products and accessories in the Dog Spa range.



It also includes a £17 dry shampoo, a £14.90 dog mouth spray and a £22.90 air and fabric freshener.

There is even an £80 Dogstar wellness pack with the air and fabric freshener and shampoo plus wipes and paw balm — with a ball thrown in, too.



Despite the range only just going on sale, some items have already sold out online.

But don’t worry, they’ll be bark in stock soon.



Last month we revealed the extreme lengths paw-rents will go to for their dogs – including cooking them bespoke gourmet meals, talking to them as if they were a child, and giving them spa days.

A poll of 1,800 dog owners found other lengths they have gone to included letting them sit in the front seat of the car and purchasing luxury bedding for them.



Typically, owners spend an average of £101 per month looking after their pooch – and are willing to spend £36 on a one-off treat.

A spokesperson for free streaming service, U, which commissioned the research following the launch of its show Wagging Rights, said: “People look after their dog like they’re VIPs, and it’s fascinating to see just how pampered the nation’s pups have become, proving the lengths we would go to for our four-legged friends.

“For many owners, no expense is spared when it comes to keeping their dog happy, healthy and comfortable.

“From luxury dinners to luxury spa days, these findings reveal that Britain’s dogs are truly being treated like members of the family.”

News.title: ‘Petrified’ Deliveroo rapist who attacked semi-conscious woman refuses to leave his cell over fears of reprisals
News.content:
Next

A DELIVEROO rapist who attacked a semi-conscious woman is terrified of prison reprisals.

Algerian migrant Salem Rekoub refuses to leave his cell and has threatened to harm himself.



We revealed that smirking Rekoub, 28, dragged his victim off a street before raping her in Chelsea, West London.

Rekoub, who was working illegally for Deliveroo, is now said to be “petrified” of fellow prisoners at Wormwood Scrubs.



He is serving a 21-year term at the London jail.

A source said: “The whole prison knows what he’s done and what a coward he is.



“He won’t leave his cell and has threatened to self-harm to guards.

“That’s often an act by someone who wants to be looked after or moved to an easier location.

“But officers must take it seriously and monitor him.”

“There is a lot of hostility to him inside.



“His prison life will be tough while he is still in the UK.

“He is on a pretty cushy regime as well, and is allowed to spend hours in his cell watching TV and playing X-Box.”

News.title: Shabana Mahmood admits foreign worker visas are being requested every week by Cabinet ministers to plug urgent shortages
News.content:
Next

CABINET ministers are begging for foreign worker visas as often as every week because they cannot fill jobs with Brits, Shabana Mahmood has revealed.

The Home Secretary admitted her Labour colleagues routinely come to her asking for permission to bring in overseas staff to plug urgent shortages.



She accused departments of becoming too reliant on “pulling the immigration lever” rather than training workers already in Britain.

Ms Mahmood told The Rest is Politics podcast: “The sheer number of requests I get from colleagues across government from other departments – can I have 10 visas over here for welders or something?”



She added: “I’m like, you’re telling me that we can’t find 10 welders?

“But it’s become a lever that is easy to pull. And everyone always says, well, it’s urgent, and we haven’t got the time. And I just think we should be more in control here.”

Asked whether Cabinet ministers really contacted her asking for visas for workers such as welders, she replied: “I have a conversation like that at least once every week or two. It happens all the time.

“From their side of the equation, they’d be thinking, we’ve got to plug a gap really quickly.

“And this is the best way to do it really quickly. To which I would say you’ve got to be able to do a bit more long term planning for your workforce in your own country. This is how you end up with a million NEETs.”

The Home Secretary singled out social care, saying the sector was “riven with poor pay and conditions” and “often very abusive working conditions”.



But Ms Mahmood stressed Britain would still need workers from overseas where there was a genuine labour shortage.

She said ministers should first improve skills, workforce planning, pay and conditions in Britain before automatically reaching for more immigration.

Her comments come days after she signalled she could soften controversial plans to make some foreign workers wait longer for permanent residency.

The proposals would normally double the route to settled status from five to 10 years, while some health and care workers could face waits of up to 15 years.

Ms Mahmood has faced pressure from Housing Secretary Angela Rayner, more than 100 Labour MPs and unions, who say it would unfairly “move the goalposts” for migrants who came to Britain legally.

News.title: Kemi needs to make voters like the Tory party again as at least they are taking on the issues worrying them
News.content:
Kemi’s soaring







Next

LAST year the Conservatives went into their annual party conference with plotting rife and misery in the air — the gloom having failed to lift in the wake of 2024’s General Election hammering.

That the mood this year is very different is down to the increasingly impressive Kemi Badenoch.



While Sir Keir Starmer was busy squandering Labour’s undeserved landslide, Kemi transformed her party with the force of her personality and her steadfast political convictions.

The Tories are suddenly bristling with ideas to tackle the big issues — a plan for stopping illegal immigration; a plan to cut the unsustainable welfare bill; a plan to build more desperately needed prison places instead of releasing dangerous criminals early; a plan to properly fund defence; and a plan to kick-start growth.



Voters like Kemi personally, too. Polls make her the most popular party leader.

Now she and her revamped frontbench team need to make people also like the Tory party again, and convince them they have learned from past mistakes.

Hard as that is going to be, at least they are taking on the issues worrying voters.

Compare that to Labour’s conference when PM Andy Burnham had virtually nothing to say about defence, welfare, energy costs or economic growth.

Just a new way to fleece OAPs; a desire to rejoin the sclerotic EU; a dreamy longing to return to socialist chaos of the ’70s; and a wishy-washy sprinkling of “hope” vibes.

Fat of the land

THE PM’s ill-advised support for Man City’s mega-rich Abu Dhabi owners in the wake of the club being found guilty of serious financial rule-breaking gets murkier by the day.



It has been revealed that Manchester city council favoured the Abu Dhabi United Group with a ten-year “sweetheart” deal giving it first refusal on land identified by the authority for development — to the detriment of British firms.

That deal was signed by the council in 2015 — two years before Burnham became mayor — but he was only too happy during his tenure to bask in the glory of the resulting building projects.

He should expect the tough questions to keep coming.

Pint-sized help

ANDY Burnham likes to burnish his man-of-the-people image, talking nostalgically about pubs and his favourite bar snacks, but his 20 per cent cut in pub business rates planned for next April may be too little, too late to save many boozers.

One in five pubs faces closure without more help to offset the Government taxes that are making them unviable.



The hospitality industry generates almost £40billion for the economy and supports almost one million jobs.

The Government lets pubs die at its peril.

News.title: Cost of new-build homes set to be cut by £50k under proposed Tory plan to boost growth
News.content:
Next

PRICES of new-build homes will be slashed by up to £50,000 through a proposed Tory war on red tape.

Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith is vowing a blitz on bureaucracy and Net Zero regulations to halt low growth.



Proposals also include backing a third Heathrow runway and scrapping a £1.5billion grocery packaging tax to ease the cost of the weekly shop.

Mr Griffith said yesterday: “No one else is coming to save our economy. Only we can inject reality, tell the hard truths and make this a country we are proud to hand on to the next generation.”



The £50,000 price cut for new builds will partly come from scrapping rules such as the Future Homes Standard on reducing carbon emissions.

They make developers include low-carbon technology, such as heat pumps or district heat networks.



But Tory Party officials say this has been shown to increase the cost of building a detached home by more than £30,000.

It comes on top of leader Kemi Badenoch’s decision to abolish stamp duty on buyers’ main homes.

The Tories will also axe the Extended Producer Responsibility — or grocery tax — that forces manufacturers to pay for the costs of collecting and recycling packaging waste.

Labour’s new workers’ rights laws, which are set to cost businesses £1billion a year, will also be repealed by the Tories.



Mr Griffith, who will address the party faithful today in Birmingham, said: “Cheaper homes, lower taxes, and less red tape. This will be the most ambitious deregulation project in a generation.”

However Robert Jenrick, Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman, said: “The Tories are once again copying our policies.

“But they cannot raise the tax-free personal allowance to £15,000 because they refuse to cut migrant welfare, Net Zero subsidies and the ballooning benefits bill.”

News.title: Kemi’s new Iron Era shows that she is ready for the battle – but a snap election is the last thing she needs
News.content:
Next

IF a week is a long time in politics, then the past year has been a whole era for Kemi Badenoch.

The jury is out on whether this was an Ice Age that saw the Tories locked in the electoral deep freeze, or a Golden Age where an empress vanquished her rivals and flourished.



Badenoch arrived in Birmingham as arguably the most sure-footed of any Conservative leader in modern times.

Her position at the top is totally unassailable and the bars at the Tory Conference are disarmingly free of the usual bitching and backbiting.



This lack of internal competition has allowed her the breathing space to grow more confident in her own abilities.

For a fairly reserved woman, a subtle swagger is starting to seep into her interviews and Commons performances.



Is such confidence arrogantly misplaced? Badenoch’s critics certainly think she is living in cloud cuckoo land.

In the year since the Tory tribe last met, the party has nudged a mere blip from 17 to 19 per cent, according to Politico’s poll of polls.

Hundreds of councillors were put to the sword at the local elections, and the party crashed to fourth and fifth respectively in Wales and Scotland.

And while the Conservatives have bumbled along in third in national polls, there has been serious horsetrading at the top as Reform slipped from 30 per cent to 23 per cent, while Labour jumped from 20 per cent to 26 per cent.



These are the new political waters in which Badenoch is swimming. Her first year was spent tangling with a runaway Nigel Farage and a downtrodden Keir Starmer.

Now, she is dealing with a wounded Farage and an energised Labour under the new management of Andy Burnham.

How does Badenoch play her hand?

Aides point to three moments last year that cemented her leadership.

First, she brought the house down at the last party conference with a popular pledge to abolish stamp duty.



Next, she made mincemeat of Rachel Reeves with a devastating response to the “Benefits Street” Budget.

Finally, she ruthlessly dispatched Robert Jenrick from her Shadow Cabinet, punching the wind out of his planned defection. All three moments were glitzy, headline-grabbing events that put Badenoch up in lights.

There is no doubt they helped give her a hearing from a public that had stopped listening to the Tories.

But her team puts a higher premium on the painstaking legwork that happens behind the scenes. The stuff which nobody sees.

Badenoch is clear that nothing gets announced without being 100 per cent copper- bottomed.



Sometimes, this can be uncomfortable. Reform tore lumps out of her while she spent months conducting work on whether leaving the ECHR was feasible.

Everyone knew that quitting was a foregone conclusion, but Badenoch was determined to show she does not make policy on the fly. Short-term pain, long-term gain.

Ditto with stamp duty, and similarly with the current reluctance to make a commitment to bin inheritance tax without finding the money first.



Announcements are therefore political sushi: a juicy morsel on the surface, but built on a layer of substance.

This is where Team Badenoch hopes to find a gap.

Burnham is already proving himself a liability, forced to eat his words with metronomic regularity.

He wanted to bung billions to WASPI women, before rowing back when he learned of the cost.

Similarly, he railed against the personal allowance being too low, only to backpedal when handed the potential price tag.



The ban on drinking at football matches was a “discriminatory” disgrace that should be scrapped, until Burnham found himself on the wrong side of both fans and the police.

Man City’s owners were deserving of our sympathy and gratitude until the PM needed reminding they were guilty of industrial-level cheating.

Reopening the toxic Brexit debate would leave Britain “stuck in a permanent rut”, until he did just that.

It is difficult to know which Andy Burnham to believe.

Farage is trying to show himself as a serious contender for government by producing meaty documents to accompany each pledge he makes.



But he is constantly blown off course by various scandals that risk turning off wavering voters.

His conference was supposed to be a showcase of Reform’s first 100 days, but was upended by the Channel 4 sting on dodgy donations.

Farage is still dogged by claims he has too little to say on issues such as defence and healthcare. Stop the boats and you might also shoot his fox.

It is therefore clear why Team Badenoch sees obvious electoral mileage in being the diligent, patient antidote to chaotic times.

Rome was not built in a day, and her allies believe they are creating the foundations on which to build.



It includes outlining her “first principles” in a 95-page document released yesterday called The Right Way.

Perhaps this is Kemi’s Iron Age. It’s not flashy. It’s sometimes bloody. But it is a necessary period of development to make the next leap.

So, I was struck when Badenoch said last week she was readying her troops for an early election.

“We could be having a general election next May,” she prophesied.

She made the prediction trying to exude confidence and show she was up for the fight.



Deep down, however, the prospect of a snap poll must give her cold sweats.

A recent mega-poll projection found the Tories would only marginally increase their current lot if an election were held tomorrow, bagging just 130 seats, up from 118.

Research by More In Common shows that Brand Badenoch far exceeds Brand Tory, and that Kemi still has work to do in detoxifying her party’s image.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Undoing the damage from 14 years will be a marathon, not a sprint, however appealing it might be to spray out sexy policies to compete in the attention economy.

Badenoch knows this. But she must also know that the last thing she needs is an early election.

News.title: Flydubai ‘hijacker wanted to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport – and aborted earlier plot because friend was onboard’
News.content:
Next

THE pilot accused of hijacking an Israel-bound plane in a suspected terror plot reportedly dreamed of crashing into Tel Aviv airport and causing mass casualties, sources claim.

Hamam al-Hammami, 29, allegedly attacked captain Smit Machchhar with an onboard crash axe as he tried to take control of a Flydubai passenger jet.



Heroic passengers and crew grappled with the Omani co-pilot to regain control of the plane after it dropped 14,000ft in just 29 seconds.

Now, Israeli sources claim that al-Hammami confessed to plotting the terrifying 9/11-style attack before he was even accepted as a Flydubai pilot.



They also claim that he admitted he “tried to get hired” at several other airlines during his interrogation.

“The dream was to crash into Ben-Gurion Airport,” he added, a source told The Jerusalem Post.



Al-Hammami is said to have been frequenting the Tel Aviv airport during his time as a pilot.

One of his last visits to Israel took place around July and was allegedly used to gather intelligence in preparation for the attack.

He is believed to have intended to carry out the plot days later, but aborted the effort when he realised a crew member he was friends with was on board.

Al-Hammami had also allegedly considered crashing a plane into a tower block close to Israel‘s headquarters.



Israeli intelligence claimed he that he planned to kill Machchhar from behind the locked cockpit door before flying on to Tel Aviv, according to Italian outlet Corriere Della Sera.

The suspected hijacker would then fly into one of the Azrieli towers close to Israel’s military headquarters, the Kirya, in central Tel Aviv.

It is thought the attack intended to mimic the Al-Qaeda attack on New York’s Twin Towers on September 11, 2001.



Al-Hammami is said to have launched his attack around 10 minutes from the Israel border as the plane flew over Jordan, which would have given IDF fighter jets almost no time to intervene.

The claims come amid the revelation that al-Hammami called for violence against women while studying at a UK university.

He wrote that women “should be stomped on” in thousands of sick online rants posted while he was studying aviation management at Buckinghamshire New University in Wycombe.

The Omani national studied the course remotely from Muscat, Oman, according to The Telegraph.

An X account strongly linked to Al-Hammami advocated for severe punishments against women justified by reference to Islamic law, homophobic abuse and sexual humiliation.



The posts were made under the name “Pilot Hamam al-Hammami” and handle @PilotHamam.

In one he replied to a woman: “I’d stomp on your head, wipe the floor with you, make you an example to others, and then divorce you :).”

In another post he called a man a “coward and a scoundrel” for failing to violently assault his wife after catching her speaking to another man.



He said: “Anyone else would have stomped on her head and made her an example to others.”

Al-Hammami also detailed his mother’s struggle to find him a wife – a subject which appeared to infuriate him.

He tweeted more than 2,000 vile messages between November 2021 and August 2022 – while at the UK university, The Telegraph reports.

A spokesperson for Buckinghamshire New University told The Sun: “Our thoughts are with the injured pilot, crew and passengers involved in this incident.

“Hamam al-Hammami previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management. He did not undertake any pilot training at the University.”



After his attempt to crash the Flydubai jet with 182 people on board, investigators are now working to establish whether he acted as a “lone wolf or has any connection with any extremist groups”.

Al-Hammami had previously been banned from flying by Oman over fears he had adopted extremist views.

A LinkedIn profile bearing the name Hamam al-Hammami said he worked at Oman Air for seven years, leaving in February 2025, before joining Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and departing in January 2026.

Two posts were made to the profile, both published in quick succession on Wednesday – nine hours after the incident.

It is unclear who published the posts or whether they were scheduled in advance.



One included a video featuring a photo of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after the death of Osama Bin Laden.

This was followed with an image of Humam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawi, who killed nine people, including seven American CIA officers, in a 2009 suicide bombing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The second post featured an AI-generated image depicting Islam’s three holiest sites – in Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem.

Flydubai has grounded all flights to and from Israel as investigations continue.

News.title: Two boats carrying up to 120 migrants dock at UK town after crossing Channel as protesters chant ‘send them back’
News.content:
Next

TWO boats carrying up to 120 migrants have docked at a UK town after crossing the English Channel – as protesters chant “send them back”.

The vessels reached UK waters in Hampshire after appearing to set off from the Normandy coastline in France early on Sunday.



Hundreds of furious anti-migrant protesters watched from behind a police cordon as two RNLI boats carrying an estimated 120 asylum seekers docked in Gosport at 10.15pm.

The demonstrators shouted “send them back”, “you’re not welcome”, and “we don’t want you, f*** off back home” as the vessels arrived.



Around 300 across all ages were contained by a riot police cordon on Haslar Road, near to the harbour.

Around 20 minutes after the migrants arrived, tensions flared amongst protesters.

Red flares were let off as they pushed the line of officers backwards.

In scenes of chaos, a fight appeared to break out amid chants of “stop the boats” and “deport the f****** lot” as police officers stood poised with pepper spray in their hands.



Cops placed nails on the road to prevent protesters from driving to the barricade after one car appeared to drive towards police at a slow speed.

Toby, 26, a chef who lives just streets away, said: “I was at home having a few drinks and then I saw on Twitter that this was happening so I thought I’d come down.

“I hadn’t been to the last ones. There are a lot of people that take it too far, but how can you trust the police when they’re doing this?

“They’re hiding the entire process from us because they know it’s wrong.

“You see all these people in France and they’ve just been let in. We’ve seen what they’re capable of. It’s affecting the whole country but Gosport is getting the worst of it.”



The migrants were taken from the boats and formed a long queue before they could be processed, with some appearing to wear orange rescue clothing.

They were then taken into a large building and two white coaches were seen next to the building, believed to be their transport.

Dave, a construction worker who lives in the area had been shouting for the crowd to join him in pushing back the police.



He said: “If we all did it, they wouldn’t be able to stop us. If it’s just me I’ll get nicked.

“I’ve worked all my life, paid all this tax, for it to go to people who have never lived or worked here.

“I’ve built houses that go straight to people that never worked. They are houses I couldn’t have.”

Another man, who wanted to remain anonymous, said: “If we were calm they would nick us. We have to be aggressive for our own protection.”

Authorities had been preparing for the arrival on the south-coast after the migrants were shadowed by the French coastguard.



Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said it had deployed officers to Gosport to “support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea”.

The force has imposed conditions under the Public Order Act as well as powers prohibiting the wearing of face coverings.

On Sunday evening, Conservative MP for Gosport Caroline Dinenage called on the Home Secretary to divert any illegal vessels “directly to Dover by water”.



“The Home Office proved just two weeks ago that this can be done,” she said.

“Gosport is not a safe or suitable location to disembark small boats. Our transport network is extremely constrained, we have no acute hospital, and our emergency services are already under pressure.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “The Border Security Command works around the clock to monitor the Channel and protect our border.

“It is vital we continue to detain, check and process every small boat arrival.”

This is the third crossing from Normandy in the space of the last month – which has led to a series of protests and arrests.



Last month, British rescue boats collected the passengers of a migrant dinghy which had spent around 30 hours at sea after setting off from Normandy.

The 51 migrants, who refused help from the French coastguard, arrived in Dover after being transferred to Border Security Command boats.

It was expected the migrants would be taken to Gosport, with hundreds of protesters gathering after coaches and ambulances were spotted in the area – six people were arrested by officers during the evening.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The provisional total for Channel crossings this year is 19,451.

This is down 43% on this time last year and 23% below the figure at this stage in 2024.

News.title: Andrew ‘will take police to court’ over Sandringham Estate home raid that led to arrest
News.content:
Andrew ‘will take police to court’ over Sandringham Estate home raid that led to arrest

The former Prince, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, was arrested on his 66th birthday in February of this year, a few weeks after the King removed his dukedom and titles

View 2 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor lost his titles in late 2025 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is set to take Thames Valley Police to court over allegations that searches of his homes may have broken the law, it has been reported.

‌



‌



The former Duke of York has been granted permission to challenge whether the force acted lawfully over the searches relating to his arrest in February, according to The Telegraph. Andrew’s application for a judicial review is said to have been made earlier this year and recently approved by a High Court judge.

‌



The King’s brother will challenge the legality of search warrants that allowed police to raid his residence on the Sandringham Estate and his former Windsor home, Royal Lodge, according to the report.

‌



It also said a private High Court hearing held in the coming days will decide whether to release certain court documents relating to the judicial review.

View 2 Images Unmarked vehicles enter the gates of the Royal Lodge a day after Andrew's arrest (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Andrew was arrested on his 66th birthday on suspicion of misconduct in public office following allegations he shared sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein during his time as the UK’s trade envoy.

The King stripped his brother of both his right to be a prince and his dukedom late last year over his association with the convicted sex offender.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Thames Valley Police have been approached for comment.

News.title: UK 'desperately needs mass food storage sites in case of national emergencies or war'
News.content:
UK 'desperately needs mass food storage sites in case of national emergencies or war'

Experts have called on the government to ramp-up planning for a possible mass impact on UK food chain - warning households can't afford to stockpile

View 4 Images Failure to prepare for a national food emergency risks shortages - or worse (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Britain should set-up a network of food storage sites to ensure families have enough to eat in the event of a national emergency, a group of 150 experts and others have urged the Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

‌



‌



It came as they warned the country had “no plan” for feeding the country if there was a major crisis, whether due to climate change, a devastating cyber attack or even war.

‌



While drastic, they say alarm bells should already be ringing given what happened during the Covid crisis, which led to panic buying, through to the threat of shortages and price risks following this summer’s record drought and forecasts chaos from the looking El Nino weather phenomenon.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images The UK's parched summer exposed the impact of climate change on the country (Image: Jacob King/PA Wire)

Top academic Professor Tim Lang, one of the leading signatories of the letter to PM and First Secretary Louise Haigh, warns the country risked “sleepwalking” into a crisis unless action is taken immediately. Without proper planning, he said there was the risk of riots and widespread civil unrest.

‌



The letter, signed by academics, businesses, civil leaders, and campaigners, has been sent ahead of today’s call for evidence deadline on updating the Civil Contingencies Act 2004, which allows the government to make last minute and drastic legislative changes on an unprecedented scale. Those behind the letter argue the Act fails to treat the food supply as a national security issue, despite mounting warnings from both within and outside the sector.

They argue that, for those can afford it, there is ready access to food, even though is highly concentrated in the hands of a relatively small number of producers and retailers, and is reliant on imports. However, they warned the UK was entering “a new era in which food supplies will be disrupted, public expectations may not be met and food can be weaponised”.

Among their recommendations is the creation of national, regional, local and community food storage schemes, rather than leaving households to stockpile food. Britain had a network of such sites after the Second World War, but these began to be wound down after the country joined the EU as they were deemed surplus to requirements, and were eventually scrapped altogether in the 1990s.

‌



Professor Lang, a leading expert in food policy City St George’s, University of London, and lead author of the National Preparedness Commission’s Just in Case report, warned the government needed to prepare as it might for war.

View 4 Images The food chain, and other industries, risk the ever-present danger from cyber attacks (Image: Getty Images)

“Everyone in the food system knows that shocks are coming and we are not preparing for them like other countries are doing,” he said. For example, Switzerland has three months’ worth of essentials foodstuffs stockpiled, he said.

‌



The UK’s Prepare website suggests households having enough non-perishable food that doesn’t need cooking, such as ready-to-eat tinned meat, fruit or vegetables, for an emergency lasting “a few days”.

Professor Lang called the advice “hopeless” given many people do not have enough to eat already, let alone stockpile food.

“This is ludicrous,” he said. “You can’t have resilience to individual households are the sole last line of defence.” He said a “just in time” system, meaning groceries are not ordered until as late as possible before they are needed, exposed the UK to even greater risk.

‌



View 4 Images Prof Tim Lang: “Everyone in the food system knows that shocks are coming and we are not preparing for them like other countries are doing." (Image: BBC/RAW Productions)

The danger was highlighted last year when Marks & Spencer and the Co-op were targeted by cyber criminals, resulting to a hit in supplies to both.

“Britain has got this hyper-efficient, super-concentrated food system and every insider knows it,” he said. “The danger is Britain sleepwalks into multiple crises. The worst case scenario, as food insiders say, is riots, it is deep anxiety, it is community against community, it's social division."

‌



Among the letter’s other recommendations is for a new system of local “food resilience committees”, tasked with preventing and mitigating food supply disruptions at the local level. It also suggests renaming the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs but ditching the last part in favour of “food security”.

Professor Paul Behrens, from the University of Oxford said: “The Government’s own national security assessment says the UK ‘does not have enough land to feed its population and rear livestock: a wholesale change in consumer diets would be required’. “That is Whitehall’s own analysis but there is still very little action on this. Food resilience, healthy diet, and environmental benefits all point the same direction: grow more of the vegetables, fruit and pulses people actually need, closer to home.”

Carina Millstone, executive director at the charity Foodrise, said: “Amidst severe geopolitical tensions and the fast worsening climate and environmental crises, food corporations have led us to an impasse that threatens the UK’s food and farming.

‌



“The signatories to this letter call for leadership from the Prime Minister to boost the nation’s food resilience and security without delay.”

A government spokesperson said: “Food security is national security which is why we're ensuring food supply is fully incorporated into our emergency preparedness planning.

"We are taking action now to deal with the impacts of extreme weather - one of the Prime Minister's first visits was meeting farmers hit by recent drought, announcing a £65million package to boost resilience.

Article continues below

"We’re also going further to address the risks of climate change, including a new taskforce to strengthen climate security and working with farmers and industry to build supply chains that can withstand future shocks."

The Cabinet Office announced plans in July fir a campaign to raise awareness of the simple steps households can take to keep themselves safe in everyday emergencies, bringing the UK into line with European countries which run similar campaigns already, with more information expected.

News.title: Domestic abusers to be flagged by courts to better track vile criminals
News.content:
Domestic abusers to be flagged by courts to better track vile criminals

Domestic abuse is already recognised as an aggravating factor in a wide range of offences, such as assault or stalking - but until now there has been no consistent way to record it

View 2 Images More than 700 prisoners were freed early from jail last week as part of the first tranche of the early release prison scheme (Image: © 2026 PA Media, All Rights Reserved)

Courts will be ordered to record when an offence involves domestic abuse to better track offenders and beef up protections for victims.

‌



‌



For the first time, perpetrators will be formally flagged as domestic abusers in the system to manage the risks they pose and identify patterns of repeat offending.

‌



Domestic abuse is already recognised as an aggravating factor in a wide range of offences, such as assault or stalking, but until now there has been no consistent way to record it once an offender is convicted.

‌



Frontline staff - including police and probation officers - will now be able to see domestic abuse flags on a criminal’s profile on their system to help them better manage risks.

Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones said: “Too many victims have suffered because patterns of abusive behaviour have not always been recognised across the justice system.

Prisoner re-arrested immediately after leaving jail as hundreds released early from prisons READ MORE :

View 2 Images Justice Secretary Alex Norris (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

‌



"This is an important step towards better identifying dangerous perpetrators, protecting victims and delivering on our commitment to halve violence against women and girls."

London’s Victims’ Commissioner Andrea Simon welcomed the new specific domestic abuse flag, especially given the early release of thousands of offenders.

She said: “Within the context of early prison releases, it is vital that justice agencies can effectively identify and respond to the risks posed by domestic abuse perpetrators and put the right interventions in place to protect victims from further harm.”

‌



More than 700 prisoners were freed early from jail last week as part of the first tranche of the early release prison scheme.

Victims’ groups have raised concerns over the effectiveness of safeguards. On Sunday, Justice Secretary Alex Norris was unable to say how many prisoners freed early from jail have been tagged.

Officials said there was a presumption that all criminals released early would be fitted with GPS tags, but Mr Norris said it was “too soon” to have the numbers.

‌



Asked how many of those released so far had been tagged, Mr Norris told the BBC : “I don’t have that figure today, it only happened on Thursday. You know, there can be a bit of a lag. We don’t have that number. But you know, we’re very candid about who’s leaving prison and when they do.”

Asked if he knew if released domestic abusers have been tagged or not, he said: “It would be too soon to know that, as it was only on Thursday. We’ve been talking to every victim to to offer them the chance to say what controls they’d like to see over that individual.”

Nearly 5,000 prisoners are set to be freed in stages over the next year under the plans.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, Mr Norris also insisted the courts backlog will still be slashed despite ministers U-turning on controversial plans to curb jury trials. He said introducing legislation for judge-only trials would have been “complicated to implement” and would slow down other planned reforms.

Former Justice Secretary David Lammy had previously told MPs the reforms were “desperately needed” to prevent victims facing “agonising delays”.

News.title: KEVIN MAGUIRE: 'Kemi Badenoch’s tax cuts for the wealthy prove the Tories still put the rich first'
News.content:
Fat tax handouts for the highest earners plucked from a phantom magic money tree are proof that under Con woman Kemi Badenoch the Tory Party hasn’t changed.

Championing the fortunate few over the struggling many is traditional Two Nation feather-bedding from a dictatorial leader imposing an intolerant cult to rival fellow Thatcherite Nigel Farage’s tyrannical grip of Reform.

Lurching to the Hard Right, parading as an upmarket defender of vested interests against a poundshop Farage, isn’t pretty and it’s a political strategy that deserves to backfire spectacularly.

Because Nasty Party-bashing of the have-nots and migrants while showering supposedly free money on the already haves doesn’t add up financially or politically if centre voters with good values are repelled.

‌



View 2 Images Where will this endless supply of money fall?

Badenoch is showering tax cuts like confetti and, should she somehow miraculously tie the knot at the election and move into Downing Street, the marriage would be extremely unhappy when she hasn’t the cash to stick by paper vows.

A potential £9billion inheritance windfall for the lucky one in 20 death lottery winners who are currently pocketing up to £1million tax-free is a priority warped to enhance inequality.

Or spending £1.4bn subsidising the private education fees of the one in 14 pupils whose parents shun the real public schools teaching 93% of kids.

‌



I believe strongly in progressive universalism – all of us paying into the system according to our means and benefiting according to our needs, yet committing £700m to fund free childcare for people on £100,000-plus by erasing a Tory cut-off wouldn’t be top of my list.

Then there is last year’s £9bn scrapping of house purchase stamp duty plus the reintroduction of tourist VAT-free bungs on Armani, Louis Vuitton and other luxury goods – dumping another Con policy that reputable experts warn would cost British taxpayers £600m.

Badenoch has a dismal record in government, Farage mini-me values and wealthfare policies that should be sounding alarm bells among those seduced by a newly-developed smileyness.

King of South?

Bolstered by a poll giving Labour (30%) clear leads over fading Reform (25%) and distant Cons (17%), if Andy Burnham triumphs in the South this week, the King of the North will look a ruler of the whole country.

‌



Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali successfully defending on Thursday a 11,500 majority in London’s Holborn and St Pancras after Keir Starmer did a runner would confirm Burnham’s revived his party nationally by uprooting Zack Polanski’s Greens.

And what a result when eight months ago the Greens turned Labour’s Gorton and Denton 13,000 majority into a 4,400 walloping.

News.title: Debris field found in search for missing medical plane near Nantucket
News.content:
Debris field found in search for missing medical plane near Nantucket

The Canadian air ambulance vanished over the Atlantic as it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston in the early hours of Saturday

View 2 Images In this photo released by US Coast Guard, crew members search by air and on the water for a Boston-bound air ambulance that vanished off the coast of Nantucket (Image: U.S. Coast Guard via AP)

Coast guard search and rescue teams have said it's difficult to say "exactly what" is in a debris field found in the search for a medical plane that disappeared while transporting a patient.

‌



‌



The Canadian air ambulance vanished over the Atlantic as it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston in the early hours of Saturday. The aircraft had six people on board and disappeared off the coast of Massachusetts as a large search and rescue operation remains ongoing.

‌



The plane plummeted 14,000ft in two minutes according to flight data, disappearing around 1.30am on Saturday. Two Canadian pilots, two Canadian medical workers and a patient from Bermuda and their relative were on board the Ontario-registered aircraft.

‌



The US Coast Guard earlier said a "debris field" associated with the aircraft has been found off the coast of Nantucket. But in an update issued this afternoon, officials said the amount of components discovered has made it difficult to identify "exactly what's there", CBC - the Canadian national broadcaster - reports.

View 2 Images A US Coast Guard C-144 jet and helicopter are searching an area south of Nantucket (Image: FlightRadar)

Lt.-Cmdr. Kastriot Kastrati, who is in charge of co-ordinating the search and rescue mission, said the size of the debris field has made it "very difficult to get into the details of what's there". The field was discovered about 20 miles off the coast of Nantucket, with the water in the area reportedly being 24 to 28 metres deep.

‌



Teams are now solely focusing on finding the six missing people. US Coast Guard Rear Admiral Matt Lake said: "Our priority is to find the six personnel on that aircraft."

"Right now, we're really just focused on finding the people," added Lt.-Cmdr. Kastrati.

The aircraft's black box has also not yet been located as crews continue searching the debris field. Mr Lake refused to speculate on the possible cause of the crash, saying this would be part of an upcoming investigation.

‌



The Gulfstream G100 took off from Bermuda’s L.F. Wade International Airport and was due to land at Boston Logan International Airport. Air traffic audio indicates the plane may have been ‘coming in blind’ shortly before it vanished.

In the audio shared by LiveATC.net, an air traffic controller can be heard asking the pilot at 12.46am: "Roger, you said you're 'coming in blind.' Is that what you said?"

The pilot is understood to have reported electrical problems and declared an emergency as the plane approached the coast. "Are you declaring an emergency or no? You’re coming in a little weak so I didn’t hear what your response was," the controller went on to ask, but received no response.

Article continues below

Cpt. John Mctamney, chief of response for the US Coast Guard's northeast district, said crews will continue their search "until we're at the point where if there were any survivors on the surface of the water, we're confident we would have found them."

News.title: Christa Pike lawyer gives health update days after botched execution
News.content:
Christa Pike lawyer gives health update days after botched execution

The 50-year-old has remained under guard in hospital since Wednesday night’s failed execution attempt, as doctors try to get a massive dose of the barbiturate pentobarbital out of her system.

View 3 Images (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction/AFP via Getty Images)

Christa Pike's lawyer has issued a health update, four days after her botched execution in Tennessee.

‌



‌



Assistant federal defender Stephen Ferrell confirmed that Pike has not regained consciousness and remains on a ventilator in hospital.

‌



The 50-year-old has remained under guard in hospital since Wednesday night’s failed execution attempt, as doctors try to get a massive dose of the barbiturate pentobarbital out of her system. Little has been released about Pike’s condition since she survived the lethal injection.

‌



Asked whether she had regained consciousness following the execution attempt, assistant federal defender Stephen Ferrell said: “Not that I am aware of.”

Her lawyers have warned that it could be several days before they know whether she will recover. Pike gave someone medical power of attorney and that person is protecting her privacy, Mr Ferrell said.

View 3 Images (Image: Tennessee Department of Correction)

‌



“I’m not sure what all they may have told that person,” he said. Pike’s lawyers have not identified who is making medical decisions on her behalf.

They said they may not know for several days whether she could recover from the botched execution.

“We don’t know right now, and we may never know what sort of torture she endured during that process, where her consciousness was, what physical pain there was, what mental torture she went through,” Mr Ferrell said.

‌



Ferrell told CNN on Sunday that the Pike’s death sentence should be changed to a life sentence “at the very least.”

“I think one of the main things that will leave this up in the air for a while is the fact that we don’t know what the prognosis is, as in, the long-term prognosis,” he said.

“If she recovers, she may not fully recover, and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don’t know any of this.”

‌



A spokeswoman for Pike’s defence team said early on Sunday: “We appreciate all respect for Christa’s rightful privacy.”

Tennessee prison officials gave Pike two doses of the lethal injection drug on Wednesday night. The pentobarbital did not kill her, but her lawyers said her arms were burned and blistered by the caustic drugs.

Pike was 18-years-old when she and her boyfriend tortured and killed classmate Colleen Slemmer in a jealous rage in 1995. She became one of the youngest women to be sent to death row.

‌



Her execution was delayed for more than eight hours on Wednesday as the US Supreme Court considered, and ultimately overturned, a federal appeals court ruling that had halted her lethal injection.

The appeals court had wanted to thoroughly review whether the jury that sentenced Pike to death should have considered sexual abuse she said she suffered as a child. Her lawyers asked a court on Friday to order Tennessee prison officials to preserve any written records, communications, images or video from the execution.

View 3 Images (Image: AP Photo/George Walker IV)

‌



Tennessee, like many other states with capital punishment, keeps many details about executions secret from the people involved, including how the drugs are manufactured or obtained and any tests carried out on their quality.

“The state of Tennessee has got to start telling its people exactly what it is doing so that in the democratic process, the people of Tennessee can decide if that’s what they want to be done in their name,” Mr Ferrell told CNN.

Pike's failed execution was the second time this year Tennessee has been unable to execute a prisoner who was seemingly moments from death. In May, officials stopped the execution of Tony Carruthers after staff placed an IV into his right arm but could not get a secondary line.

‌



Frank Strada, commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Correction, announced on Saturday that he was resigning. Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent investigation into the state's capital punishment system, to be conducted by former US attorney Ed Stanton.

Mr Stanton also reviewed Tennessee's execution procedures after Mr Lee called off a different execution in 2022 and found the state had not complied with its own lethal injection process. Prison officials and the Tennessee Attorney General’s Office have said little since Pike was taken to hospital.

If she recovers, it is unclear what will happen in her death penalty case. Her lawyers have asked the governor to commute her punishment to a life sentence.

Article continues below

Pike did not deny killing 19-year-old Ms Slemmer in 1995. The pair were classmates at Knoxville Job Corps.

Prosecutors said Pike feared Ms Slemmer was a romantic rival and lured her to a secluded area where she and her boyfriend slashed her with a box cutter and beat her with a large piece of asphalt.

The case attracted widespread attention because of the brutality of the killing, the ages of those involved and the fact a satanic symbol was carved into the victim’s body.

News.title: Noah's Ark site mystery as 'underground corridors' found beneath Turkey
News.content:
Noah's Ark site mystery as 'underground corridors' found beneath Turkey

US expert Dr Khosrow Bakhtar said he is '100 per cent sure' the organised patterns discovered at the Durupınar formation in Turkey come from the same object

View 3 Images The Durupınar formation in Turkey is a large, boat-shaped geological formation located about 29km south of Mount Ararat (Image: NoahsArkScans.com / SWNS)

New mysterious "underground corridors" have been found at a site in Turkey where remains of Noah's Ark are said to be located.

‌



‌



The discovery comes as US expert Dr Khosrow Bakhtar claims he has detected an array of unnatural, organised patterns buried deep beneath the surface. He described the findings as an "anomaly".

‌



Dr Bakhtar said: "This is the most significant finding for 40 years of my career. I have never seen this kind of anomaly before."

‌



The veteran scientist made the discovery discovery using his high-tech subsurface scanner called the "BakhtarRadar". The scanner was used on the famous Durupınar formation in Turkey as the radar removes geological noise such as rocks and dirt.

View 3 Images Scans showing possible corridors and rooms within the Durupınar formation (Image: NoahsArkScans.com / SWNS)

Dr Bakhtar's findings also include massive underground corridors and chambers running through the 515-foot boat-shaped mound near the Mountains of Ararat, the Express reports.

‌



Other scientists, however, have previously dismissed the Durupınar formation as a natural geological quirk. But Dr Bakhtar said: "If the anomalies were not important, we would not have seen them at all.

"But the fact that they showed so clearly indicates that they come from something. I am a hundred per cent sure that they come from the same original object."

He added: "As we entered the boat, we identified a very strong interface, which is a very dark line going all the way down. If you look at the strength of the signature, it doesn't matter what depth you're looking at, they all have the same strength.

‌



"We can quantify the repeated anomalies that, when you connect them, form corridors. Because of that, I think all the anomalies are related to one particular object."

View 3 Images In biblical terms, Noah’s Ark is the vessel that, according to the Book of Genesis, Noah built to survive a catastrophic flood (Image: NoahsArkScans.com / SWNS)

The results were released by the research group Noah's Ark Scans, which boldly declared that the site is "100 per cent not geological." Dr Bakhtar, however, said he remains open-minded about what actually made the mysterious outline.

Article continues below

His comments came after an international expedition, jointly authorised by the Turkish government, ramped up physical work at the site. Researchers have begun coring and drilling into the formation to pull up soil and rock samples for laboratory testing.

But geologists insist that extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, leaving the world waiting on the lab results to see if Dr Bakhtar's mysterious "corridors" really are the remains of Noah's Ark.

News.title: 'Trainee shaman' jailed after drugs from Peru 'medicine man' sent to home
News.content:
'Trainee shaman' jailed after drugs from Peru 'medicine man' sent to home

The discoveries prompted officers to raid Kinta's home, where they uncovered what police described as a 'home laboratory' in a front bedroom

View 3 Images

A 'trainee shaman' had kilos of a Class A psychedelic drug posted from a 'medicine man' in Peru to his home in the Midlands.

‌



‌



Scott Kinta had six packages sent to his former home in New Ollerton, Nottinghamshire, with the parcels intercepted by Border Force officers at Coventry Airport last year.

‌



Each of the packages contained around four kilograms of N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT), a Class A drug. A further package, which had been sent by Kinta to an address in Texas, was also intercepted.

‌



The discoveries prompted officers to raid Kinta's home, where they uncovered what police described as a 'home laboratory' in a front bedroom. The room contained a forensic unit, bottles, jars, petri dishes, syringes, scales and packaging materials.

Similar items were also found elsewhere in the property, giving officers further evidence of Kinta's alleged involvement with the drugs.

Police then examined Kinta's mobile phone and found incriminating conversations with a contact, reports Coventry Live.

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Nottinghamshire Police)

Kinta later pleaded guilty to being concerned in the supply of Class A drugs and being concerned in the fraudulent evasion of a prohibition on the importation of a Class A drug. He told police that the drugs had been imported from a 'medicine man' in Peru.

Kinta said he had agreed to receive the packages in return for future training in shamanic and tribal healing practices.

‌



His unusual explanation formed part of the circumstances surrounding the case, with police later warning of the serious consequences of importing and exporting Class A drugs.

Kinta, of Yorke Street, Mansfield Woodhouse, appeared at Nottingham Crown Court on Wednesday, September 28.

He was jailed for five years.

‌



Speaking after the case, Detective Constable Joel Hughes said people involved in importing illegal drugs were normally more cautious when conducting their business.

He said: "For obvious reasons, people involved in the importation of illegal drugs are usually more cautious when doing business. Kinta, however, was literally having packages of Class A drugs delivered to his own front door and was similarly open in sending the drugs on from his local Post Office.

View 3 Images (Image: Nottinghamshire Police)

‌



"He may well have been motivated by his interest in shamanic rituals but, as he has just discovered to his cost, the punishments for importing and exporting Class A drugs will always be very severe."

The case involved packages travelling thousands of miles from Peru before being intercepted by Border Force officers at Coventry Airport. Officers were then able to link the parcels to Kinta's former address and carry out further enquiries.

The contents of the packages, along with the equipment found inside his home, helped investigators build a case against him.

Article continues below

The court heard how Kinta's interest in shamanic and tribal healing practices had been connected to his explanation for receiving the drugs from Peru.

However, he was ultimately convicted of offences relating to the supply and importation of Class A drugs and sentenced to five years in prison.

News.title: US removes all bombers from RAF Fairford base
News.content:
The US has withdrawn all of its bombers from RAF Fairford, the British military base at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter terror police.

A statement from a US department official confirmed on Sunday it had removed all of its bombers from the base back to their home stations in America.

The US did not give a reason for the withdrawal, but it follows a major incident on 27 September when police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences near the base and subsequently released on police bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Whitehall sources have not disputed the decision from Washington was in response to the incident at RAF Fairford.

The BBC has also been told it was a military rather than a political decision - taken at an operational level - and communicated from the US military to its British counterparts.

The UK's Ministry of Defence has not commented.

Days after the incident, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but did not provide further details. Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

Initially, five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF). All five were UK nationals from London.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".

The sixth man, aged 25, was arrested in London on Thursday on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts. Counter terror police confirmed on Saturday he had also been released on bail.

RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.

In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

Days after the incident, and before the arrest of the sixth man, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Fox News that it "clearly involve[d] the hands of a foreign actor".

Rubio did not provide further details - saying at the time he was limited on what he could say on air.

US President Donald Trump separately said he was "surprised" the five men had been released on bail.

"We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.

News.title: Green Party members back 'Zionism is racism' motion
News.content:
Green Party members have adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism, in a move that has divided senior figures at the top of the party.

The party's joint deputy leaders have been at odds over the subject, with Mothin Ali backing the move, and Rachel Millward describing the wording as "problematic".

Activists endorsed the policy motion, which was put forward by a group of members at the party's conference in Brighton, by 1022 votes to 813.

Discussion about the vote has dominated the conference, and exposed divisions between the party's newly enlarged membership base under leader Zack Polanski and its MPs elected at the last election.

The motion adopted by Green members defines Zionism as an ideology in support of "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" and backs a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine".

"The real, material, manifestation of Zionism has been the historic and ongoing dehumanisation, displacement, dispossession, disenfranchisement and destruction of Palestinians," it says.

It has attracted criticism from some Jewish groups, including the Board of Deputies and the Jewish Leadership Council who wrote a letter to the party ahead of the vote.

In a statement on Sunday evening, the organisations called the motion an "attack on the Jewish community".

"Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it," it said.

"Branding most British Jews and Jewish institutions 'racist' stokes anti-Jewish hatred after a year in which British Jews have been murdered attending their synagogue, stabbed in the streets, and seen their community buildings firebombed."

Israel's Foreign Ministry said the motion went beyond "the boundaries of legitimate political debate" and was "a stain on the history of the United Kingdom".

Later on Sunday, it said Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar had banned Polanski from entering Israel in response.

Debate about the motion, as well as the conflict in Gaza, has featured heavily during the conference, which is taking place after a surge in its membership in the wake of Polanski's election as leader in September last year.

Speaking after the vote, Lubna Speitan, the Green member behind the motion, argued its backers wanted to voice opposition to "racist systems of oppression".

"We stand united against all forms of racism and discrimination - no exemptions," she added.

Polanski himself did not vote in the debate, having left the conference early to campaign in Holborn and St Pancras, where he is standing to be the MP. A full list of candidates in the contest can be found here.

News.title: I'm a classic old school Conservative, says Kemi Badenoch
News.content:
Kemi Badenoch has declared herself a "classic old school Conservative" as she begins her party's annual conference with a string of policy pledges and a 100 page statement on her guiding principles., external

"I believe in common sense, people working hard and being rewarded for that effort," she told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg.

She added that welfare should be a "safety net, not a lifestyle".

The Tory leader is trying to ensure her party stands out in a crowded political field. The Conservatives are trailing Labour and Reform UK in the opinion polls and have yet to recover from their historic defeat at the 2024 general election.

Badenoch, whose personal poll ratings are higher than that of her party, has characterised Reform leader Nigel Farage as a "grumpy grandpa" and she told Laura Kuenssberg that Labour leader Andy Burnham is "the cheesy uncle who does all the dad jokes".

She described herself as a "no-nonsense mum".

Asked if her plan for benefit cuts and a massive increase in prison places was a return to the "nasty party" of the past, she said: "It's the common sense party. That's what we're doing.

"And, quite frankly, if we were doing so well the old way, then why did we have such a terrible issue in 2024?"

In her essay The Right Way - a deliberate echo of an essay written by Margaret Thatcher in 1976, external entitled The Right Approach - Badenoch says the last Conservative government failed because it did not know what it stood for.

Despite the party's rhetoric during its 14 years in power, she said: "We did little to reverse the structural changes Labour had made which took the country in the wrong direction.

"The result was that the state grew by stealth."

The essay says the "next Conservative government will have one central principle: business, not government, creates growth".

The Tories would achieve growth through tax cuts, cutting red tape and reducing the size of the civil service back to pre-pandemic levels, the essay says.

And it adds: "What is really missing from politics and government today is people prepared to say no.

"Political parties now need to recruit those who have the stomach to say no to good causes when the resources simply are not there to do everything."

News.title: British Museum announces changes to ease Bayeux Tapestry queues
News.content:
The British Museum has announced changes to how visitors see the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition after concerns over long queues and overcrowding.

The measures include plans for longer opening hours, as well as an audio guide, additional seating and clearer signage.

A museum spokesperson said the public response to the 11th Century embroidery had been "extraordinary", but acknowledged that some visitors had waited longer than they would have wanted.

Some people reported waits of up to two hours, while hundreds of ticket holders were reportedly turned away due to backlogs when the museum closed early last week due to a private event.

Some ticket holders took to social media to complain about the disruption.

One disappointed visitor said the trip had been a "big event" they had looked forward to, while another wrote she had been waiting since she was seven to see the Bayeux Tapestry, and bought tickets only to be turned away after queuing.

The museum later apologised to those who had been unable to enter and said they would be issued refunds and priority booking slots for a rearranged time.

From Monday, visitors will be offered an audio guide with more information about the embroidery, while additional signage and seating will be provided for those queuing to reach the main exhibition.

The museum said it planned to introduce longer opening hours to prevent queues building during the day and allow people with later bookings more time to view the exhibition.

Details of the extended hours have not yet been disclosed.

News.title: Protesters gather as migrants brought ashore on south coast
News.content:
Protesters have gathered in a south coast town as more than 100 people believed to be migrants were brought ashore after crossing the Channel in a small boat.

A number of people were seen arriving at a marina in Gosport, Hampshire, having been transported aboard two RNLI boats late on Sunday. Their dinghy appeared to have set off from near Utah Beach in Normandy during the morning, according to ship tracking data.

French media reported there were about 120 migrants on board.

Hampshire Police said it deployed officers to "support our partners in the event of an emergency at sea". The force imposed conditions under the Public Order Act as well as powers prohibiting the wearing of face coverings.

News.title: Shadow chancellor to unveil Tory plans to cut taxes and regulations
News.content:
Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith is to outline his plans for the UK economy, including hopes to cut taxes, red tape and house-building costs.

Griffith and his colleagues will use day two of the party's conference in Birmingham to also explain how they would want to reduce food costs, support Heathrow Airport expansion and abolish Natural England and the Environment Agency.

Another prospective policy is replacing agreements designed to compel developers to fund community projects and services in areas they want to build.

Griffith will describe his approach as the "most ambitious deregulation project in a generation". Reform UK suggested the Tories were "copying our policies".

Griffith's speech comes after Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch published a 100-page document, external explaining her guiding principles and how her party would act should it return to government by winning the next general election.

Following their historic defeat in the 2024 general election, the Conservatives have been trying to rebuild and convince voters that they can be trusted again.

The Tories have faced repeated attacks from their opponents for their record in government, including on the economy, between 2010 and 2024.

Griffith is expected to say: "No-one else is coming to save our economy. Only we can inject reality, tell the hard truths and make this a country we are proud to hand on to the next generation."

He will accuse Prime Minister Andy Burnham of wanting to pursue a "socialist fever dream of the 1970s", adding the Tories want to deliver "cheaper homes, lower taxes, and less red tape".

Chancellor John Healey last week said all promises the government made would be "built on the rock of fiscal discipline" and the Budget on 28 October would "give families and businesses a bit of breathing space".

During a series of speeches on Monday, Conservative shadow ministers will continue to make their case and provide more details of their proposals.

This will include ditching environmental and energy efficiency regulations, including the future homes standard.

The Tories believe their changes could cut the cost of delivering a new home by up to Â£50,000, which in turn they expect could save money for buyers.

A single levy for developers would be implemented in place of section 106 agreements and the Community Infrastructure Levy, which fund projects in the community when building plans are progressed.

The Conservatives argue this new charge would remove delays and improve how the funds are spent to the benefit of residents.

The party has been critical of the roles of Natural England and the Environment Agency in relation to house building and flood prevention work respectively, and wants to abolish both. Their functions would be looked after by the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra).

The Extended Packaging Responsibility (EPR) scheme, which requires firms to cover the cost of collecting, recycling and disposing of packaging it produces, would also be scrapped by the Conservatives.

The party believes this would help lift a "burden" from businesses and in turn could cut the cost of the weekly shop.

On Heathrow, Griffith is expected to say the next Conservative government would do "whatever it takes to end the delays and boost capacity by backing the third runway".

Plans for expansion were scrapped by the Tory-led coalition government in 2010.

Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves championed the runway to boost the economy after Labour won power, although Burnham has refused to say whether he backs the project since becoming prime minister.

Burnham has described it as "principally... a matter for London and Londoners".

Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper said the Conservatives have "cemented their position as a pointless anti-growth anti-business party" by rejecting closer ties with Europe.

She added: "No-one can take anything the Conservatives say on the economy seriously given their litany of fantasy-land financial pledges."

Reform UK economy spokesman Robert Jenrick accused the Conservatives of "once again copying our policies".

He added the Tories were unable to match Reform's pledge to raise the tax-free personal allowance to Â£15,000.

News.title: France to close up to 500 schools on Monday over student protests
News.content:
Up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday after clashes between riot police and student protesters in recent days, the French education minister said on Sunday.

Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400 to 500" high schools as security conditions "have not been fulfilled", Ãdouard Geffray said.

He also said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protests.

Thousands of students have been demonstrating over education standards and the protests, which started last week, have spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille.

High school pupils and others have objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

On Friday, French Justice Minister GÃ©rald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools had been affected "one way or another" by violent protests.

The education minister warned the number of schools potentially affected on Monday could be comparable to Friday's figure but promised a "partial, progressive return to lessons".

"There are activists - particularly from the far-left - who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Ãdouard Geffray claimed.

"Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he said. Geffray added that 78 staff members in education had been wounded, which he described as "something we have never seen before".

On Friday 1,747 people were arrested, according to French Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez.

News.title: Girl, 12, fatally shot in US during 'dispute over parking space'
News.content:
A 12-year-old girl was killed in Baltimore over the weekend during an apparent disagreement over a parking space, police in the US city said.

The girl was caught in the crossfire of bullets between two men who police said were allegedly fighting over a parking space in a park where children were playing American football.

In addition to the young girl, a woman was also found with gunshot wounds when police arrived on the scene. Two men also visited area hospitals for injuries believed to be related to the shooting, police said.

Police are now searching for at least two suspects, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said at a news conference. No arrests have been made.

"What we know is there was some type of argument between two cowards," Worley said. "They both opened fire on each other. In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl, who was probably down there watching football, was shot and killed."

Worley said the girl, who police have not named, was not a target of the shooting.

The girl was pronounced dead in hospital. The other three individuals who were injured have non-life-threatening injuries, Worley said.

The incident happened after 18:00 EDT (23:00 BST) on Saturday.

Authorities are still investigating the shooting and have asked any witnesses to bring information to police.

It remains unclear how many shots were fired, Worley said.

"Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone," Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said at the news conference.

"We never should have to say something like that. What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen in my life."

News.title: Rugby league fans in Wakefield for bus parade
News.content:
Thousands of rugby league fans turned out to watch an open-top bus parade, after Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions.

Trinity beat Warrington Wolves 23-10 in Saturday's Grand Final at Old Trafford - their first title win since 1968, long before Super League was established.

To celebrate the victory, two buses, carrying players and staff, travelled from the club's ground at Belle Vue to Wakefield Town Hall for a civic reception.

Fullback Max Jowitt, who has made 188 appearances for Trinity and scored three goals in the final, said the parade had been an "unbelievable" experience.

"The fans have been unbelievable, the city is unbelievable and the trophy's unbelievable," he said.

News.title: Kneecap visit Garvaghy Road to show support for residents
News.content:
In a statement issued to the Press Association after their visit, Kneecap said they support the residents of Garvaghy Road, and described them as a "determined and strong community".

The group did not perform during their visit.

BreandÃ¡n Mac Cionnaith, from the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition, told BBC News NI that was a "very deliberate decision".

"Kneecap isn't everyone's cup of tea but they wanted to come down, show a bit of solidarity to the kids in the area. They visited the the gaelscoil and bunscoil (Irish language schools), the youth club and community centre. That was their primary focus," Mac Cionnaith said.

On the expected court hearing on Monday, Mac Cionnaith said he "didn't want to pre-judge any outcomes".

Media reports on Sunday, external suggested that the Orange Order has offered to walk away and never return if they secure one last march along the Garvaghy Road.

Speaking on this, Mac Cionnaith said: "There was an agreement beforehand by the Orange Order that they would have their final march on the Garvaghy Road. They had their final march on the Garvaghy Road, and they threw it back in our community's face and said they would be down the road the following year.

"That's the fact. That's the reality."

He added: "Could we trust that organisation again, or trust any of their representatives?

News.title: Triathlete was 'very sick' in hospital after swimming in 'dirty' open water
News.content:
A triathlete who travels the world to take part in races says making his dreams come true comes with serious risk after one event led to him being "very sick" in hospital.

Andrew Jones, from Carmarthen, takes part in various events, and has even earned a slot in the Ironman World Championship in Kona, Hawaii this month.

But the triathlete said swimming in "dirty" open-water made him very unwell ahead of the event after he contracted Campylobacter, external â an infection caused by bacteria.

Triathlon Cymru said its Safer Blue Spaces project, which is the first of its kind, was now using small sampling devices on triathletes to test the water and provide reliable data on water quality in Wales.

Jones said contracting Campylobacter from polluted water was "pretty nasty".

"It made me very sick unfortunately. In the house on a Sunday evening, I felt really unwell," he said.

"My temperature went up, my heart rate went up, I was shaking uncontrollably and unfortunately went straight to A&E."

News.title: Nine fire engines called to Glasgow city centre bar fire
News.content:
More than 40 firefighters have been called out after reports of fire at a bar in central Glasgow.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said it was alerted just after 14:40 and nine appliances were in attendance on Sunday evening.

Images from the scene showed parts of Renfield Street and West Regent Street were cordoned off, with a number of fire crews gathered outside both the Bistro and Maltman bars.

There were no reports of casualties. People have been advised to avoid the area.

News.title: Glastonbury 2027 tickets sell out in 42 minutes
News.content:
Tickets for Glastonbury Festival 2027 sold out in 42 minutes, organisers have said.

Thousands of people joined the online queue at 09:00 BST in the hope of securing tickets to the festival at Worthy Farm in Somerset, which returns from 23 to 27 June after a fallow year.

Organisers confirmed last month that tickets for the weekend were at their highest price ever - Â£408, including a Â£5 booking fee per ticket - an increase of Â£29.50 from the last event in 2025.

Headliners have yet to be announced but organiser Emily Eavis previously said the team was "very excited" and things were "coming together really well".

Glastonbury posted on Instagram shortly after 09:40 to announce that tickets had sold out, and notified those who were in the queue.

"Thank you to everyone who bought one and we're sorry to those of you who missed out on a morning where demand greatly exceeded supply," the post said.

"There will be a resale of any cancelled or returned tickets in Spring 2027."

News.title: Bellamy bemoans new schedule after Denmark loss
News.content:
