Sorba Thomas threatened on the left flank, intermittently destroying the Denmark right-back Rasmus Kristensen and Liam Cullen, now of Leicester, was industrious as a playmaker. But Wales failed to test Mads Hermansen, a former Leicester clubmate of Ward’s. It was almost as if this was the fourth game in a marathon camp. “Physically, it makes no sense,” Bellamy said. “We know it’s a complete disadvantage to us … I think, really, it is designed for the elite.”

Sports.title: Hallgrímsson calls on Uefa to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after bad-tempered draw
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland’s manager Heimir Hallgrímsson has called on Uefa to keep his side away from Israel in future draws after a pair of fixtures he admitted “has been tough on us all”. Ireland were pegged back to a draw in another tetchy encounter, this time played without fans at TSC Arena in Backa Topola, Serbia.

Hallgrímsson did not want to comment on a half-time confrontation, after which it is understood a member of his backroom staff alleged he was spat at by an Israeli player – something the Icelandic manager said was better left to a disciplinary committee.

“We need now some time to reflect and go forward,” he said. “It’s also the best time to find your enemies when you’re lying on the ground and people are kicking you. It’s easy to see who was trying to kick you.”

Asked on RTE whether the two sides should be playing in the future, he said: “No, they shouldn’t. That’s not ours to decide, that’s Uefa. I wouldn’t want or wish any national team to go through what we have gone through these two weeks. Uefa needs to step in and do something.’

Troy Parrott’s first-half ­penalty was cancelled out after the break in the Group B3 game. Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his past seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two ­minutes after the restart.

Ireland players again wore black armbands and bowed their heads ­during the Israeli national anthem before the teams’ second Nations League meeting on Sunday. The Israeli players also wore black armbands in memory of the people killed in the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023.

Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher stepped in as captain for Dara O’Shea – who was excused to be with his wife for the birth of their child – and he pointedly avoided shaking hands with the Israel captain Peretz, despite completing the usual pre-match formality with the referee and one of his assistants.

Kelleher repeated O’Shea’s actions before the first match in Debrecen, Hungary last week, when O’Shea declined to shake the Israel captain Manor Solomon’s hand. Ireland went on to win that game 3-0 through three first-half goals. Solomon was dropped to the bench for Sunday’s match. The Israel forward Sayed Abu Farchi was back in the squad after serving a suspension for getting sent off following his goal celebration during Israel’s 3-1 defeat to Austria last month.

Finn Azaz, whose mother has Israeli heritage, was among the Irish substitutes after playing from the start against Austria on Thursday.

View image in fullscreen The Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher avoids shaking hands with the Israel captain Dor Peretz before the game. Photograph: Andrej Čukić/EPA

Ireland had started to find some fluidity when Dunne won a penalty. The Israel goalkeeper Assaf Tzur scrambled to smother the ball, and Jimmy Dunne was brought down under the challenge, with the spot-kick confirmed after a lengthy VAR check.

Peretz levelled the scoring two minutes after the restart. An Oscar Gloukh effort took a favourable deflection off Liam Scales and into the path of the acting captain, who gave ­Kelleher no chance with a low finish.

YesterSunday’s game was initially supposed to be played in Dublin, but the Football Association of Ireland moved the game to a neutral venue for “operational reasons” in June following widespread calls for a boycott in protest of Israel’s actions in Gaza. The FAI said the game would be played with no fans present.

It followed the FAI’s own motion the previous November calling on Uefa to ban Israel from club and international competitions.

The difficult atmosphere between the sides spilled over during a clash as the sides entered the tunnel at half-time. Officials then broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

Sports.title: Nations League roundup: Haaland limps off in Norway’s loss to Portugal
Sports.content:
Title-holders Portugal maintained their 100% record in the Nations League with a 2-1 home win over Norway on Sunday to seal a place in ⁠the March quarter-finals, while Manchester City’s problems may have got worse after Erling Haaland limped off for the visitors.

Portugal hope their victory at the Estádio Do Dragão shifts the focus further away from Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt exit from the squad last week. Gonçalo Ramos netted 11 minutes from time to ensure they secured a top-two ⁠finish in Group A4 as ⁠they moved six points ​ahead of second-placed Denmark, who won 1-0 at Wales.

The home side in Porto were still under a cloud from Ronaldo’s dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, although they were triumphant without him in Denmark ⁠last Thursday after he walked out on the squad, and continued their winning ways on Sunday.

Norway took the lead in ​the 36th minute from centre-back Kristoffer Ajer, who hit a ‌dipping half-volley from the edge of ‌the box. But if that effort was sumptuous, João Cancelo’s thrashing effort to equalise two minutes later was even more awe-inspiring.

Ramos’s ‌winner came off his calf after João Félix had headed across goal for him to score.

Portugal’s win was soured by a red card for Francisco Conceição four minutes from time. He gave the referee a cynical thumbs up after receiving a yellow card and was immediately shown a second.

Afterwards, Jesus said Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes: “If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team … we can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who’s going to decide.”

View image in fullscreen Gonçalo Ramos knocks down the corner flag in delight after scoring. Photograph: SPP/Shutterstock

The Netherlands took over at the top of Group A2, after beating Serbia 2-1 in Eindhoven, but only on goal difference from ⁠Greece, who held on grimly for a goalless draw at home to Germany in Thessaloniki.

With their captain Virgil van Dijk celebrating a 100th cap, the Netherlands went ahead against Serbia when Teun Koopmeiners’s 31st-minute free-kick evaded all in the penalty area and ​crept into the corner. However, the visitors were level within four minutes as Aleksa Terzic crossed for teenager Mihajlo Cvetkovic to rise over Koopmeiners and head in his first international goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It took until the 72nd minute to go back ahead when Denzel Dumfries’s low cross was turned back across the goal by Tijjani Reijnders, sliding in at the far post, and tapped in by Joshua Zirkzee, who ⁠received a late call-up to the Dutch squad last week.

Germany dominated away against Greece, but Jürgen ​Klopp’s inexperienced side could not find the net, ​and they have won only one of ​their first four games under the new coach.

Austria needed a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Kosovo ​but still have a three-point ‌lead at the top ​of Group B3 after the ​Republic of Ireland and Israel drew 1-1 behind closed doors in the Serbian town of Backa Topola.

In Group D2, Abdulakh Khaybulayev’s first-half goal was enough to send Azerbaijan top of the standings with a 1-0 win over previously unbeaten Lithuania, while veteran Teddy Teuma came on as a second-half substitute to hand Malta a 1-0 home win over Andorra in Group D1.

Sports.title: Shaw seals thrilling win over Arsenal to extend Manchester City’s 100% WSL start
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s under-pressure head coach Renée Slegers still believes they will turn their form around, despite falling 10 points behind Manchester City with Sunday’s defeat in an absorbing six-goal thriller against the defending champions.

Arsenal were last season’s runners-up in the Women’s Super League and had high hopes of mounting a strong challenge this term but their chances of lifting a first WSL title since 2019 now appear to be hanging by a thread after five rounds of fixtures, while City maintained their 100% start by coming from behind twice to beat Slegers’ struggling side.

The 37-year-old Dutchwoman, who in January signed a new contract until the summer of 2029, said on Friday that she felt the full support of the club. Asked, after this pivotal 4-2 defeat, whether she would be the one in charge after this month’s international break, she replied: “All I know so far is that the last couple of days we’ve been together as a club, as a team, with support, aligning on the direction. Of course, this result is disappointing, but I’m here, I’m full of energy and I care a lot for the club.”

Slegers added she feels the international break will come at a good time to change environments and that there will be a “big review of our season so far” during the break. She continued: “We see solutions and we see the closeness. It’s not that we’re totally off it. It’s been consistently about margins – when we get them on our side, I think we’re going to be really good.”

The match was the first to be played at the Etihad Stadium since the Premier League published the guilty verdict against Manchester City and there was something of a subdued atmosphere outside the stadium in the buildup to kick-off. That quickly changed once the game started, and was wholly different in the second half as the hosts began to take control and their supporters were thoroughly enjoying themselves.

City had frequently insisted their women’s team were treating this as “business as usual” before their draw with Real Madrid on Thursday. There were very few references to the ongoing saga here on Sunday, aside from some Arsenal fans chanting “same old City, always cheating” during the first half, and one City fan – sitting just in front of the media seats – who defiantly shouted about which part of the anatomy people could “stick your 115 charges”, but nobody else joined in. Matters on the pitch were more interesting.

City will have felt aggrieved about the nature of Arsenal’s opener, as replays showed that Lisa Baum appeared to be offside when Lotte Wubben-Moy headed goalwards. Baum was the quickest to get to the rebound after Ayaka Yamashita’s save and poked home. The visitors could not hold on until the break, however, as Lauren Hemp’s deflected strike found its way into the far corner.

Arsenal went back in front shortly after half-time when Yui Hasegawa lost the ball inside her own area and Alessia Russo pounced, curling a terrific finish into the far corner. It was her first league goal of the campaign. Arsenal appeared to be in control until a triple substitution from Andrée Jeglertz, including the introduction of Kerstin Casparij, changed things.

View image in fullscreen Alessia Russo pounces to make it 2-1 to Arsenal at Manchester City. Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/Reuters

The 26-year-old, playing as an inverted full-back, latched on to a loose ball and curled in a delightful strike to equalise and soon afterwards Hemp tucked a tidy finish through Anneke Borbe’s legs to make it 3-2. Suddenly Arsenal’s body language changed and City were on top. They added a clinical fourth when Shaw latched on to Aoba Fujino’s excellent through-ball and her low finish was superb.

Jeglertz was full of praise for Casparij and his centre-back pairing of Jade Rose and Alex Greenwood. Asked about Arsenal’s woes, he said he still expects them to have a strong campaign, saying: “They have great football players - I’m pretty sure that when we are coming into spring that they will definitely be one of the teams battling.”

Arsenal’s problems were exacerbated by their midfielder Mariona Caldentey going off with a suspected hamstring injury. The Arsenal defender Wubben-Moy said there was unity as she told Sky Sports the players “fought for ourselves, for Renée and for the fans - but ultimately the result didn’t do that justice”, adding: “This is an unprecedented position for Arsenal to be in. It’s up to us to get ourselves out of it.”

Her words may offer some solace to Slegers. So will the sight of the 2,000 travelling fans applauding her after the game. The upcoming “review” will determine whether or not that was a farewell.

Sports.title: Clàudia Pina hits four as Barcelona score seven goals to demolish Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Clàudia Pina smashed in four goals as Barcelona demolished Real Madrid 7-0 to earn a five point lead at the top of Liga F on Sunday over their rivals.

The 25-year-old Spain international was in lethal form in front of goal as a dominant Barça won the Clásico battle with ease at the Camp Nou in front of over 40,000 fans, continuing their perfect start to the campaign. The match was pushed back by two hours after torrential rain in the Catalonia region over the weekend.

Pina put Barcelona, who have won the league seven seasons running, in the driving seat after just four minutes with a neat finish after breezing into the area.

The Catalan side controlled the ball and Madrid found it hard to pry it away from them, although managed to fend them off until Pina’s second in the 28th minute, the first of three goals in around five minutes.

Ewa Pajor’s shot was blocked and Pina polished off the rebound, completing her hat-trick a few minutes later by blasting into the top corner.

European champions Barça immediately struck again through Caroline Graham Hansen, who skipped past a defender before slotting home.

Pina scored her fourth with a blast inside the near post before the interval as Barca yet again pulled apart Madrid’s defence. The fifth came early in the second half for Pere Romeu’s side, through Polish striker Pajor.

Three-time Ballon d’Or winner Aitana Bonmatí came on for the final 30 minutes as she continues her return to full fitness following a broken leg.

Swiss midfielder Sydney Schertenleib scored a stunning seventh from long range to round off Barça’s rout late on.

Real Madrid have beaten Barca just once in 25 meetings between the sides across all competitions. Madrid’s women’s team began in 2020 after taking over CD Tacon.

Sports.title: Jesse Marsch: ‘We Americans have been inundated with propaganda since we were young’
Sports.content:
Peak leaf hasn’t yet arrived in Montreal but the bursts of gold and butterscotch up on the hill that gave this place its name still mushroom out by the hour.

Sitting in a glass-panelled hotel mezzanine at the foot of Mount Royal, Canada men’s coach Jesse Marsch has his mind on another harvest. When this extended autumnal international window ends, he will decamp to Italy, where the olive crops at his Tuscan villa are ready for reaping.

Flight paths between Canada and Europe have been busy lately, and figurative transatlantic distances are closing fast. As Canada’s relations with the noisiest neighbour to the south stretch and fray, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney is forging alliances with the EU so close that the bloc is apparently inventing new membership categories.

As an American residing in Europe who is also a Canadian leader with robust approval ratings, Marsch is watching. To him, it feels right.

“I’ve always thought Canada was a little bit more European than the US anyway. Right?” Marsch tells the Guardian. “But certainly now there’s enough happening politically and economically that you would say, we’re looking much more like that. There’s talk of [Canada becoming an associate EU member] even actually happening. I like that aspect.

“There’s a uniqueness to Canada in terms of how truly multiethnic this country has become. You can see that Canada is not just a North American country any more, you know? That bodes well for our sport and for the makeup of our team, the makeup of our fans.”

Having led Canada’s men to historic highs at this summer’s World Cup, Marsch is feeling his way into his second act in the job. Some of his sideline displays – we’ll get to that meme – may have irked outsiders, especially in his homeland, during the tournament. Yet, having extended for four more years, Marsch is someone an overwhelming majority of Canadians are happy to have at the helm. There are more than a few cross-points between Marsch and Carney.

“My impression is that first of all, he is a really smart guy, but a really normal guy,” Marsch says of Carney, who attended a number of Canada’s World Cup matches. “Sometimes you meet a US president, and you’re overwhelmed, maybe by their presence, the position itself. I’ve met Clinton, George Bush Sr, Obama, Trump, Biden. Oh, and Carter. Six in person. Carney, compared to all of them, the closest would be Obama. A real air of intelligence, but a real air of being a regular guy. I think that that’s perfect for this country and this moment.

“He has shown great support for us. I made a joke with him that ‘I heard you’re an Everton fan?’ and he goes, ‘Yeah’. And I go, ‘I’m sorry about that’. He replies: ‘Why does everybody say that? Everybody has to pick their team and stick by them.’ I said, ‘I appreciate that you don’t switch from Everton to Arsenal or Liverpool, like everybody else’. There’s something so genuine [about] that. Could a president of the US ever be an Everton fan? No chance.”

View image in fullscreen Canada prime minister Mark Carney greeted Marsch’s team in the locker room after the team’s win over Qatar at the 2026 World Cup. Photograph: Jared C Tilton/Fifa/Getty Images

Circumstances, as well as natural impulses, have led Marsch to play statesman during this prolonged cooling of relations between Canada and his home country. He’s been defiant – lashing out at Donald Trump’s “51st state” barbs – then more deft. Sometimes, especially when it comes to the US Soccer Federation he said led him on with a job offer only to renege, he finds it hard to hide his disdain.

This window is the start of turning the page to the next phase of his Canada project. He admits, with a chuckle, that the four years stretching ahead feel long but there are imminent goals – a first trophy in 25 years, cracking and consolidating inside the world’s top 24.

A win over Chile in Toronto and 2-0 win over Peru here on Saturday afternoon in games billed as The Homecoming made for a solid start. New caps have been handed out. Key players arrived thriving in new surroundings, none more than Jonathan David at Atlético Madrid. Extended injury absences and the awkward non-attendance of captain Alphonso Davies (skipping the window to honeymoon) have been overcome.

But Tuesday’s clash with the US in Saint Paul means more American questions are coming. Looking back, the Folarin Balogun affair feels absolutely tailor-made for a Marschian verdict. He, of course, has thoughts.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Well, this is a deep conversation,” he says, leaning back. “We, as Americans, have been inundated with propaganda since we were young. We’re the No 1 country in the world, we deserve everything, we dominate everything, No 1 in every aspect of life. This is what we’ve been told. So, when things happen and we don’t feel like we’re in control of it … we feel like we deserve to be treated differently because we’re Americans. That is one of the things that infuriates the rest of the world about Americans. And Americans don’t know that if they don’t ever leave the country.

“So what I feel when the Balogun ruling happens is that would never happen in any other country in the world, and this is why everyone around the world hates America. That was proven to be so. The US had had a good World Cup, was doing well. All that switched in one moment. But do I think that that’s about corruption and unfairness? The problem is, football is inundated with this kind of stuff.”

The meme is another World Cup leftover. “I’ve had all kinds of people ask me what it was, was it a meat slicer?” he says of his sideline gyrations during their match against Qatar. The incident spawned a gif which has been used plenty in the Marsch family WhatsApp since. “I don’t know what I’m doing sometimes. As soon as I’ve done it, I’m like: ‘Why did I do that? I’m such an idiot’.”

He doesn’t feel fooled, however, by the sport’s latest, arguably greatest, modern corruption crisis. Defeats to Manchester City in 2022-23 didn’t help the Leeds United side Marsch had managed when they missed safety by five points. That campaign is not one of the “sham” seasons which were part of the damning verdict against City last week. But he’s adamant the unfairness extended to his time in England.

“I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew,” says Marsch, who also pointed to Everton and Nottingham Forest later being deducted points for issues in the same season when Leeds were relegated below both.

“That summer [2022], us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money. For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips [to City]. We had a lot left over from what we bought. At the time, we weren’t in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn’t have deep pockets. Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, ‘Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?’

“When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it’s like: ‘Yeah, OK, sure!’ So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, ‘This is football’.”

Sports.title: Alexander’s absence weighs heavy as Bradford try to keep promotion push on track
Sports.content:
It was a bruising start to the week for Bradford City when news filtered through to the players that Graham Alexander had stepped down as manager. They were top of League One and his departure was a sudden and unexpected blow for a side that had started to let imaginations run wild about a return to the second tier for the first time in 23 years.

The coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle took interim charge and called a meeting with the squad last Monday. “Some of the players were a little unsettled, didn’t know what was going on or who was taking the team,” Trueman said. “But the players have just got on with business and that’s the key. It shows the mentality of the team. This could quite easily derail them, but they’ve continued to do the right things.”

If any caretaker can keep Bradford on track, it is Trueman, who has now stepped in temporarily five times since joining the club as an Under-18 coach six years ago. This time, though, is different. Previously, his job was to raise the team during low periods. Now the task is to maintain the upward trajectory that began the moment Alexander arrived in 2023.

Bradford were stuck in the bottom tier of the EFL and sitting in 16th when Alexander took over. They finished ninth in his first season, then third in his second to earn automatic promotion, followed by a stunning fourth-place finish back in League One, losing in the playoff semi-finals last May.

It has been a thrilling ride rarely enjoyed by Bradford fans. They twice reached the EFL Trophy semi-finals in successive seasons. At one stage, they won 10 consecutive home games, breaking a club record set in 1953.Last year they had the best home record of any side in Europe’s top five leagues. Alexander won 79 times in 158 games – the best win rate of any Bradford manager in charge for at least 65 games.

The chief executive, Ryan Sparks, said Alexander and the assistant manager Chris Lucketti, who has followed him to Preston, delivered “some of the most incredible moments in our recent history”.

They looked set to deliver more, with Bradford top of League One when the Preston opportunity came out of the blue. Alexander told the club he had ambitions to manage in the Championship, but you wonder if he might have achieved that with Bradford had he stayed. Perhaps he believed that two promotions in two years would risk them becoming relegation fodder in the Championship, whereas Preston presents a more stable platform. Ultimately, the lure of a club that he once captained – playing 400 games during an eight-year spell from 1999 to 2007 – d in the city where his children were raised proved too strong.

View image in fullscreen Graham Alexander’s sudden departure has left Bradford to rebuild early on in the season. Photograph: Paul Thompson/ProSports/Shutterstock

On forums and social media, fans shared a mixture of sadness, anger and anxiety. Most believe Alexander has left the club stronger, but frustration is shared among a sizeable minority about the timing – less than two months into a season after a summer spent recruiting specifically for his aggressive, direct, high-pressing football. After Jake Beesley headed Bradford into a fourth-minute lead at Reading on Saturday, the 1,118 supporters who made the 400-mile round trip sang about being top of the league, but did not chant for their departed manager once.

Rapid developments in the space of a few weeks leave a huge hole. Bradford now find themselves in unfamiliar territory: it is the first time in 43 years they have lost a manager mid-season, and fans are nervous about the executives’ aptitude for finding a suitable replacement, given the shaky record before landing Alexander.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In the opposition dugout at Reading’s Select Car Leasing Stadium stood one of the favourites to take over. Before the match, Leam Richardson faced questions about whether he was interested. His response – that he would be in the Reading dugout for the match – neatly sidestepped the prospect that he might not be beyond this weekend, though he insisted he had not been contacted. Meanwhile Michael Duff, sacked by Wycombe last month, is also being heavily linked.

Nonetheless, Sparks and the head of football, David Sharpe, would have been watching closely from the directors’ box to see whether Reading showed signs of a style of football that would fit the framework Alexander built. Plenty makes Richardson a logical candidate. He previously worked with Sharpe, who was chair at Wigan when Richardson was manager, and he has also coached Callum Connolly, in the Bradford starting XI, and Nick Powell, who came on from the bench.

Others are in the frame, including the Plymouth manager Tom Cleverley, the former Manchester United midfielder – a Premier League winner in 2013 – who at 37 has quietly built his managerial reputation these past two years. Udoka Godwin-Malife’s second-half equaliser meant Plymouth moved above Bradford on goal difference. The next appointment is crucial. Getting Alexander so right makes getting it wrong so much more costly.

Sports.title: Match of the Day! Hosts Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates 'are dating' after his ex confronted him over suspicions
Sports.content:
Match Of The Day presenters Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates have reportedly scored off set as the duo are said to be dating.

The Sun claims that the pair are romantically involved after Chapman, 52, was accused by his ex-girlfriend Clere Collier of dating Cates while they were still together.

Chapman reportedly split suddenly with Collier, a Dubai-based mother-of-two and estate agent, in April after three years together. He insists there was no overlap between the relationships and that he had remained faithful.

A source told The Sun: 'Mark split with Clere out of the blue, without much explanation.

'They had been making plans for the future and their relationship had been going strong.

'They stayed in touch after the split, but Clere soon realised that Mark and Kelly were close and she accused Mark of dating Kelly.

Match Of The Day presenters Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates are reportedly dating

The duo became the main presenters of Match Of The Day last season alongside Gabby Logan

'Mark admitted the relationship, but insisted there was no overlap between the two women and that he hadn’t cheated on her.

'He told her that he had been a single man when he started spending time with Kelly. Of course, it left a bad taste in Clere’s mouth, and she didn’t believe him.'

Chapman and Cates became the main co-presenters for Match Of The Day alongside Gabby Logan last season after Gary Lineker left.

While their shifts presenting the show do not overlap, Chapman and Cates did appear on Celebrity Gogglebox on the same sofa together in July.

Chapman, a highly respected broadcaster paid between £335,000 and £340,000 per year by the BBC, was already heavily involved with the show as Match Of The Day 2 presenter before his promotion.

He was married to his wife Sara for 19 years until she died aged 44 in 2020 after a battle with cancer. They had three kids together.

The Greater Manchester-born TV star is believed to have started dating Collier in 2023, with her making regular trips to the United Kingdom from the United Arab Emirates.

Meanwhile, Cates is the daughter of Scotland and Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish.

She was previously married to her TV producer husband Tom, with whom she has two children, but they split in 2021.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal lifeline: Boss Jorge Jesus and team-mates leave the door open for 41-year-old to return after he stormed out of camp amid rift with manager
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a lifeline by his Portugal manager and team-mates, who insist they would welcome his return despite his explosive walkout.

Ronaldo missed Portugal's 2-1 win over Norway in the Nations League on Sunday after abandoning their international camp due to a row with manager Jorge Jesus.

The iconic forward was fuming that he was left on the bench for the entire first game against Norway a week before. He then missed three training sessions and the Thursday game against Denmark, flying away on his private jet.

He still risks a six-month ban from Portugal duty for his conduct after he also pledged to tell 'the truth' about the scandal one day.

There have been reports that Portugal are in negotiations for a possible farewell match for Ronaldo, but these have been dismissed by Portuguese outlet Record. Ronaldo also appeared to not watch the game against Norway as he was on his private jet with his family in a picture shared by his wife Georgina Rodriguez.

But after their comeback victory against Norway, manager Jesus insisted Ronaldo could return in the next international break in November, saying: 'As far as I'm concerned, everything is open. It's up to Cris to decide his own life. In the next call-up, if Cris is playing and wants to be in the national team, why not?

Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal manager and team-mates insist he is welcome back

Ronaldo caused a storm by walking out on their international camp - and appeared to skip watching their match against Norway on Sunday

'Resentment? Nothing, it was a misunderstanding. In my opinion, it's easy to resolve. When will I resolve it? I don't know. The game is over, and only afterwards will we know how things will turn out.

'It's not up to me. To reach an agreement with two people, both people need to talk and agree. That's not up to me.

'Just because it was him, and perhaps rightly so because he's a symbol, this whole problem of him coming on, warming up, not coming on. How many players warmed up today and didn't come on? Will there be a problem? No.

'With Cris it's different, he's a symbol. But is it a problem? For me it wasn't a problem. If Cris wants to and is playing for Al-Nassr, he'll be in the next squad. We talked before this squad and we can talk before the next one. It's Cris who will decide.'

Portugal needed a 79th-minute winner from AC Milan star Goncalo Ramos to complete their comeback victory in a match which saw Erling Haaland limp off for the opponents.

Despite winning all three of their recent games without Ronaldo, and the shocking nature of his behaviour, his team-mates have said afresh that they want him back.

Full-back Nuno Mendes told Sport TV after the game: 'We're a united group, and Cristiano, as well as anyone else who isn't here, will always be welcomed with open arms.'

Joao Cancelo added: 'As Bruno (Fernandes) already said, Cristiano is our captain, he is the symbol of our national team, he is the best player Portugal has ever had and things will certainly end in the best way.'

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists he will have Ronaldo back if the forward wants to return

Georgina Rodriguez leapt the the defence of Ronaldo after his controversial walkout

Fernandes had led the way in trying to recover the situation, with the Manchester United midfielder revealing recently that he had held clear-the-air talks with Ronaldo.

He said: 'I had a conversation with Cris. What I told him is that the most important thing, regardless of what happens, is that he will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team and country, for everything he has done in Portugal and around the world.

'He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of the Portuguese people.

'We cannot divide ourselves; the national team is one, and all parties should resolve their issues behind closed doors. I think that's how it will be, and that everything will end well on both sides.

'We are out of the matter; we spend a lot of time playing cards and are outside the controversy surrounding this issue, but I ask that the country not be divided, not make choices, and accept all sides.

'Cris will always be the greatest icon of our national team, of world football, and deserves the respect of all Portuguese people, regardless of who likes him more or less.'

Ronaldo's fiery withdrawal - months after a World Cup in which it was perceived that he held back Portugal - has been one of the dominant stories of the international break.

He confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by manager Jesus in a press conference.

After leaving camp, Ronaldo said: 'I will tell the truth to all Portuguese people about the reasons that motivated my departure'

Bruno Fernandes (right) has held clear-the-air talks with Cristiano Ronaldo (left) after the latter stormed out of the Portugal camp

The feud started when Ronaldo was left on the bench for Portugal's win over Norway – the first time in 18 years he had missed the full 90 minutes for the national side barring injuries and suspensions.

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

The tension seems to have boiled over following Jesus' press conference. The manager said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

The coach, who also managed Ronaldo in Saudi Arabia, insists his conscience is clean.

Rodriguez and Ronaldo married in the summer after more than a decade together

'It's not difficult for me to focus,' he added. 'You know what's difficult for me? It's not understanding what's going on inside. It's not knowing how to train my players. That's what's difficult for me. The rest... zero.

'What's important is what we have to do. The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us.'

One iconic name to come out in support of Ronaldo is Zinedine Zidane, now the manager of France, who coached the forward at Real Madrid.

He said: 'We really must pay tribute to his great career. I was lucky to have him with me. He helped me win a lot of titles.

'Hats off to Cristiano! I always have a great deal of respect for those I've spent time with.'

Ronaldo's wife Georgina Rodriguez swiftly leapt to the defence of her husband by posting a fake Sir Alex Ferguson quote, which she deleted.

Georgina Rodriguez, 32, wrote of Portugal manager Jesus: 'I don't know how this man can carry the name of Christ,' and below her sniping comment was a fictitious quote from Ronaldo's former boss and legendary Man United manager Sir Alex Ferguson.

It read: 'If Jorge Jesus knew in his heart that he had no intention of using him, then why did he call him up in the first place? To make a point? That’s not authority, that’s insecurity.'

Ferguson has not spoken about the Ronaldo row and the quote and imagery appeared to be AI generated.

Rodriguez quickly deleted what she'd shared on her Instagram story with 78million followers.

She is part of a blended family, raising five children with Ronaldo, two of whom are biologically hers.

Sports.title: Ireland staff member claims Israel player 'SPAT' at him during half-time melee - as Israeli government make 'Nazi Germany' comparison after Irish players bow their heads during rivals' national anthem and refuse to shake hands
Sports.content:
A member of Ireland’s back-room staff alleged they were spat at by an Israel player during a half-time tunnel bust-up during their highly charged Nations League fixture in Serbia. Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle made the accusation following a confrontation as the teams left the field, according to the Irish Times. Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson declined to comment on the incident post-match, suggesting it was 'one for the [UEFA] disciplinary committee to look at'. 'There have been a lot of those incidents that could have escalated,' Hallgrimsson added to Irish broadcaster RTE following a 1-1 draw. 'We were clever enough to stop it before it went too far. I felt that was the intention to try to intimidate us and make us do something stupid, but a big credit to the players for how they handled their emotions.' The incident came with Ireland leading 1-0 at the break, with Troy Parrott having put Hallgrimsson's side ahead from the penalty spot in the 39th minute. A member of Ireland's staff reportedly alleged he had been spat at by an Israeli player during their Nations League match Ireland's players again bowed their heads at the Isreali national anthem played before kick off Ireland captain Caoimhin Kelleher and Israel counterpart declined to shake hands before kick-off Israel levelled two minutes after the interval with Dor Peretz beating goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher from close range. Kelleher and Peretz, who captained their respective nations on the night, had earlier declined to shake hands or exchange pennants pre-match. The pair repeated the stance from last weekend’s initial fixture, when Dara O’Shea and Manor Solomon had led out the two teams. O'Shea missed the second match due to attending the birth of his child, while Solomon was only fit enough to start the match on the bench for Israel. Solomon had previously vowed that his side would take 'revenge' after Ireland's 3-0 win in the first match, after which he said 'they hate us and we don't like them.' Ireland again bowed their heads when the Israeli national anthem played prior to kick-off, while they also wore black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost in the war in Gaza. Israel’s official Government account hit out at the Irish team on social media minutes after the match kicked off, accusing them of ‘moral blindless’. The post explosively compared the pre-match stance to when Ireland played Nazi Germany in May 1939, months before the Second World War. Israel’s official Government hit out at the Irish team minutes after kick-off, explosively drawing a comparison between Ireland's stance and a fixture they played against Nazi Germany in 1939 Troy Parrott gave the Republic of Ireland a first half lead from the penalty spot The match, which initially was set to be held in Dublin, was held behind closed doors in Serbia ‘While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal,’ the post read. ‘1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany. 2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel’s anthem. ‘Different generations. The same moral blindness. ‘Today, Israel’s players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin. ‘Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it.’ The Irish team had come under intense pressure to boycott both fixtures due to Israel’s military actions in Gaza. The calls to withdraw were part of a 'Stop The Game' campaign, organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine. The campaign was supported by former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr and ex-international James McClean. Dor Peretz scored Israel's equaliser two minutes into the second half of the fixture Dor Peretz kissed a black armband, which was worn by Israel players in memory of victims of the attacks on October 7 in 2023 Ireland players voted to play last weekend and wore black armbands in the fixture, which ended in a 3-0 victory. Players and staff, as well as lowering their heads during the Israeli national anthem, opted against exchanging pennants pre-match. Hallgrimsson's players and staff repeated the stance pre-match in Backa Topola. The Serbian town had been selected to host the fixture after a Football Association of Ireland decision in June to move the match overseas. Israel players wore black armbands for the second meeting, with UEFA approving a request to honour the memory of victims of attacks on October 7 in 2023, which saw around 1,200 people killed and 251 taken hostage. Ireland were again without second choice goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who made himself unavailable for both fixtures. Finn Azaz, who has Israeli heritage, was again named on the bench having played the duration of Ireland’s other Nations League ties against Kosovo and Austria. 'It would have been tempting to put him [Azaz] in, but I did not want to put that load on him,' Hallgrimsson said. 'It has probably been the toughest two weeks for him of all our players and staff, an emotional week for him.' On the eve of the match, Ireland were forced to end Hallgrimsson's press conference early after his players were accused of using a racist term to describe Israel players by an Israeli journalist. Heimir Hallgrimsson called for Ireland and Israel to be prevented from playing each other in future The journalist alleged that Ireland players had called their Israeli counterparts 'monkeys', prompting an immediate response from Ireland press officer Kieran Crowley, who said: 'That is completely untrue. That is completely untrue.' An Irish official then attempted to take the microphone from the journalist who insisted that he was doing 'his job' and told him 'you cannot take it' in an attempt to keep hold of it. Irish media reported prior to kick-off that two Israeli journalists were banned by UEFA from attending the post-match press conferences following the chaos. Hallgrimsson was asked post-match whether Ireland and Israel should play together UEFA competitions in future following the animosity over the two matches. ‘No, they shouldn’t. That is not ours to decide, that is UEFA to decide that,' he told RTE. There is obviously a big support for Palestine in Ireland, there are not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does. ‘I wouldn’t wish any national team to go through what we have gone through these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something.'

Sports.title: Erling Haaland limps off during Norway's Nations League clash with Portugal to leave Man City sweating just a week before Liverpool showdown
Sports.content:
Manchester City are sweating over Erling Haaland's fitness after the forward limped off during Norway's Nations League defeat against Portugal on Sunday night.

The 26-year-old had signalled that he wanted to come off with a hand motion during the second half.

His withdrawal comes just a week before Manchester City travel to Liverpool, with their guilty verdict in their batle with the Premier League hanging over them.

The forward was able to walk off the pitch unaided with the score at 1-1, but a 79th-minute goal from Goncalo Ramos saw Portugal win 2-1 in the absence of Cristiano Ronaldo.

Haaland started all four of Norway's Nations League matches in a 10-day spell, scoring in earlier fixture against Denmark and Portugal.

It remains to be seen how much of a headache this could be for City, who also saw Nico O'Reilly withdraw from England duty mid-way through the international break with an injury.

More to follow.

Erling Haaland asked to be subbed and limped off during Norway's 2-1 defeat by Portugal

Haaland has enjoyed a flying start to the season, scoring seven in as many appearances for City, who are top of the Premier League with a perfect record.

He did not get much of a summer break, with Norway having reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup, where they lost to England.

His success is partially built on his capacity to play plenty of games without getting injured. Last season he only missed one match with a knock, and the longest injury of his career in 2023-24 did not even keep him out for two months.

It has been a tough international break for City after the Premier League condemned them for making 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies.

On Friday last week, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges against them.

However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel who oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024.

That then dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'.

It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee.

The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges

As the Premier League note, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend.

Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'.

The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'.

It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies.

Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'.

The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker.

Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.'

Manchester City have insisted on their innocence throughout the saga (Pep Guardiola pictured with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak)

In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’.

It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’

City have until Friday to appeal.

Man City were first charged with the 115 breaches in February 2023. While that totemic number stuck, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130.

Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’.

Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018), an eight-year period which saw the club win four Premier League titles, the FA Cup, and three League Cup competitions.

There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018.

There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023.

The hearing into the 130 breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre, with the Premier League sparing no expense and enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

Sports.title: Tom Brady owns up to rookie on-air mistake that sparked technical issues behind the scenes on Fox broadcast
Sports.content:
Tom Brady owned up after accidentally causing audio issues in the Fox Sports booth during their Week 4 assignment.

Brady and the Fox A-team were in Philadelphia to watch the Eagles take on the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field.

But he inadvertently silenced his producers, causing disruption for him and partner Kevin Burkhardt in the first half before realizing what happened and the fact he was to blame in humiliating circumstances later exposed live on air.

'You want to fess up?' Burkhardt asked his partner. 'The mic issue?' before Brady took the opportunity with both hands.

'Okay, my fault,' Brady said. 'I have this big clunky board which I have all this information about what I want to say all day.'

He showed a large fold-up card filled with notes about the two teams, an insight into his level of preparation, before explaining the chaos it caused.

Tom Brady owned up to a humiliating mistake in the Fox booth during NFL Week 4 action

Now that's a QB owning up to his mistake �� @TomBrady https://t.co/wUt5Zagrpz — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) October 4, 2026

'And I dropped it on the talk back button' he continued. 'And I'm sitting here going, 'guys, I can't hear anyone', and it's my fault the whole time.

'That's like a quarterback owning up to his mistakes, that's what it is.'

Brady was back on air for the first time since an explosive, tell-all book about his life was released.

Lars Anderson, the man who wrote 'Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness,' dove into the seven-time Super Bowl champion's split from the actress and his subsequent romance and marriage to supermodel Gisele Bundchen.

The Daily Mail exclusively published the first extract of the book last week sharing the ugly details of his marriage to Gisele and details of their split.

A second extract from the book shared insight into Brady's private life dating back to his college career and the secrets stashed from the years long before his fame.

Anderson, a Sports Illustrated writer, has previously written a book on the Manning Family and explained his desire to try and give readers an insight into who the seven-time Super Bowl champion 'really is' behind the scenes.

'Numerous books have been written about different aspects of Tom Brady's career, but no one has authored the definitive biography on him: a meaty, deeply reported narrative that gives readers a 360-degree view of his iconic life,' Anderson said to PEOPLE.

A new book on Brady's life has shed light on his marriage and divorce with Gisele Bundchen

'This was the goal as I spent two years digging into the bedrocks of Brady to explain him, interpret his story and answer the fundamental question of who he really is.

'I explore what he represents, what makes him tick, and why he inspires so much passion — you either love him or loathe him.

'I looked at why his relationships with the two famous women who bore his children failed, examined the price of genius and probed his category-five obsession with perfection.

'Employing put-you-there storytelling techniques, my goal was to place the reader next to Brady at all the key moments of his life, recreating scenes to show sides never before seen of the winningest player in NFL history.'

PART ONE: Every ugly detail of Tom and Gisele's marriage... the secret letter stashed in a drawer... and her savage last three words

PART TWO: Why Tom Brady's college teammates were convinced he was gay... until one uninhibited night proved the truth: Secrets from his years before fame - and existential crisis that drove him to the brink

Sports.title: Phil Mickelson is tipped for stunning return to the PGA Tour by LIV Golf's biggest critic in the wake of his 'family trauma' rehab
Sports.content:
Phil Mickelson's biggest critic has tipped him for a shock return to the PGA Tour after it emerged he has been in rehab amid ongoing personal issues.

Mickelson reportedly entered and has already left an addiction center. His representatives told TMZ: 'Phil was seeking treatment for family trauma and addiction.'

The news comes after the 56-year-old, a six-time major champion, stepped away from professional golf this year.

In the meantime, LIV Golf has been torn apart after the withdrawal of Saudi funding, leading to questions over the future of its stars.

Brandel Chamblee, now lead analyst on Golf Channel after his own playing career ended, has been the most outspoken critic of those who turned their backs on the PGA Tour for LIV Golf.

He also has a long history with Mickelson in particular, who told GOLF Magazine in 2018: 'He and I don't see eye to eye on anything.'

Phil Mickelson has been tipped for a PGA Tour return after spending time in a rehab facility

Brandel Chamblee has long been one of Mickelson and LIV Golf's most vocal public critics

But Mickelson has found a surprising olive branch from Chamblee, who believes the legendary leftie would be forgiven and welcomed back if he wanted to be.

Speaking on the We Need a Fourth podcast, Chamblee was asked whether Mickelson has tarnished his legacy for good.

'I don't know about forever,' he said. 'I think we're in a pretty forgiving world. He's obviously got his demons that he fights, and I wouldn't wish them on anybody, but he's not alone in fighting demons.

'I think if he hadn't gone to LIV, he would have been Arnold Palmer reincarnated. He would have been Ryder Cup captain numerous times. He would have been an honorary starter at Augusta. He would have been the lead analyst at CBS. He would have been the pied piper everywhere he went.

'But I think if he came back and said 'look, I've made mistakes, I've tried to deal with them. Sorry for the damage I've caused.

'The game's been so good to me. And for the rest of my life, I'm going to try and be good back to it', I think everyone would put their arms around him and go 'welcome back, sorry you had so much trouble, hope you get your life straightened out'.

'Life's hard, it doesn't matter who you're talking into, running into. Everybody's dealing with something. Everybody's got some battle that they've faced or will face.

'I started doing commentary in 2004, so 2004 until Phil left, I used to say Phil was a gift to the game of golf. His talent, his showmanship, his look at me quality, it was incredible. What a talent, what an amazing talent.'

The golfer and his wife are seen taking in the action on the Sunday of the 2021 Ryder Cup

Mickelson and Amy are pictured with their children, Evan, Sophie and Amanda, after his victory at the 2013 Open Championship

Mickelson stepped away from golf earlier this year and cited an unspecified private family matter involving his wife, Amy, for his absence.

Mickelson has been married to Amy, 54, for almost 30 years after tying the knot back in November 1996. The couple share three children together in Evan, Sophie and Amanda.

He has been candid about his struggles with gambling, previously opening up on his addiction in 2023.

He said at the time that he had 'crossed the line from moderation into addiction which isn't fun at all.'

'The money wasn't ever the issue since our financial security has never been threatened, but I was so distracted I wasn't able to be present with the ones I love and caused a lot of harm,' he said.

He also described how this 'lack of presence' has been 'so hurtful' for his family, saying he's been 'often' told throughout his addiction, 'You're here, but you're not with us.'

'It affected those I care about in ways I wasn't aware or could fully understand,' Mickelson said. 'It's like a hurricane is going on outside and I'm isolated in a shelter oblivious to what was happening.'

'When I came out there was so much damage to clean up that I just wanted to back inside and not deal with it,' he added.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon is playing with swagger and belief - and his telepathic connection with Lewis Hall could mean Thomas Tuchel FINALLY solves a problem area in his team
Sports.content:
It’s a goal and an assist once an hour for Anthony Gordon in an England shirt at the moment. Eight of those vital contributions in his last six games since clambering off the bench for the rescue act against DR Congo, another two added to the growing collection during Saturday’s demolition job in Croatia.

Count winning a penalty in the Azteca as the assist it was and the statistics are even more favourable: a goal contribution every 53 minutes.

Whatever the numbers, something has clicked inside somebody who has felt somewhat underappreciated by the English public and actively wanted to leave the Premier League to alter perceptions of his abilities.

Barcelona suits him, the £68million man whose performances in Catalonia are delighting Culers in much the same way as his use of Spanish at the summer unveiling.

Thomas Tuchel has noticed an extra air of confidence to him through this international camp (three goals and an assist), a sense of greater understanding around new-found seniority and a belief that he is now one of England’s main pillars.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Bukayo Saka are locks in three of the attacking positions. It’s impossible to argue against Gordon’s inclusion as the fourth after the past few months.

Anthony Gordon (centre) and Lewis Hall (right) have a flourishing understanding

‘Anthony plays with a lot more edge,’ Tuchel said. ‘He’s for sure found another level, another gear, and is very decisive.’ The very best grow the higher they climb.

Gordon believes that Congo, changing the game in Atlanta’s indoor arena when the air was rapidly leaving England’s World Cup balloon, positively shifted his international arc.

By his own admission, it takes him a while to settle within a group – although that hasn’t seemed a problem at Barca – and now approaching 30 caps, it has become time to take ownership of the left wing. Particularly as Marcus Rashford nudged himself back into the frame last season and provided stiff competition in America.

Gordon’s goal in Rijeka on Saturday evening, England’s third of the night, was a flying header to follow up another smart header in Prague days earlier. To highlight just how things are landing for him right now, the former Newcastle United forward has not scored a single header across 248 career club appearances.

There is a swagger, noticeable in how he toyed with markers at the weekend. Josip Stanisic of Bayern Munich will have endured nightmares. The way Gordon stopped an attack dead, stood Stanisic up and then strutted past provided embarrassment for a full back who started both legs of the Champions League semi-final under Vincent Kompany last season. Croatia might as well have picked one of the kids in the stands.

Poor Stanisic was only provided mercy by Slaven Bilic once Gordon had earned his rest, which in itself felt unfair. Yet there might be some relief that the 25-year-old didn’t make the experience even more chastening, missing three big chances across his 70 minutes. It really could, and should, have been 10.

One of those arrived seconds after Kane’s early opener and engineered by Lewis Hall, his former team-mate at St James’ Park. Hall’s had a strong week himself after Nico O’Reilly’s injury and the connection between the two is obvious, a telepathy that Tuchel must want to tap into more.

Quieter and more reserved, Hall is offering evidence that an incisiveness from the middle third – the pass for that Gordon chance had precision and perfect weight – is being matched by defensive doggedness. Possessing both is a rare find in modern full backs.

Gordon's form for Barcelona and England has taken him to a different level this season

To illustrate that, during a brief moment of England panic – Croatia breaking and the visitors defensively misshapen – Hall held up the galloping Franjo Ivanovic to allow others a return to their normal positions and the danger was adequately snuffed. Later on, and with England already five goals up, it was Hall’s relentless pressing inside the Croatia box that prompted a gift for Saka to smash into the net’s roof.

Hall had to deal with the setback of missing out on the World Cup squad and felt he was worthy of a spot, the response being an encouraging start to this campaign and carrying on where he left off for Newcastle. Hall, 23, has spoken openly about having to ‘play catch up’ with Tuchel’s general messaging during the camp, with the majority of the players familiar after seven weeks together Stateside.

Individually things are going well and as a pairing, they look a proper package. Tuchel loves his combinations – Bellingham and Kane, Guehi and Konsa, Quansah and Saka when Reece James isn’t fit. He wants them all over the pitch and the left-hand side has felt like a forever problem for England.

Gordon has unequivocally done more than anybody else to nail down the attacking spot, with Hall now in a straight battle with O’Reilly for the supporting role. Even before this week, the left has appeared in ruder health than for some time.

In the knockout stages of 2021, 2022 and 2024 tournaments, Luke Shaw had the place sorted for himself but there was uncertainty about what lay ahead of him. Phil Foden’s versatility meant he was shunted wide in 2022 and two years later, in a bid to play the Manchester City star inside, Shaw operated as a wing back as Gareth Southgate went to a back three to the detriment of any real flair.

The combinations weren’t quite there and Tuchel has had some questions answered across his tenure, with some crystallised during the first camp of the season.

‘I don’t want to write Nico O’Reilly off because he played for us in the first match,’ Tuchel said. ‘Lewis had two good matches now. He loves to play in the offensive full back position, he’s very good on the ball. He loves ball possession. He is very clinical, loves these little movements.

‘He played very well with Anthony. You can see that they’ve played many seasons together in the coordination of their movements. He helped Anthony a lot.’

Gordon has now taken ownership of the left wing position under Thomas Tuchel

Saturday was their 58th start together for club and country; as Tuchel alluded to, it showed. There is a little more power and physicality than advertised in them, Gordon leaning into his wiry frame and hustling in recovery runs to back up his mate, with Hall’s engine providing a different dimension going the other way.

‘I’m nowhere near the player I can be,’ Gordon told ITV last week when dissecting the move to Barca and his increased international standing. He regularly journals private targets and starring in La Liga appears to have been one. ‘Maybe delusionally I’ve [envisioned] it from a young age. Why would I have so much confidence from a young age? It makes no sense. I can’t explain why.

‘I’ve become a different player in a lot of people’s eyes. I always felt in England that people respected me because I was fast and I pressed but they never actually respected the quality and IQ that I play with. Only the players I play with seem to notice that. Now that I’m at Barcelona and playing a different style, those qualities are highlighted much more and people are starting to take notice that I’m not just quick.’

He spoke at length with Kane about the prospect of Barca, the side effects of leaving familiarities, and given the captain’s explosion at Bayern – in the running for this year’s Ballon d’Or – the feedback was to go for it wholeheartedly.

Gordon has never been shy, Everton fans will tell you that with the way he moved to Newcastle, and is still surprised at coming off against Argentina as England retreated. In being honest with himself in the quest for constant improvement and proving he deserves a place on this stage, he vows to become more selfish around the box.

Five assists in his first four Barca matches suggests that might need a bit of work. Not a lot else does and it is inarguable that Gordon looks even slicker with his mate behind him.

Sports.title: Former Premier League boss Jesse Marsch claims 'EVERYONE knew' about Man City's cheating - and calls for club to be relegated after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Former Premier League boss Jesse Marsch claims 'EVERYONE knew' about Man City's cheating - and calls for club to be relegated after guilty verdict

Former Leeds United manager Jesse Marsch has insisted 'everyone knew' about Manchester City's cheating and has called for the club to be relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching financial rules.

Marsch was appointed as Leeds boss in February 2022 but was sacked 12 months later as the club battled to avoid relegation from the Premier League.

The 52-year-old, who is now in charge of Canada, was asked about an independent commission ruling verdict that ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period peppered with ‘sham’ deals.

In a damning 40-page verdict, published on Tuesday, found City artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

While the ruling covered the period between 2009-2018, Marsch expressed his belief that there were 'inconsistencies' even during his time in the Premier League.

Marsch told the Guardian that Man City should be relegated from the top flight as a result of the verdict. Man City confirmed on Friday that they have lodged an appeal to overturn the independent commission's verdict.

Jesse Marsch, left, has claimed 'everyone knew' about Man City's cheating as he called for the club to be relegated from the top flight

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of charges against them by the Premier League, but have launched an appeal against the decision

'I think Man City should be punished severely. I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew,' Marsch said.

'That summer [2022], us and Man City were the only teams that said we made money.

'For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips [to City]. We had a lot left over from what we bought.

'At the time, we weren't in a position financially to not save. Our ownership didn't have deep pockets.

'Whereas when Man City says this, I was literally like, "Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?"

'When they said they got Erling Haaland for £52m, it's like: "Yeah, OK, sure".

'So, I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, "This is football".

The 2022 summer referred to by Marsch had seen clubs reveal their accounts for the 2020-21 season, which had been played behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

Marsch questioned Man City announcing profits in the summer of 2022, along with questioning their £52m deal to sign his former player Erling Haaland from Borussia Dortmund

Man City signed Kalvin Phillips from Leeds in the summer of 2022 in a £42million transfer

Leeds announced an operating profit of £5.5m, with the club's income having been boosted by their return to the top flight following promotion from the Championship the previous campaign.

Man City reported a narrow £2.4m profit in the same period having reported losses of £126m in the 2019-20 season.

The club's run to the 2021 Champions League final and their fourth Premier League title under Pep Guardiola were cited as key reasons for their financial success.

Marsch's comments also highlighted the summer transfer window in 2022, which saw Man City sign Haaland for £52m and bring in Phillips from his Leeds side in a £42m deal.

Leeds also sold Brazilian star Raphinha to Barcelona for £55m, with the club using the finances from both deals to fund close to £140m of incomings.

Leeds, who sacked Marsch in February 2023, were relegated at the end of the season.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that the Premier League could review transactions following 2018, the final year covered by their investigation into Man City.

Man City's appeal against the independent commission verdict was made on Friday, with the club stating it 'maintains its innocence'.

Much of their defence will claim commercial contracts were paid for by the Abu Dhabi government rather than their owner.

Sports.title: £65m Man City signing hints at return to old club days after 114 charges verdict
Sports.content:
£65m Man City signing hints at return to old club days after 114 charges verdict

A player who signed for Manchester City for £65million in the summer has hinted that he would be keen on a move back to his former club

View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye signed for Manchester City in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City summer signing Iliman Ndiaye has hinted that he would been keen on returning to former club Marseille in the future and admitted: "I don't think the story is over."

‌



‌



Ndiaye, 26, joined City in a £65million deal from Everton in the summer and has made an impressive start to life at the Etihad Stadium. Although the Senegal international hasn't produced a single goal or an assist in his first four appearances, he has helped City continue their winning start and was a standout performer when he came on against Manchester United last month.

‌



But, despite joining City less than five weeks ago, Ndiaye has now revealed that he would like to return to Marseille in the future. The French-born attacking midfielder spent one season at the Stade Velodrome, after joining from Sheffield United for £20m in 2023, before leaving to sign for Everton 12 months later. He scored just four times and provided five assists in 46 games for the Ligue 1 side.

‌



Man City fight back with 'PROOF' government paid sponsorship deals in appeal over 115 charges READ MORE :

When asked about Marseille fans chanting for him to return to the club, Ndiaye said: "The shouts from Marseille supporters asking me to come back? It is nice to hear. I don't think that the story is finished, but we will see. I'm just saying, I never know where it'll lead me, but we'll see anyway.

"I only have positive memories of my time at OM [Marseille], and it was a source of pride for me. I don't miss a single match. It's my club, and it always will be."

Ndiaye is thought to have supported Marseille since he was a child and jumped at the chance to sign for them when he left Sheffield United three years ago. Although it didn't work out during his short time in southern France, it appears he wouldn't say no to giving it another shot.

‌



View 2 Images Iliman Ndiaye in action for Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Ndiaye's comments come just days after the Premier League announced that City have been found guilty of all charges concerning breaches of its financial regulations spanning from 2009/10 to 2017/18. These included artificially inflating revenue by over £900million through "sham" sponsorship agreements.

City, however, have denied any wrongdoing and appealed the decision on Thursday. The club believe they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and say they have "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their case.

‌



"Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter," City said in a statement on Friday.

"The Club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

Article continues below

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."
