World.title: IPO: University students hail Dangote Foundation’s free share initiative
World.content:
…Foundation engages campus journalists on IPO

By Udeme Akpan

University students across Nigeria have welcomed the Aliko Dangote Foundation’s Student Share Grant Initiative, describing it as an opportunity to participate in wealth creation and gain practical investment experience through the ongoing Initial Public Offering, IPO, of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, DPRP.

As part of efforts to raise awareness and deepen financial literacy among young Nigerians, the Foundation, over the weekend, held an online engagement with campus journalists from tertiary institutions across the country.

The session focused on the Dangote Refinery IPO, the importance of financial education, responsible investing and opportunities available through Nigeria’s capital market.

Under the Student Share Grant Initiative, eligible students aged 18 and above in public and private tertiary institutions can receive free DPRP shares after purchasing a minimum of 10 shares through the dedicated platform, ipo.alikodangotefoundation.org. For every qualifying subscription, the Foundation provides an additional 10 shares at no extra cost to the student.

The programme is designed to introduce young Nigerians to investing early in life while promoting financial literacy, ownership and long-term wealth creation.

The initiative has generated interest across campuses, with students describing it as an opportunity to become shareholders in one of Africa’s major industrial projects while gaining practical knowledge of investment.

Speaking on the initiative, Amaechi Rosemary, a student of the University of Ibadan, said the programme had made investing more accessible to students.

“Many students hear about shares and investments but never imagine they can become shareholders while still in school. This initiative removes that barrier and gives us an opportunity to learn about wealth creation through practical participation,” she said.

Emmanuel Ndah, also of the University of Ibadan, described the initiative as both educational and empowering.

“Owning shares in a world-class refinery is exciting. Beyond the additional shares, the programme teaches us important lessons about investing and financial responsibility. It is encouraging to see young people being included in Nigeria’s economic growth story,” he said.

Similarly, Moshood Muheeb of Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, said the initiative demonstrated confidence in the ability of Nigerian youths to build wealth responsibly.

“This programme sends a strong message that students are not too young to invest. The support provided by the Foundation makes the opportunity even more attractive and encourages young people to start planning for their financial future,” he said.

Esther Olatunji of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, said the initiative could encourage students to take investing and financial planning more seriously.

“This is more than a share offer. It is an opportunity to learn about ownership, financial discipline and long-term wealth creation. Programmes like this can inspire students to develop healthy investment habits that will benefit them throughout their lives,” she said.

The students also noted that the initiative had generated conversations around investing, saving and asset ownership on campuses, potentially broadening awareness of financial planning among young Nigerians.

Eligible students enrolled in recognised tertiary institutions can visit the Foundation’s dedicated platform to complete the verification process. Following successful verification, participants can subscribe for a minimum of 10 DPRP shares and qualify for an additional 10 shares funded by the Aliko Dangote Foundation.

According to the Foundation, the initiative is a stand-alone programme designed to encourage investment participation among Nigerian youths and help develop a generation of financially informed investors with a stake in the country’s economic future.

Chairman of the Aliko Dangote Foundation, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, said the initiative aligned with the Foundation’s commitment to empowering young people beyond traditional educational support.

“Supporting young people goes beyond access to education. It also involves providing opportunities that enable them to participate meaningfully in economic growth and wealth creation. Through this initiative, we want students to understand the value of saving, investing wisely and building wealth through ownership,” he said.

Dangote said exposing young people to investment opportunities early could positively influence their financial decisions and encourage greater participation in the formal economy.

“When young people understand ownership and investing from an early stage, they are better equipped to make sound financial decisions, build wealth responsibly and contribute to national development,” he added.

Chief Executive Officer of the Aliko Dangote Foundation, Mrs Zouera Youssoufou, said the programme combined financial education with practical investment experience.

“Financial literacy becomes more meaningful when individuals can apply what they learn. This initiative enables students to experience the investment process firsthand, from verification and subscription to share ownership, while reinforcing the importance of responsible participation in the capital market,” she said.

Youssoufou added that the Foundation’s objective extended beyond the current IPO.

“We hope to inspire a lifelong interest in investing, financial literacy and asset ownership among young Nigerians. The experience and knowledge gained through this programme can serve as a foundation for sound financial decision-making throughout their lives,” she said.

The Student Share Grant Initiative forms part of the Foundation’s broader youth empowerment and economic inclusion efforts, encouraging students to embrace saving, investing, entrepreneurship and long-term wealth creation.

World.title: Ronaldo can return to Portugal team if he wants – Coach Jesus
World.content:
File: Portugal’s forward Cristiano Ronaldo reacts during the UEFA Nations League semi-final football match between Germany and Portugal in Munich, southern Germany on June 4, 2025. Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP.

Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo can return to the squad if he wishes, despite walking out on his team-mates, said national team coach Jorge Jesus on Sunday.

Jesus said Ronaldo can come back into the fold “if he wants to” after the team beat Norway without the veteran attacker to reach the Nations League quarter-finals.

The dispute began last week when Jesus left 41-year-old Ronaldo on the bench for Portugal’s first win over Norway. Ronaldo subsequently walked out on the squad on Wednesday after learning he would not start against Denmark.

“For me, Cris, in the next call-up, if he’s playing at Al-Nassr, he’ll be a player who can be called up,” Jesus told reporters, referring to Ronaldo’s Saudi club side. “If he wants to, he’ll return to the national team.”

The coach said if Ronaldo wishes to speak to him before Portugal’s next matches in November, that would happen.

“If he wants to, as we did before this call-up, we talked before the call-up, we can talk before the next call-up,” continued Jesus. “But Cris is the one who’s going to decide.”

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo is Portugal’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

Jesus said he had told Ronaldo he needed him in the squad for his first games at the helm after replacing Roberto Martinez following the 2026 World Cup.

“Cristiano should end his time in the national team the way he wants, he’s the one who will decide how he wants it,” said Jesus.

“That’s how we talked, the two of us — I said, ‘I need you’. In my first call-up, I said, ‘I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you’. And now I’m saying the same thing.”

Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football.

The forward has been a fixture of the national team for more than two decades and has played at six World Cups.

In Ronaldo’s absence Portugal became the first team to secure a place in the quarter-finals, with two group games still to play.

Ronaldo’s long-time rival for the title of the world’s best player, Lionel Messi, will play his final match for Argentina in a friendly against Benin in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.

Vanguard News

World.title: 2027: Tinubu will harvest more votes in Southeast – Umahi
World.content:
Umahi

Minister of Works Dave Umahi has predicted that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will make significant gains in the South-East in the 2027 presidential election, saying President Bola Tinubu will secure far more support in the region than the party did in the last election.

Umahi spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, where he discussed the APC’s prospects in the region and its chances of improving on its 2023 performance.

“I will not tell you whether we win the five votes of the South-East or not, but the President is going to harvest a lot of votes in the South-East. It can never be the same like it was before,” he said.

Asked specifically how many of the five South-East states he believed the APC could win, Umahi said he expected the party to take all of them.

“My faith is telling me we’ll win the five states,” he said.

Umahi also dismissed the suggestion that Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), poses a threat to Tinubu or the APC ahead of the 2027 election.

“By the way it is not only Peter Obi that is from the South-East that is contesting. We have about three or four other presidential candidates who are contesting.

“We have the Labour Party and I think there are other two, even a woman is involved. So, Peter Obi is not a threat as far as I am concerned,” Umahi said.

The minister’s comments come as political parties and presidential contenders intensify preparations ahead of the 2027 general election, with the South-East expected to remain a key battleground.

Vanguard News

World.title: Tinubu visits Oba of Lagos, receives prayers, counsels
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday paid a courtesy visit to the Oba of Lagos, Oba Rilwan Akiolu, at Iga Idunganran Palace, Lagos Island.

The visit provided an opportunity for the President to receive royal prayers and counsel from the traditional ruler for his administration.

Tinubu was received at the palace by members of the royal household and enthusiastic residents who gathered to welcome him.

Supporters, All Progressives Congress (APC) members and well-wishers lined the streets around Marina and Isale Eko as the President’s motorcade approached.

The gathering created a festive atmosphere, with residents cheering the President and expressing enthusiasm over his presence on Lagos Island.

The royal father offered prayers for Tinubu, his administration and the nation, seeking divine guidance and continued peace and prosperity.

Oba Akiolu also offered counsel to the President on matters concerning the country and the wellbeing of Nigerians.

The meeting underscored the traditional institution’s role in maintaining dialogue with the Federal Government and supporting national development.

Tinubu was accompanied by Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Also accompanying the President were APC stalwarts, political associates and other dignitaries who joined him during the visit.

The President’s visit formed part of his engagements with prominent Nigerians, traditional rulers and other stakeholders since his return to Lagos.

Tinubu returned to Lagos from his working vacation and has continued meetings with important personalities and stakeholders across different sectors.

The engagements have provided opportunities for the President to interact with influential figures and exchange views on national and state-level developments.

His meeting with Oba Akiolu further strengthened the longstanding relationship between the presidency and traditional institutions in Lagos.

The Oba of Lagos, as a prominent traditional authority, remains an influential voice on issues affecting Lagos State and the country.

The President’s presence also drew significant public attention, with residents gathering along major routes to catch a glimpse of his motorcade.

The visit ended with Tinubu departing the palace after the traditional ruler’s prayers and goodwill for the President and the country.

World.title: Portugal edge Norway to become first team through to Nations League quarter-finals
World.content:
Portugal’s forward #09 Goncalo Ramos celebrates with Portugal’s forward #11 Joao Felix and Portugal’s defender #03 Ruben Dias (L) scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Nations League Group 4 football match between Portugal and Norway at Dragao stadium in Porto on October 3, 2026 (Photo by Miguel RIOPA / AFP)

Portugal defeated Norway 2-1 without sulking superstar striker Cristiano Ronaldo on Sunday to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Goncalo Ramos secured a comeback victory for Jorge Jesus’s Portugal in the Group A4 clash after Joao Cancelo’s rocket levelled Kristoffer Ajer’s stunning opener for Norway.

Portugal played out the final minutes with 10 men after Francisco Conceicao was dismissed for two yellow cards in the space of a few seconds for dissent after he appealed for a penalty unsuccessfully.

Former Real Madrid and Manchester United striker Ronaldo walked out on the squad on Wednesday ahead of the previous game against Denmark, after Portugal’s all-time top goalscorer learned he would not start.

Portugal are now guaranteed to finish in the top two spots in the group with two matches to spare, thus becoming the first team to reach the last eight in March 2027.

“Cristiano is our captain, the best player Portugal has ever had,” Cancelo told RTP.

“Things will certainly end in the best way (with Ronaldo) but the important thing is the four victories.”

Norway took the lead in Porto against the run of play with a stunning effort from Brentford defender Ajer after 36 minutes.

The Norwegian met a bouncing ball on the edge of the box perfectly to bend it into the top corner.

However two minutes later Barcelona defender Cancelo scored a similarly superb goal, rifling home from around 20 yards.

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland fired across the face of goal after an hour and was replaced by Jorgen Strand Larsen a few minutes later.

Nations League holders and two-time record champions Portugal nosed in front when AC Milan striker Ramos, starting in place of Ronaldo, tucked home from close range.

Ramos was teed up by Joao Felix, who reached Vitinha’s lofted pass and put it on a plate for the forward.

Ramos scored for a third consecutive game, and helped Portugal seal back-to-back wins since 41-year-old forward Ronaldo left the squad.

Conceicao’s foolish dismissal left Jesus’s team in a tough spot for the final few minutes. The Juventus winger was about to be replaced by Pedro Neto but his complaints led to a red card before the substitution could happen.

Portugal held on to triumph for the fourth time in four games in the group, completing a successful first international window for 72-year-old coach Jesus, despite the Ronaldo controversy.

“Any player who comes to the national team is welcome, obviously. If Cris returns, we’ll be here to receive him with open arms,” said Portugal defender Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Brazil braces for results of election battle between Lula and Bolsonaro
World.content:
A couple walks down the street wearing Brazilian national team jerseys during the presidential election in Porto Alegre, Brazil, on October 4, 2026. Brazilians head to the polls in a highly polarized presidential election between incumbent leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva -seeking a fourth presidential mandate- and right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who emerged as the leading figure of the conservative movement following the conviction and imprisonment of his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. (Photo by SILVIO AVILA / AFP)

Brazilians waited anxiously Sunday for the results of a tight election race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro that will determine if the Latin American powerhouse joins a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump.

From the Amazon rainforest to the agricultural heartlands in the south and sprawling urban favelas, Brazilians queued to cast their vote, many of them fed-up with familiar choices.

Lula, almost 81, is seeking a fourth term in an election which he has branded a battle between democracy and “barbarism,” warning voters that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake in the face of US pressure.

He is facing a tough battle against right-wing senator Bolsonaro, 45, eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his failed 2022 re-election bid.

Little known until a few months ago, Flavio Bolsonaro, who describes himself as more moderate than his firebrand father, has vowed to “rescue” Brazil from Lula, corruption, high taxes and crime.

Oscarina de Oliveira, a 62-year-old caregiver, told AFP she had planned to vote for Lula, as she always has. But “when I got there, I switched to Bolsonaro. Just to see what happens, to see if anything changes.”

Results are expected within a few hours after polls closed, due to the vast nation’s electronic voting system.

Opinion surveys show neither Lula or Bolsonaro were likely to score more than 50 percent — the threshold required to win in the first round. They and are neck-and-neck if the vote goes to a runoff on October 25.

Both candidates have extremely high rejection rates in the deeply polarized nation where a bitter election campaign featured more scandals and mud-slinging than policy and promises.

While all eyes are on the presidential race, Brazilians are also electing lawmakers, senators and governors.

– ‘Flaws and all’ –

Lula is more popular in Brazil’s poor northeast, among low-income voters, Catholics, and women.

“Lula is the only one doing anything for us — at least for us working-class people — flaws and all,” said Sabrina, 34, selling drinks in Rio de Janeiro.

Revered for social welfare programs that lifted millions out of poverty, Lula made a dramatic comeback to office in the 2022 elections after being jailed on a corruption conviction that was later thrown out on procedural grounds.

Riots in Brasilia and the botched coup attempt after his election allowed him to cast himself as guardian of Brazil’s democracy.

In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, but voters complain about a high cost of living.

Lula has also sharply curbed deforestation in the Amazon, while backing oil exploration.

Despite a growing number of extreme weather events in Brazil, climate change has been absent from the campaign.

“It is important to elect a candidate who defends our territory, who defends nature,” said Tainara da Costa Cruz, 22, who lives along the banks of the Rio Negro in Amazonas state and voted for Lula.

– Trump watching –

Buoyed by his father’s legacy, Bolsonaro leads in the south, among wealthier voters and evangelical Christians.

In a cascade of scandals that dominated the campaign, it emerged that Bolsonaro was under investigation for corruption over the financing of the biopic “Dark Horse” about his father.

For many voters, this did little to move the needle.

“Things are truly terrible. As far as I’m concerned, the left just doesn’t work anymore,” said tech worker Joao Batista, 36, in the Rocinha favela, saying he was fed up with the “horrible” expense of basic goods.

Bolsonaro’s rallies featured massive US flags and images of Trump, who has said he is “very closely” watching the election, but did not endorse the candidate.

The US president has wielded tariffs and sanctions to pressure Brasilia over complaints ranging from the trial against his ally Jair Bolsonaro to alleged unfair trade practices.

Lula repeatedly warned him not to “meddle” in the elections.

He also argued that Brazil would retain control over the development of its vast reserves of rare earths, which have attracted interest from Washington and other foreign powers.

Flavio Bolsonaro has pitched Brazil as a “solution” to ease US dependence on China for these critical minerals.

“I support Lula because he stands up for the poor. Flavio will sell our Brazil off to foreigners,” said Victor Jorge Martins, a 25-year-old event planner.

World.title: NGE Demands 50% Presidential Threshold, Pre-Inauguration Resolution of Election Disputes
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator



The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called for a constitutional and electoral reforms, including a requirement that presidential candidates should secure at least 50 per cent of votes cast to be declared winners, as well as the resolution of electoral disputes before the swearing-in of declared winners.

The Guild also called for a review of the appointment process for the Chairman, National Commissioners and Resident Electoral Commissioners of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), as well as State Electoral Commissioners, to strengthen the independence and credibility of electoral institutions.

The resolutions were contained in the communiqué issued at the end of the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC 2026), recently held in Enugu, as signed by the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh.

The conference, with the theme, “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive,” was chaired by the Obi of Onitsha, His Royal Majesty, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, while the Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, His Eminence John Cardinal Onaiyekan, delivered the keynote address. Vice President Kashim Shettima participated virtually as Special Guest of Honour, while Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, was the Chief Host.

More than 500 editors, publishers and senior media practitioners from print, broadcast and digital platforms, alongside political, traditional, religious, academic, regulatory and development-sector leaders, participated in the conference.

The Guild said the conference examined challenges confronting Nigeria’s electoral democracy ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly voter apathy, electoral insecurity, declining public confidence, misinformation, disinformation and the growing threat posed by artificial intelligence.

According to the editors, although the ballot remained the principal instrument through which citizens exercise their sovereign will, its value depended on credible information, confidence in the electoral process and the assurance that votes would be properly counted and respected.

The Guild attributed voter apathy to several factors, including poor governance, electoral violence and intimidation, administrative shortcomings, declining public confidence and concerns over the relationship between electoral outcomes and subsequent judicial decisions.

It said judicial interventions in some electoral disputes had created perceptions in sections of the public that court decisions could displace outcomes recorded at the ballot box.

The NGE, however, stressed the need to respect judicial independence, while advocating an electoral adjudication system that is “timely, transparent, predictable and impartial.”

It called for electoral disputes to be resolved within appropriate timelines and, preferably, before the swearing-in of declared winners.

The editors also recommended the consideration of a constitutional threshold requiring a presidential candidate to secure up to 50 per cent of votes cast, with a run-off where no candidate attains the threshold.

The Guild further called for a review of limitations preventing ordinary voters from challenging electoral results and advocated a constitutional framework that would allow independent candidacy.

On the independence of the electoral management body, the NGE called for reforms to the process of appointing the INEC Chairman, National Commissioners and Resident Electoral Commissioners, as well as State Electoral Commissioners.

It also urged INEC to sustain nationwide election-readiness assessments, strengthen technical partnerships for cybersecurity and electoral technology, ensure the technical integrity of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and safeguard the institutional independence of the commission.

The editors said all technology deployed in elections must remain subject to “human oversight, transparency, accountability and legal verification.”

The Guild also raised concerns over the growing use of artificial intelligence in election-related disinformation, warning that generative AI, deepfakes, voice cloning and automated networks could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

It noted that synthetic content could now be rapidly produced and distributed, including fabricated election results, cloned voices of public officials, forged documents, manipulated result sheets and fake reports attributed to established media organisations.

“The greatest danger is not merely the circulation of individual falsehoods but the broader erosion of public trust when citizens become unable to distinguish authentic information from fabricated content,” the Guild said.

It consequently urged newsrooms to institutionalise fact-checking and verification systems and integrate digital verification, deepfake detection and forensic tools into their editorial workflows ahead of the 2027 elections.

The editors also reaffirmed the Nigerian Media Code of Election Coverage (Revised 2022), jointly endorsed by the Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria, Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria, Nigeria Union of Journalists, NGE, Radio, Television, Theatre and Arts Workers Union and Guild of Corporate Online Publishers.

The Guild urged news organisations to adopt the code and train journalists and other editorial staff on its provisions.

On the role of the media, the NGE reaffirmed its responsibility to provide accurate, verified and independent information while scrutinising governments, political parties and other centres of power.

It, however, cautioned that media scrutiny should not amount to suppressing legitimate achievements.

The Guild called for evidence-based journalism that neither exaggerates failures nor suppresses verified achievements, stressing that editorial neutrality means impartiality among legitimate political contenders.

It added that neutrality did not require journalists to remain silent in the face of verified wrongdoing or create false equivalence between established facts and unverified claims.

The conference also called on governments at all levels to remain transparent and accountable and cooperate with the media in the legitimate exercise of its watchdog role, including scrutiny of public programmes and expenditure.

It urged government and political actors to guarantee equitable access to media space for both government and opposition voices while respecting editorial independence.

On election security, the Guild declared that the protection of journalists must be an integral part of electoral security.

It warned that the electoral process could not be fully transparent where journalists were threatened, attacked, obstructed or prevented from independently observing and reporting events.

It therefore called on security agencies and political actors to protect journalists and allow them to perform their constitutional and professional responsibilities without intimidation.

The editors also addressed the challenge of reporting terrorism, noting the need to balance the public’s right to know with the risk that irresponsible reporting could amplify terrorist propaganda, aid recruitment, compromise security operations or traumatise victims.

The conference consequently endorsed the principle, “Inform, Don’t Amplify.”

It urged newsrooms to identify terrorist claims as claims until independently verified and avoid reproducing propaganda, recruitment messages, slogans or graphic material except where there was compelling editorial justification.

The Guild said acts of terrorism should be reported responsibly and accurately without giving undue publicity or “oxygen” to terrorist organisations or inadvertently encouraging further violence.

The NGE also reaffirmed that the media should remain “pro-Nigeria, pro-Ballot and pro-People”, rather than align with any political party.

It stressed that the credibility of Nigeria’s democracy ultimately depended on an electoral process in which citizens could make informed choices, cast their votes freely and have confidence that their votes would be accurately counted and respected.

World.title: 2027:   Non-Indigenes, Hunters in Ogun, Youths in Kwara Pledge Support for Tinubu
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta and Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Hunters and Non-Indigenes resident in Ogun State as well as youth group in Kwara State, weekend, pledged to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in next year’s general election.

The hunters operating under the umbrella of Ilupeju Egba Hunters Assocition, Abeokuta and Association of Non Indigenes in Ogun State, expressed their positions during a separate meetings with the convener of Pan Nigerian movement campaigning for re-election of Tinubu, “The Alternative”, Chief Segun Sowunmi.

While Sowunmi met with hunters at a hall in ancient area of Itoko in Abeokuta, he held meeting with non indigenes comprising Igbo. Igede, Tiv, Igala among others at Leme area also in Abeokuta, Ogun State capital.

Seriki Ode of Egbaland, Chief Bamigbose Olusegun, who spoke on behalf of the hunters, assured Sowunmi that they had no doubt that Tinubu would consolidate on the good works that the All Progressive Congress (APC) administration was doing.

Bamigbose said with Sowunmi, they were sure that he would carry their messages to the top.

On behalf of non-indigenes, Chief Francis Nweze, urged Sowunmi to continue his support for non indigenes residing in the state.

Addressing the meetings, Sowunmi described the 2027 election as an opportunity to demonstrate support for the rotation of political power to the South.

Sowunmi, who emphasised his longstanding relationship with communities from different parts of Nigeria resident in Ogun, said he regarded them as part of what he described as the “Ogun tribe”—a broad identity encompassing everyone who lives, works and contributes to the development of the state.

“That tribe called the Ogun tribe is the tribe that contains all of us that agree that this Ogun State is our home, our place of business, our place where we are living and doing everything we are doing,” he said.

52-Youth Coalition Backs Tinubu in 2027

Also, in Kwara State, the 52-Youth Coalition in has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election to enable him consolidate his laudable programmes for the people of the country.

The coalition said Tinubu remains the only option currently available for the next year general election as none has demonstrated that they were better than him.

Speaking at a press conference on the state of the nation in Ilorin, the Deputy Central Coordinator of the group, Mr. Issa Abdulgafar Arikewuyo, faulted the purported claim of the APC governors in the country that the emergence of Rainbow Coalition would affect the chances of Tinubu’s reelection.

The coalition, made up of young professionals drawn from the 52 wards of Kwara Central, said it was working with similar groups in Kwara South and Kwara North to build a statewide platform focused on accountability, security, economic opportunities and democratic participation.

It said its support for Tinubu at the national level did not amount to an endorsement of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) government in Kwara, adding that voters could support different political parties for different elective offices.

According to the group, the arrangement was not new to Nigerian politics, citing the 1999 and 1983 elections in Kwara as examples of voters making different choices at the presidential and state levels.

“Let us be clear about where the 52-Youth Coalition stands. We are supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu because, among the options currently available, none has demonstrated that he is better than him.



“Besides, we believe President Tinubu also deserves the time required to consolidate the policies and reforms his administration has begun.

“Here in Kwara, we are working actively and deliberately to deliver victory for the candidates of the Rainbow Coalition, the Peoples Democratic Party’s candidates for the governorship and the National Assembly.

“We strongly believe Kwara needs fresh air in its leadership and governance. We cannot continue to reward a government defined by insecurity, waste, absenteeism and intolerance for accountability within its own ranks.

“We, therefore, call on all Kwarans, young and old, across the 16 local government areas, to vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the presidential election, and for the candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party in the governorship and National Assembly elections in 2027,” Arikewuyo added.

World.title: 2027: 3,000 APC Members, Baruten APC LG Chairman Defect to PDP in Kwara State
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Ahead of the 2027 general election, about 3,000 members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Alanamu Ward, Ilorin West Local Government Area of Kwara State, weekend, defected to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).



Also, the chairman of the APC in Baruten local government area of the state, Hon. Sani Isa Adamu, has resigned from the party and joined the PDP in the state.



The defectors, who were supporters of Senator Saliu Mustapha under the aegis of Saliu Mustapha Supporters (SMS), were drawn from various polling units across the local government.

They were officially received into the PDP on Saturday after a rally attended by key party stakeholders.



Speaking at the party secretariat in Alanamu Ward, Alhaji AbdulRazaq Adio, who led the defectors, said their decision to join the PDP was driven by their continued support for Senator Mustapha, as well as their confidence in the leadership of former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, and the direction of the party ahead of the 2027 elections.



Adio said they decided to align with the PDP following Senator Mustapha’s defection from the APC and his emergence as the party’s senatorial candidate for Kwara Central.



“We are here because of our principal, Senator Saliu Mustapha. He (Senator Mustapha) is a distinguished politician who is loved by all. We will continue to stand by him wherever he chooses to pursue his political career.

“We are also encouraged by the leadership of our former Senate President, Dr Bukola Saraki, and the direction of the PDP in Kwara State. We believe in the party’s leadership and are ready to work with other members to achieve success in 2027.”



The PDP Alanamu Ward Chairman, Mallam Abdulgafar Alawo, while receiving the defectors, described their decision to join the party as timely and significant.



He assured the defectors of the party’s support and cooperation, noting that their arrival would further strengthen the PDP at the grassroots.

Alawo, however, urged them to see their membership of the PDP as an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to the success of the party in the 2027 general elections.

Meanwhile, the chairman of APC in Baruten Local Government Area of the state, Hon. Sani Musa Adamu has resigned from the party and also joined the PDP in the state.



Adamu, in his letter of resignation, stated that, “This decision has been reached after careful reflection on my political journey, personal convictions, aspirations, and my commitment to the people of Barten Local Government and Kwara State.



“I sincerely appreciate all APC leaders, members, friends, and associates with whom I have shared political experiences over the years.

“I hold no bitterness against anyone, and I remain grateful for the relationships and lessons gained during my time in the party.





“Having taken this decision, I am now fully prepared to join the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and continue my political engagement under its platform.

World.title: Inuwa Yahaya Takes Stock of NNGF Gains, Regional Body Charts Next Phase of Action
World.content:
*Lists security, infrastructure, economy

*Seeks stronger delivery mechanism to turn resolutions into measurable results

Segun Awofadeji in Gombe

Gombe State Governor and Chairman of the Northern Nigeria Governors Forum (NNGF), Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, weekend, said the North-East Governors’ Forum (NEGF), has recorded significant progress in regional cooperation since its establishment in 2020.

He said the collective action has already begun to yield concrete results across infrastructure, energy, connectivity and economic development.

For example, Yahaya noted the rehabilitation of strategic roads, renewed efforts on regional power and connectivity, the revival of the North-East Trade Fair and progress towards establishing a regional airline, among others.

He said the achievements reflected the value of the six states working together to address challenges that transcended individual state boundaries.

He spoke on Saturday in Maiduguri, Borno State, while delivering his opening remarks at the 13th meeting of the North-East Governors’ Forum.

He, however, challenged the Forum to build on the progress recorded by moving beyond policy resolutions and strengthening mechanisms that would ensure decisions translate into measurable outcomes for the people.

He said the Forum was established out of necessity, as challenges confronting the region, including insurgency, banditry, cross-border crime, infrastructure deficits, energy shortages and the humanitarian crisis could not be effectively addressed by individual states acting in isolation.

Six years and twelve meetings later, he said the NEGF had evolved into an institutional platform with a Secretariat, Technical Working Committee of the Secretaries to State Governments, Technical Working Group of experts and sectoral committees responsible for advancing decisions between meetings.

Yahaya said one of the clearest outcomes of the Forum’s collective advocacy was the joint presentation of 17 strategic road projects, the Port Harcourt-Jos-Bauchi-Maiduguri rail corridor and frontier oil exploration opportunities at Kolmani and the Lake Chad Basin to the Federal Government in September 2025.

He noted that the federal government subsequently flagged off the rehabilitation of the Dikwa-Gamboru Ngala and Bama-Banki roads, covering nearly 99 kilometres of strategic corridors critical to security, recovery and cross-border trade.

He added that the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri highway had also been adopted as a legacy road project of President Bola Tinubu.

On energy, Yahaya said the Forum had helped shift the conversation from isolated state-level concerns to a regional energy agenda, noting that the Dadinkowa Hydropower Plant was now feeding the national grid.

He said the new electricity law had also created opportunities for states to reform their electricity markets and expand renewable energy solutions, including solar power and mini-grids.

He further cited the revival of the North-East Trade Fair in Bauchi in 2024 as another example of a Forum resolution being translated into concrete action.

According to him, the region’s ability to pool resources had also been demonstrated through the N30 billion financing plan, with each of the six states contributing N5 billion, for the establishment of a North-East regional airline.

In his remarks, the host, Governor Babagana Umara Zulum of Borno State, commended the federal government for interventions supporting recovery and economic resilience in the North-East, particularly the One Billion Dollar Household Prosperity and Economic Social Protection Project (HOPE-SP).

He said the intervention was significant for a sub-region that had endured prolonged insecurity, displacement, disrupted livelihoods and humanitarian dependence, noting that it could help vulnerable households rebuild their livelihoods and become economically self-reliant.

Zulum stressed the need for a deliberate shift from relief to recovery and sustainable prosperity, with the return of displaced persons backed by access to housing, education, healthcare and economic opportunities.

He also acknowledged the considerable improvement in the security situation across the North-East, attributing the progress to the sacrifice of the Armed Forces and other security agencies, the resilience of the people and the commitment of governments at all levels.

World.title: ADC PCC Tackles Shettima Over Claim Tinubu Saved Nigeria from Collapse
World.content:
*Knocks APC over AK-47 threat, says party plotting violence ahead 2027

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has taken a swipe at Vice President Kashim Shettima’s claim that President Bola Tinubu saved Nigeria from economic collapse, arguing that the current administration could not disown the record of the All Progressives Congress (APC) government under former President Muhammadu Buhari.

The council said Shettima’s assertion that Nigeria was heading towards “Caracas” before Tinubu assumed office was an indictment of the Buhari administration, which, like the Tinubu government, was elected on the platform of the APC.

The reaction was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan.

Ologbondiyan said Shettima, in an attempt to defend what he described as the abysmal failures of the Tinubu administration, had resorted to rewriting the history of the APC.

He said if Nigeria was indeed heading towards economic collapse before Tinubu took office, as claimed by the Vice President, then the APC must accept responsibility for the situation because it controlled the Federal Government for eight years under Buhari.

“Vice President Shettima’s statement is self-indicting. If Nigeria was heading to Caracas under Buhari, it means Buhari and the APC deceived Nigerians for eight years.

“And if that is the case, why should Nigerians believe Tinubu, who is of the same APC stock and was a major promoter and defender of the Buhari administration?” Ologbondiyan queried.

He said the APC could not disown its own record, recalling that Tinubu had repeatedly defended the Buhari administration and assured Nigerians that his government would build on Buhari’s legacy.

According to him, the attempts by Tinubu and Shettima to distance the present administration from Buhari amount to an admission that the APC has failed Nigerians.

“But Nigerians do not know Buhari as an individual; Nigerians know APC. It is the APC, on whose platform President Tinubu is seeking a second term, that has failed Nigerians for almost 12 years and is undeserving of another four years,” he said.

Ologbondiyan accused the APC government of failing across several sectors, citing the state of roads, electricity, public institutions and the rising cost of living.

He said the immediate concern of Nigerians was not political propaganda but access to affordable food and basic necessities.

“Our roads are no longer motorable, there is no electricity, our institutions have collapsed. But what concerns ordinary Nigerians today is food, food and food, not baseless propaganda.

“President Tinubu has not saved Nigeria from collapse; he has pushed the country deeper into economic ruin, marked by unprecedented hunger, hyperinflation, naira devaluation, insecurity, mass unemployment and excruciating cost of living,” he said.

The ADC campaign council spokesman further argued that Nigerians were already experiencing what Shettima described as the “Caracas” scenario, not merely heading towards it.

“Nigerians are not heading to Caracas; under the APC, Nigerians are already living the Caracas experience in their own country,” Ologbondiyan said.

He also faulted Shettima’s promise to deploy 10,600 electric tricycles, 300 buses and electric taxis under an e-logistics programme “in the coming weeks”, describing it as another promise that Nigerians should treat with caution.

Ologbondiyan reminded the Vice President of the administration’s earlier promise that transportation costs would come down by October 1, 2026, asking Nigerians to judge the government by its delivery rather than fresh promises.

The ADC-PCC urged Shettima and the APC to stop what it described as attempts to insult the sensibilities of Nigerians through revisionist narratives and instead acknowledge the challenges confronting the country.

The council also assured Nigerians that the ADC remained committed to providing what it described as a credible political alternative capable of rescuing the country from APC rule.

Ologbondiyan therefore called on Nigerians to unite behind the quest for a government that would make life more affordable and restore economic security and confidence in the country.

ADC PCC Knocks APC over AK-47 Threat, Says Party Plotting Violence Ahead of 2027

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), has condemned the threat by the Edo State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Jarrett Tenebe, to deploy AK-47 rifles against anyone who attempts to deny the party the 2.5 million votes it has promised President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

The ADC-PCC also condemned the reported attack on members of the ADC and destruction of vehicles belonging to party supporters at Gegu in Koton Karfi Local Government Area of Kogi State.

The council described the alleged threat and the Kogi incident as acts of intimidation and political violence capable of undermining the 2027 general elections.

The Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, stated this in a statement yesterday.

Ologbondiyan said Tenebe’s alleged plot was “inciting” and “terroristic,” arguing that it amounted to an attempt to intimidate voters and create an atmosphere of fear ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said the council had waited for the APC leadership and President Tinubu to condemn or demand a retraction of the statement but received no such response.

“We are shocked that a state chairman of a ruling party, Mr. Jarrett Tenebe, can stand before the public and threaten Nigerians with AK-47 rifles if they refuse to vote for his party, the APC.

“This is terrorism, and not politics. This is the height of desperation by a party that has failed Nigerians woefully,” Ologbondiyan said.

He further alleged that since President Tinubu’s reported statement that “all is fair in politics,” some APC members had increasingly resorted to intimidation, harassment and violations of the law.

Ologbondiyan argued that the APC could not legitimately secure 2.5 million votes in Edo State through a free, fair and credible electoral process, describing Edo voters as politically sophisticated and increasingly dissatisfied with what he called the hardship and insecurity under the APC administration.

He said the threat to use AK-47 rifles against voters was a violation of the Electoral Act and the Constitution and should be investigated by the relevant authorities.

According to him, the alleged statement had further reinforced concerns that the APC might resort to violence and intimidation in its bid to retain power in 2027.

World.title: Nwifuru Charges NYSC Members on Skills Acquisition, Entrepreneurship Development
World.content:
*HURIWA demands rescue of abducted corps members

Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki

Ebonyi State Governor, Chief Francis Nwifuru, has charged Corps Members to take full advantage of the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development programme of the NYSC, as tools that would make them self-reliant, create employment and contribute meaningfully to the economy.

This was as the Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA), has demanded the immediate and safe rescue of the 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other travellers abducted in Imo State.

It urged the federal government to deploy every available intelligence, security asset and specialist capability to secure their release.

Nwifuru stated this during the swearing in of the 2026 NYSC Batch ‘C’ Stream 1 Corps Members held at NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Afikpo in the state.

The governor said his administration remained committed to building a state where development creates opportunities, infrastructure supports economic activity and young people are equipped with the skills required to compete in a changing world.

“We are also creating an environment that supports enterprise, investment and skills development. The establishment of the National Automotive Design and Development Council Automotive Training Centre in Abakaliki is another step towards equipping our young people with practical skills and connecting them to emerging opportunities in the automotive and technical sectors.

“We are equally investing in agriculture and human capital development because we believe that the future of Ebonyi depends largely on the capacity of our young people to create value and build sustainable livelihoods.

“My dear Corps Members, opportunities are not always found by waiting for employment. Sometimes, opportunities are created through skills, innovation, enterprise and the courage to solve problems.

“I therefore encourage you to take full advantage of the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development programme of the NYSC. Do not regard the skills you acquire during this service year as merely another requirement for passing out. See them as tools that can help you become self-reliant, create employment and contribute meaningfully to the economy.”

Harping on the theme of the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Orientation Course, “Reimagining the NYSC Orientation Course: Building Resilient, Responsible and Service-Oriented Corps Members for a Changing World,” Ebonyi state Coordinator of NYSC, Mrs Malgwi Pat. Maidariya emphasised the need to equip Corps Members with the values, knowledge and practical skills required to respond effectively to contemporary challenges and contribute meaningfully to nation-building.

“The theme also aligns with the development agenda of the Ebonyi State Government, particularly its emphasis on human capital development, youth empowerment, skills acquisition, entrepreneurship, responsible citizenship and inclusive development,” she said.

HURIWA Demands Rescue of Abducted Corps Members

In another development, HURIWA, has demanded the immediate and safe rescue of the 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other travellers abducted in Imo State.

It, therefore, urged the federal government to deploy every available intelligence, security asset and specialist capability to secure their release.





HURIWA said the reported discovery of the kidnappers’ forest hideout, coupled with the revelation that the camp has been surrounded by improvised explosive devices, made the rescue operation an urgent national security priority.





In a statement by the National Coordinator of the group, Emmanuel Onwubiko, the association demanded that security agencies must not allow the mined forest terrain to become an excuse for prolonged delay in rescuing the victims.

HURIWA called on the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigerian Army, the Department of State Services and the Nigerian Air Force to establish a unified rescue command and deploy specialised personnel trained in hostage rescue, explosive ordnance disposal, intelligence gathering and jungle operations.

World.title: DRAINING THE POOR TO FEED THE RICH
World.content:
What policymakers consider economic reform translates into real hardship for many in the country, contends MAJORITY OJI

Government officials in Nigeria are actively engaged in driving progress. Across federal, state, and local levels, the focus remains on ongoing development, with officials asserting that they are diligently working to advance the economy and improve the nation. From the government’s perspective, there should be adequate food supplies, better road infrastructure, and other developments that facilitate a more comfortable life for Nigerians. In this context, the government claims that the Nigerian economy is on the path to recovery, representing its chosen benchmark for accountability.

There is no doubt that the government is taking steps to address issues, a fact acknowledged by the World Bank. Together, they justify the need to eliminate the ‘costly fuel subsidy’. While Nigeria indeed faces significant fiscal challenges, the government argues that unsustainable exchange rate distortions must end. They claim the reforms aim to restore economic stability. Officially, they state that inflation is starting to stabilize and that economic growth is trending upward, even though measuring the real impact of these changes on the daily lives of ordinary Nigerians remains a significant challenge.

Let’s take a closer look at this issue from the standpoint of the average Nigerian, the common man who faces the daily challenges posed by the nation’s current economic situation. The government’s claims of success clash strikingly with the reality of an economy that has taken a significant downturn, leaving countless people grappling with uncertainty. The much-touted recovery often feels like an added burden rather than a relief. For ordinary Nigerians, these reforms are more than just abstract economic adjustments discussed in government meetings. They show up at the dinner table through rising household expenses, diminishing purchasing power, increasing financial strain, and a growing struggle to meet basic needs. What policymakers consider economic reform translates into real hardship for many in our communities.

This dissonance is why Nigerians are increasingly pressing for clear answers regarding the removal of the fuel subsidy. They are eager to understand who actually benefits from this policy and, equally important, who bears its immediate and disproportionate costs. It is entirely reasonable for citizens to expect the government to look beyond mere calculations of fiscal savings and address the broader economic and social implications of such policies for the people they affect.

The central issue revolves around accountability. If the government has saved significant financial resources by removing the fuel subsidy, where exactly are those savings being allocated? What happens to the funds that were spent on the subsidy? How much of that actually benefits the Nigerian people through improved public services, better infrastructure, effective social intervention programmes, or direct financial assistance? It is not enough for the government to claim substantial savings; Nigerians deserve transparency regarding how these savings are being used, their effectiveness, and, most importantly, what real improvements they bring to the lives of citizens who have borne the immediate impacts of this reform.

Many Nigerians are yet to feel the relief promised by the government’s reforms. Instead, they are confronted with a relentless proliferation of costs, as corporations and service providers erect towering ‘cost skyscrapers’ above them. Ironically, every additional layer of cost imposed by profiteering and rent-seeking interests places a further burden on already strained households. Take, for instance, the government’s increasing taxes and levies. The channels through which direct and indirect taxation hits citizens keep expanding. The stark truth is that Nigerian consumers now shoulder a heavy tax burden at almost every transaction, every purchase, and every instance of consumption. What was marketed as economic relief often feels like just another layer of financial pressure for many households.

In light of this situation, the government’s ability to address the financial crisis it has created seems questionable. Rather than providing credible explanations, the administration has resorted to flip-flopping and denying the evident difficulties. By refusing to acknowledge its economic missteps, it continues to declare success, while millions of citizens wrestle with deepening poverty.

Continuing with the cost skyscraper metaphor, let’s examine the next layer: fuel. The government’s transition from subsidizing petrol to requiring consumers and businesses to pay market rates has had a dramatic effect on the Nigerian economy. Before the May 2023 reform, the government absorbed a significant portion of the gap between import costs and regulated pump prices. However, after the fuel subsidy was eliminated, petrol prices soared overnight from around ₦190 to over ₦500 per litre. For households and businesses already grappling with rising expenses, this was not just a price change; it was another substantial floor added to the already towering cost skyscraper, escalating the costs of transportation, production, distribution, and, ultimately, the basics of daily life.

Since then, fuel prices have remained unpredictable, akin to an aircraft struggling with faulty engines. Currently, Nigerians are facing petrol costs around ₦1,500 per litre. Many may not realize that these elevated prices act as an unrecognized tax on transportation, mobility, manufacturing, and commerce, despite not being categorized as official taxes. This prompts important questions: Was petrol genuinely more affordable for the average person during the subsidy era? And considering wages, purchasing power, and inflation, has the removal of the fuel subsidy improved Nigeria’s fiscal situation enough to offset the significant decline in household purchasing power?

Electricity supply constitutes yet another layer in the cost skyscraper metaphor, imposing a heavy burden on both households and businesses. Traditionally, the government subsidized electricity by bridging the gap between generation costs and what consumers paid. However, with deregulation came the privatization of distribution companies (DisCos) aimed at creating a self-sustaining and efficient market. Now, consumers are facing much higher rates, yet they must question: have these increased costs been accompanied by noticeable improvements in electricity supply, reliability, and service quality? Is the increased cost affordable by Nigerians? If not, the added financial strain on households and businesses warrants immediate attention.

The reality is that the challenges faced by Nigerian electricity consumers post-deregulation extend well beyond steeper tariffs. For a developing nation like Nigeria, the key takeaway is evident: moving towards market-based electricity pricing without first securing adequate power generation, effective regulation, modern infrastructure, sufficient investment, and strong protections for vulnerable consumers can lead to dire consequences. Consumers may find themselves paying significantly higher market rates while still grappling with unreliable and low-quality electricity services. This really sums up the tough situation confronting electricity consumers throughout Nigeria.

It is no secret that high electricity tariffs, unscrupulous operators, and an unstable power supply have significantly hindered Nigeria’s economic growth and national development. Yet, it seems that the financial strategists within the government have underestimated the crucial role electricity plays in developing nations. This issue goes beyond merely ensuring homes have power; electricity is a cornerstone of national progress. For Nigeria to achieve lasting economic growth, it must provide affordable, reliable, and sufficient electricity to meet the demands of its expanding population and business sectors. A stable power supply is vital for industrial growth, quality education, healthcare, modern agriculture, job creation, technological advancement, and attracting both domestic and foreign investments. Access to reliable and affordable electricity is not a luxury; it is essential for boosting productivity, enhancing economic competitiveness, and improving the living standards of Nigerians.

To secure the country’s economic future, it is imperative to focus on expanding, modernizing, and fortifying Nigeria’s electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and renewable energy infrastructure. The government must act decisively to keep electricity affordable for both businesses and households. If not, businesses may face significant financial pressure, forcing them to raise prices for consumers who are already dealing with rising living costs. In light of this, is the government truly on the right path by trying to relieve the financial burdens faced by electricity distribution companies (DisCos)? Do the facts and evidence support the DisCos’ claims for ongoing government assistance? More importantly, do their financial situations, operational effectiveness, and cost structures warrant the extent of public funding they are seeking?

Government’s persistent presentation of unsettling statistics highlighting the significant financial strain of subsidizing an already privatized electricity sector becomes wearisome. According to the Ministry of Finance, the Federal Government incurred ₦3.14 trillion in electricity subsidy costs from June 2023 to December 2025, supposedly to protect consumers from escalating electricity tariffs. Yet, the irony is glaring: both consumers and businesses are expressing frustration over arbitrary charges imposed by electricity distribution companies.

Current government policy seems to prioritize shielding private power companies from accountability rather than protecting consumers. By funneling billions in public funds to companies accused of unfair billing practices, we find ourselves in a situation where citizens pay twice: first through inflated electricity tariffs and then again through taxpayer-funded subsidies. Instead of fixing the structural issues, this approach risks socializing the costs of private enterprises while leaving the profits in their hands. Ultimately, public funds are being utilized to shield operators from the necessary regulatory oversight.

Oji is a Professor of Mass Communication, Delta State University, Abraka

World.title: Moniepoint CEO Named among World’s Rising Stars
World.content:
Emma Okonji

Co-founder and Group Chief Executive Officer of Moniepoint Inc, Tosin Eniolorunda, has been named to the 2026 TIME100 Next, TIME’s annual list recognising 100 of the world’s most influential rising stars shaping the next generation of leadership across industries.

He joins emerging leaders from business, technology, politics, science, sport and culture, whom TIME described as shaping the future.

The only African among the business, technology and AI leaders on this year’s list, Eniolorunda’s inclusion recognises his role in building financial infrastructure that has helped expand access to financial services across Nigeria.

Founded in 2015 and a unicorn since 2024, Moniepoint has grown to serve more than 20 million businesses and individuals, powering about eight in every ten in-person digital payment transactions in Nigeria with an agency banking network spanning all 774 local government areas. Its blue POS terminal has become a familiar fixture of everyday commerce across the country.

According to TIME Chief Executive Officer Jessica Sibley, “This year’s listmakers are pushing boundaries, creating new possibilities, and advancing their fields and communities around the world. The list is the outcome of a long and deliberate editorial process which TIME is famed for.”

World.title: [Watch] Cape baboons launch ruthless attack on tourists
World.content:
Two viral Cape baboon attacks were caught on camera. Images via TikTok

Two viral videos of Cape Peninsula baboons attacking visitors have gone viral on social media.

This comes amid outrage by animal activists over the increase in deaths of the animals, believed to be “hunted” by members of the public. Others have been lethally removed under a controversial official baboon-management translocation guideline.

WATCH: CAPE PENINSULA BABOONS ATTACK!

On her TikTok account, a German female student living in Cape Town posted a video of a Cape Peninsula baboon attacking her.



In the clip, the animal lunges at her, stealing her handbag containing various food snacks.

“Going to the beach in Cape Town. But the saxophones are getting louder”, she captioned the post.

In another viral video, a baboon was seen attacking another female, who quickly escaped into her nearby car.



TRANSLOCATION BACKLASH, DEATHS

Last year, the Cape Peninsula Baboon Management Joint Task Team (CPBMJTT), comprising representatives from South African National Parks, Cape Nature, and the City of Cape Town, issued a controversial proposal to translocate the baboon population, whose numbers have exceeded available management resources.

The group outlined plans for baboon troops to be captured and relocated to a newly established sanctuary on the peninsula as soon as February.

The animals will be enclosed by a “baboon-proof” fence line, patrolled by rangers to prevent the baboons from accessing urban areas and farmland.



Euthanasia was described as a last resort.

The plan has received backlash from animal activists.

In recent months, activists have also expressed concern at the deaths of several baboons, believed to have been “hunted” by members of the public.

World.title: Anele Mdoda claps back at ‘racist’ label: ‘Let’s move on’
World.content:
Anele Mdoda claps back at claims she is 'racist'. Images via X

Anele Mdoda has clapped back at trolls who labelled her “racist”. This comes amid a call from rugby fans to boycott the 947 presenter’s breakfast show following her comments about Springbok Andre Esterhuizen.

The media personality called for the Bok to receive a rugby ban amid reports of his alleged K-word racial attack in 2012.

ANELE MDODA CLAPS BACK AT ‘RACIST’ CLAIMS

On her X account, Anele Mdoda claimed back at trolls who labelled her “racist” over her Andre Esterhuizen comments last month.



When one claimed that she “hates white culture”, Anele responded: “If you are going to be full of insults, you are going to have to be well read.

Another troll called her an “inferior hateful black”, to which she clapped back with a quote that read: “Baby, they’re stupid. Now let’s move on”.

‘HE DID USE THAT WORD’

Over the past few days, Anele Mdoda’s name has been trending on social media after she publicly condemned Andre Esterhuizen’s alleged K-word racial slur.



The media personality had responded to a media clipping from 2012, when the Springbok was just 18 years old. Anele tweeted: “He should be banned from playing rugby period!”

Her views were met with backlash, with rugby fans calling for a boycott of Anele’s 947 breakfast show.

The 42-year-old clapped back at one critic on her X account, posting: “You need to be very careful with the media storm you are calling towards Andre here. 

She added: “It won’t end well cause he did use that word”

Anele added that she had been inundated with verbal attacks from the “hyenas on Facebook”.

World.title: RIP Dewald Naude: Cause of death revealed
World.content:
Dewald Naude cause of death has been revealed. Images via Facebook

Paarl Boys High Old Boy Donald Dewald Naude – who played for the Bulls under 21 side and Tuks rugby squad that lifted the Varsity Cup – died on Saturday, 3 October after a battle with brain cancer.

The 31-year-old player was diagnosed with a brain tumour earlier this year at his club at the HBU Sandy Bay in Hong Kong.

He leaves behind a wife, Annabel.



DEWALD NAUDE DIES AFTER BATTLE WITH BRAIN CANCER

In a statement, HBU Sandy Bay confirmed Dewald Naude had died on Saturday, 3 October, after a battle with brain cancer.

The Hong Kong club paid tribute to the South African player, sharing: “Those who knew him will remember how effortlessly he could put a smile on somebody else’s face and make them forget their worries.

“He had a genuine heart for serving others, and even during the most difficult period of his own life, Donald continued to put those around him first.

“Through all of it, he faced his illness with extraordinary courage, carrying the same optimism and positivity he always had. It never changed the person we knew and loved”

Dewald Naude’s loved ones appealed for public donations earlier this year after he was diagnosed with a brain tumour.

In the time that passed, Dewald underwent an 8.5-hour “awake” craniotomy operation to resection the tumour.



WIDOW: ‘SO PROUD OF YOUR BRAVERY AND STRENGTH’

In an Instagram post, Dewald Naude’s wife, Annabel, shared a touching tribute.

She shared: “What a privilege and honour it has been to be your wife and soulmate. I have been blessed with the best husband. You have taught me to always have courage, determination, perseverance, strength, and, most of all, self-belief.

“Through your bravery, I have learnt to remain positive even through the darkest of times. Thank you for always making me feel loved and for being my calm. I am so proud of your bravery and strength”.

Dewald Naude’s final Instagram post was dedicated to his wife on her birthday in August

“I’m truly blessed & grateful to have you in my life”, he shared.

World.title: Ramaphosa’s ankole bags record R6,4 MILLION at auction
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa has sold the most expensive Ankole in South Africa. Images via X

A pregnant Ankole cow named Queen Arusha was auctioned off for a whopping R6,4 million, becoming the most expensive cow of any breed sold in South Africa. The heifer was sold by Ntaba Nyoni Ankole, a cattle breeding company owned by President Cyril Ramaphosa.

The farm is located at his Phala Phala farm, near Bela-Bela, in Limpopo.

The president is believed to own more than 100 of the unique breed, which is indigenous to African countries such as Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and parts of Tanzania.



CYRIL RAMAPHOSA BAGS R6.4M FROM RECORD ANKOLE SALE

On Saturday, 3 October, Cyril Ramaphosa’s Ntaba Nyoni Ankole company netted a record-breaking sale at an auction at his Phala Phala farm.

A female heifer, Queen Arusha, sold for a whopping R6,4 million to an anonymous buyer. The Ankole was born in 2023 and is already in calf.

The sale reportedly set a South African record for a female animal across all cattle breeds, not just Ankole.

It’s not the first time the president has netted a small fortune for his pedigree cattle.

In 2022, his Ankole heifer, Fafa, was sold at auction for R2.1 million to businessman Patrice Motsepe, his brother-in-law.

In 2024, another pregnant heifer, Khethiwe, was sold for R1.8m at his auction.



WHY IS QUEEN ARUSHA SO EXPENSIVE?

Queen Arusha is a stud female, making her valuable primarily as a breeding animal and for her elite genetics.

Her R6,4 million price tag is attributed to the following:

Genetically valuable

Queen Arusha comes from a highly sought-after Ankole bloodline. She is the full sister of Optimus Prime, an Ankole bull whose horns measure about 68 inches. During the auction on Saturday, President Ramaphosa’s Ntaba Nyoni Ankole company bought two vials of Optimus Prime’s semen for R250 000 each.

Pregnant, and breeding potential

As a stud female, Queen Arusha has an enormous breeding potential through producing calves and embryos. Her genetics can potentially be multiplied through artificial insemination and embryo transfer.

The Ankole is also an in-calf heifer, meaning she is pregnant with her first calf.

Ankole is a niche market in South Africa.

According to the Ankole Cattle Breeders’ Society, there were only about 1,792 registered Ankole cattle, of which 1,198 were Fullblood, in its 2025 figures.

Hardy breed

Ankole – known for their long horns – produce lean meat, rich milk, and quality leather. Their horns are also considered a hot commodity. The breed is known to be “hardy cattle” and can live up to 30 years, relying on limited food and water.

AN AVID ANKOLE FARMER

In 2004, Cyril Ramaphosa—then an astute businessman—bought 43 Ankole cattle from Uganda, but they had to be brought into South Africa via artificial insemination.

The embryos of the cows were implanted in surrogate cows.

In his 2017 coffee table book, Cattle of the Ages, Ramaphosa described his fascination with the breed.

He said, “They each had long, white, beautiful horns glinting in the African sun. I suddenly became fixated and couldn’t stop looking at them. I was intrigued and in awe and fell in love with these creatures immediately”.

He now owns more than 750 elite cattle, including breeds such as Bonsmara, Boran, Nguni, and Wagyu.
