World.title: Cape Town areas to experience 11-hour water shutdown
World.content:
The City of Cape Town has confirmed that some areas will experience a 10-hour water shutdown on Wednesday,

The Water and Sanitation Directorate said the planned maintenance forms part of ongoing efforts to upgrade critical infrastructure and improve water supply across the city.

CAPE TOWN AREAS SET TO EXPERIENCE WATER SUPPLY DISRUPTION

The City of Cape Town said planned maintenance work, including pipe and valve installations, repairs, and replacements, will result in water supply disruption to these areas:



Part of Grassy Park – The water supply to Dieman Road, Iris Road and possibly surrounding streets in Grassy Park will be shut off temporarily on Wednesday, 7 October 2026, from 08:00 until 19:00. This will allow the maintenance teams to safely connect the newly installed pipelines to the existing water supply infrastructure in the area.

“These streets and possibly surrounding streets will experience no water during this period,” the municipality said.

Parts of Woodstock – The City of Cape Town will start with the pipe replacement project that will affect the water supply intermittently to parts of Woodstock from Monday, 5 October 2026 until Friday, 30 April 2027.

The metro municipality said this will result in the water being shut off in Ravenscraig Road, Woodlands Road, Pine Road, Queens Road, Beyers Road, Warwick Street, Salmon Street, Coventry Road, Duke Road, Park Road, High Street, and possibly surrounding streets in Woodstock temporarily from 08:00 until 17:00 daily.

“This will allow the maintenance team to safely carry out the pipe and valve replacement in the area using trenchless technology, which is less of an inconvenience to residents and motorists. These streets and possibly surrounding streets will experience no water during this period and will be notified in advance when they will be affected,” the municipality said.

Parts of Strand – Similarly, the City of Cape Town will shut off the water supply to parts of Broadlands Road, from the vicinity of the Strandfoam Group (Pty) Ltd to the N2, Lwandle Helderberg Industrial and possibly surrounding streets in Strand temporarily on Wednesday, 7 October 2026, from 09:00 until 18:00. This will allow the maintenance team to safely carry out a new connection to the 300mm-diameter water main in the area. These areas and possibly surrounding streets will experience no water during this period.



ZERO-PRESSURE TESTS

Additionally, the City of Cape Town said it will conduct zero-pressure tests (ZPT) and conditional assessments on the water supply network, resulting in water supply disruptions in the following areas:

Wednesday, 7 October 2026, 09:00 to 16:00: Martinville – Bizweni.

Martinville – Bizweni. Thursday, 8 October 2026, 09:00 to 16:00: Helderzicht, Lourensia Park, Paardevlei, Victoria Park, Silvertas, Garden Village and Carey Park.

Helderzicht, Lourensia Park, Paardevlei, Victoria Park, Silvertas, Garden Village and Carey Park. Thursday, 8 October 2026, 09:00 to 16:00: Da Gama Park, Welcome Glen and Scala Road.

Residents have been advised to store water in advance as a precautionary measure in clean, sealed containers for domestic use during this period.

World.title: ‘Heist of the century’: Fans react to Orlando Pirates’ R20.2m court bid
World.content:
Orlando Pirates supporters have reacted after the club launched an urgent court application to freeze R20.2 million allegedly diverted from its accounts.

The matter was filed in the Johannesburg High Court, with the funds reportedly linked to hundreds of unauthorised transactions allegedly involving former finance manager Darryl Joselowsky.

According to reports by Sowetan, Pirates is seeking to freeze four bank accounts allegedly linked to Joselowsky, which have a combined balance of R20.2 million.



The club is also seeking further information from Standard Bank to establish where the money went and who ultimately benefited from the transactions.

Orlando Pirates, however, stressed that the court application does not constitute a finding of wrongdoing.

“The application is not a finding of wrongdoing and should not be interpreted as one. The individual concerned is cooperating, and the Club is committed to a fair process for everyone involved,” the club said in a statement.

The allegations have sparked plenty of reaction among football supporters on social media, with some questioning how a club of Pirates’ stature could allegedly lose such a substantial amount of money through unauthorised transactions.

Fans react to Orlando Pirates ‘losing millions’

@SpholaM6 wrote: “For such a big institution to have these weak internal controls when it comes to its banking process is shocking…”

@Deeflowwd4 added: “They were busy swearing at Pitso and Modiba while a heist of the century was in place.”



Meanwhile, @SundownsOGs joked: “Darryl Joselowsky won’t see heaven. So the whole Betway Premiership prize money is gone.”

“He is very brave. Pickpocketing the Iron Duke?” tweeted @S_Gwiliza.

Orlando Pirates are in action this coming weekend against Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final.

What’s your take?

World.title: IFP leader calls for no bail and life sentences for convicted rapists
World.content:
Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) leader Velenkosini Hlabisa says people accused of rape should not be granted bail and those found guilty should receive life sentences without parole.

Hlabisa made the remarks while addressing party members at the Greyville Racecourse in Durban on Sunday, 4 October, where the party launched its eThekwini manifesto.

IFP CALLS FOR TOUGHER ACTION AGAINST RAPE

During his address, Hlabisa urged men to join the fight against gender-based violence (GBV) and femicide, emphasising their responsibility to protect women and children.



“Once you are arrested on a case of rape, the person must not be given bail until the case is finalised. When found guilty, the person must be given a life sentence without parole because rapists and murderers are monsters in our society who must be removed once and for all,” said Hlabisa.

Hlabisa’s comments come amid continued concerns about GBV and femicide in South Africa, with political parties calling for stronger action against perpetrators.

SIBIYA FACES RAPE AND OTHER CHARGES

IFP leader Velenkosini Hlabisa’s remarks also come as suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Shadrack Sibiya faces six charges, including rape, sexual grooming of a minor, human trafficking and negligent handling of a firearm.



Sibiya is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman and sexually grooming a 16-year-old girl. He has denied the allegations, telling the Randburg Magistrates’ Court that his sexual encounter with the 18-year-old was consensual.

His bail application is ongoing, with the state opposing his release. The matter was postponed to 7 October.

World.title: 'Deal with drugs and gangsterism' - DA grilled on Cape Town crime
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Crime, homelessness and the rising cost of living are putting Cape Town communities under pressure.

This has now seen residents demanding more than just increased policing.

Law student and independent candidate Thaafir Mustapha said crime cannot be separated from the economic hardship facing communities.

“It would be short-sighted to think about crime without thinking about the cost of living. Ultimately, it's one bad bill that separates you from a homeless person or someone desperate enough to commit a crime," he said

Mustapha spoke at eNCA’s WeTheNation election debate held at the University of the Western Cape on Sunday.

Another attendee challenged the DA over its approach to crime and what it had done since taking over from the ANC in 2006.

READ | WATCH | Cape Town’s ‘well-run’ image challenged over inequality

He criticised the party for focusing heavily on law enforcement while failing to address drugs and gangsterism.

“You are saying that more boots on the ground [are needed], but you are not bringing any facilities to deal with the issues that are affecting our communities,” he said.

The Democratic Alliance's Carl Pophaim said the party has “pushed the boundary” in the city, spending more than R8 billion on municipal security over the last five years.

This included deploying “more than 1,300 new metro police officers, while SAPS has decreased.”

He conceded that more needed to be done.

World.title: A ‘city good to the elite’ - Cape Town's spatial inequality scrutinised
World.content:
“The city is good to the elite. It is not good to the poor and the oppressed.”

These were the words of the Economic Freedom Fighters’ Carl Niehaus in his assessment of Cape Town as political parties and residents clashed over whether enough is being done to undo decades of spatial inequality.

Niehaus was addressing eNCA’s WeTheNation election debate at the University of the Western Cape on Sunday.

He used Dunoon, a township in Cape Town, to explain that thousands of residents live in squalor despite promises of affordable housing.

READ | WATCH | Cape Town’s ‘well-run’ image challenged over inequality

But the governing Democratic Alliance argued they were not trying to claim they had undone decades of apartheid spatial planning and injustice.

Carl Pophaim contended that efforts to address the legacy problem were there.

He pointed to the expansion of the MyCiTi network and the building of affordable accommodation in the inner city.

A student who was part of the gathering hit back at the DA’s assertions.

READ | 'Our City has a lot of actors,' ACDP calls for stability in NMB

“Saying that you are going to give us MyCiTi pass - you are not solving spatial inequality. In fact, you are reinforcing it because spatial inequality is deeply entrenched in the land. You are not doing anything to fix it,” he explained.

The Good Party's Brett Herron echoed similar sentiments.

World.title: WATCH | Cape Town’s ‘well-run’ image challenged over inequality
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Civil society group Budget Justice Coalition has laid bare the reality of inequality in the City of Cape Town.

According to Sibabalwa Nobandla, while political parties continue to boast about Cape Town being “well-run”, the city remains a “tale of two cities”, with inequality still largely unaddressed.

This as he pointed to the housing backlog as one example.

Nobandla was speaking at this week's #WeTheNation election edition, held at the University of the Western Cape on Sunday.

“It's quite disappointing that I don't think most of the political parties have addressed how they would tackle the growing inequality in Cape Town,” he said.

Taking on the question, National Coloured Congress's Larry Varrie argued that those in power continue to benefit while ordinary people suffer.

He shifted the focus to Cape Town’s coloured community, arguing that it remains marginalised despite making up a significant proportion of the city’s population.

“The point is that housing is being built. All these promises that people are making are promises that our people have been hearing for many years. But is there political will for those who are in power to achieve those things? There is no political will,” he said.

Democratic Alliance's Carl Pophaim, however had a different view.

He questioned how inequality could be addressed if a political party focused primarily on one racial group.

World.title: Woman found dead near University of Limpopo campus fence
World.content:
SOVENGA – A partially dressed young woman has been found dead outside the University of Limpopo’s fence.

Police in Mankweng have opened an inquest docket following the discovery of the body of a 22-year-old female along Sovenga Street.

Officers were patrolling when they were informed of the discovery.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Hlulani Mashaba said the woman’s head was positioned inside a trench adjacent to the fence.

“The body was inspected and no visible external injuries were observed at the scene. A bag containing the deceased's identity document and NSFAS card was found next to the body.

“Members of the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) were summoned and declared the 22-year-old female dead upon arrival at the scene.

“It is suspected that the deceased may have accidentally fallen into the trench and the exact circumstances surrounding her death are under investigation,” Mashaba said.

The identity of the deceased will be revealed once her family has been notified.

Police have opened an inquest and investigations are continuing.

World.title: A war of words as Lamola and Bozell tensions continue
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - There’s no thaw in the frosty ties between South Africa and the United States.

If anything, relations have hit a new low.

And the diplomatic cold front is only intensifying.

Earlier on Sunday, US Ambassador Leo Bozell accused International Relations Minister Ronald Lamola of personally insulting him.

Bozell's accusation comes via a post on the social media platform X.

He was responding to a Sunday Times article quoting Lamola saying 'if Bozell is tired of talking, he should get out of the kitchen'.

In the same article, Lamola also accused Bozell of undiplomatic conduct.

All this unfolds just days after Lamola’s office confirmed issuing Bozell his third demarche since taking up the post earlier this year.

A demarche is diplomatic-speak for a formal slap on the wrist, short of kicking an ambassador out.

How Pretoria responds to Bozell’s latest jab remains to be seen.

World.title: Nine arrested for illegal mining
World.content:
MASHOBODO - Nine Mozambican nationals have been arrested in Mashobodo, Mpumalanga, for alleged illegal mining.

The arrests were made under Operation Vala Umgodi, as police intensify efforts to crack down on illegal mining across the country. A multidisciplinary unit acted on intelligence before making the arrests.

Police also recovered mining equipment and chemicals suspected to have been used to process gold-bearing material.

World.title: Attacks on JMPD officers a concern - metro police
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Seven off-duty JMPD officers have been attacked and four killed since last June.

The metro police’s Xolani Fihla said one of the latest shootings looks like a hit.

The motive for the attacks is baffling the department, since JMPD officers do not investigate criminal cases.

It's now trying to establish whether these attacks are personal or part of the wider violence gripping Johannesburg.

“Only this past week we saw three of our officers who were violently attacked. It has been happening for the past year. I know that from last year, let's say from June up until where we are right now, we've lost approximately four other officers due to violent attacks as well and those officers of course were also off duty as well.

“So it is a deep concern and not only just because it is JMPD officers, but a deep concern of the violent acts that we do see. One particular incident was definitely concerning because it did look like a hit because the officer had just knocked off, was still in his uniform and went to see the significant other and the officer was shot but his firearm wasn't taken.

“So it is something that we definitely have to look into whether it is either private affairs between the officers or just general violence within the city

World.title: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war
World.content:
TERHAN - Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

The main point of contention remains Iran's attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.

"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.

"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.

Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.

The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.

On Sunday, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz "reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room", though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.

The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel's origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.

- Focused on Hormuz -

Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.

Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.

Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being "in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues".

"We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz," he said, adding that reopening the waterway required "an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions".

The United States and Israel have characterised the war as being necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, a goal it has long denied pursuing, though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.

The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region.

US media outlet Axios reported that Washington has deployed additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to help protect key energy facilities from possible Iranian retaliation.

It also reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group were heading to the Middle East, where they could join two other US carrier strike groups already in the region.

Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

By Sébastien Ricci

World.title: End of long wait as Linda Mwananchi gets Sifuna's 2027 vehicle
World.content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, George Natembeya, James Orengo, Bonnie Khalwale during the launch of The Equitable Party on October 4, 2026. [Edward Kiplimo, Standard]

Linda Mwananchi has finally found a political home for its 2027 presidential bid, taking over the leadership of The Equitable Party, a party registered in 2022, with Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna unveiled as its leader and presidential candidate.

The development ends months of uncertainty over the political vehicle for the movement, which has been seeking to transform its growing political presence into a formal party structure ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Egypt records official decline in number of cancer victims
World.content:
Egypt has achieved a significant healthcare milestone following the announcement by GLOBOCAN—a platform under the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC/WHO)—of an official decline in incidence and mortality rates for several of the most prevalent types of cancer.

Liver, bladder, and breast cancers were the top three cancers which saw noticeable declines.

This reflects the advancement of Egypt’s healthcare system and the state’s efforts in prevention, early detection, and treatment.

The latest IARC estimates revealed a marked improvement in cancer control indicators in Egypt between 2022 and 2024.

This progress was driven by the implementation of national health initiatives—particularly the “100 Million Healthy Lives” campaign—alongside the expansion of screening and early detection programs and the updating of treatment protocols, all of which directly contributed to lowering incidence and mortality rates.

The data showed a 23.5 percent drop in the standardized cancer mortality rate in Egypt, alongside a 17.2 percent decline in the standardized incidence rate, over the course of just two years.

The number of new cancer cases fell from 150,600 to 137,400, while the number of deaths dropped from 95,300 to 80,500—despite a 9.8 percent population increase during the same period. This reflects a clear improvement in the effectiveness of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment programs.

Liver cancer showed the most significant improvement among cancer types; associated deaths declined by 22.1 percent and incidence rates fell by 16.7 percent.

Health authorities attribute this to the major success of the “100 Million Healthy Lives” initiative in eliminating Hepatitis C, a leading cause of liver cancer in Egypt.

National success

Egypt’s representative to IARC and Director of the Egyptian Center for Medical Research at Ain Shams University, Hisham al-Ghazaly, stated that these results reflect the success of a national operational model based on integration among various state institutions.

Institutional has contributed to the implementation of effective national programs for prevention, early detection, and treatment, alongside support for scientific research, training, and the expansion of health services, he said.

This has directly resulted in improved cancer control indicators and enhanced healthcare quality.

He added that Egypt’s achievements serve as a successful model of institutional integration, underscoring that unifying the efforts of all relevant stakeholders is fundamental to achieving sustainable health development, improving citizens’ quality of life, and bolstering Egypt’s regional and international standing in the fight against non-communicable diseases.

Ghazaly further noted that reducing cancer incidence relies primarily on mitigating risk factors—foremost among them smoking, Hepatitis C infection, obesity, and improper use of hormones.

He emphasized that Egypt’s success in eliminating Hepatitis C is a global achievement, particularly given that the country was once among those most severely affected by the disease; he noted that this success has directly resulted in a decline in liver cancer incidence rates.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Trump announces leadership of AI task force
World.content:
President Donald Trump on Sunday announced the creation of a “Super Intelligence Force” to “ensure that America continues to lead the world” when it comes to artificial intelligence.

The president said the task force will coordinate the government’s engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, infrastructure providers and AI companies.

The group will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon chief technology officer Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor. The task force will report to Trump and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, the president said.

This announcement comes just days after the president hosted top AI executives at the White House. The group signed a new commitment aimed at better “self-policing” their companies’ AI models, arguing that the light-touch approach represents the best way to balance safety concerns with the president’s desire to accelerate a technology he’s dubbed “Super Intelligence.”

Trump heaped praise on the CEOs who attended a high-profile White House luncheon — while dismissing concerns about the dangers of the fast-developing AI technology.

This story is developing and will be updated.

World.title: Co-pilot accused of trying to hijack Flydubai plane probably acted alone, Israeli sources say
World.content:
Tel Aviv — The co-pilot accused of attacking his colleague on board the The co-pilot accused of attacking his colleague on board the Flydubai flight to Israel and trying to seize the controls probably acted alone, Israeli sources told CNN.

International investigators are still working to determine a motive but an Israeli official said information from the inquiry suggested the suspect acted alone.

Another Israeli source said that, at the moment, Israel does not know of any link to a group or government. Both stressed this was their understanding so far.

In the aftermath of the attack, US President Donald Trump said that the suspect could be linked to Iran “based on what I’m hearing.” But he gave no other details.

Flydubai flight FZ1073 narrowly avoided disaster on its journey from Dubai, plummeting thousands of feet and passengers and crew bravely rushing into the cockpit to regain control of the aircraft.

Sources told CNN the suspect, named as Hamam al-Hammami, is an Omani national who had been removed from a previous job at Oman’s national airline last year following concerns about his extremist views. A post on one of his social media accounts included a photo of a photo of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after the death of Osama Bin Laden.

World.title: Egypt face a tough friendly test against South Africa at the Cairo International Stadium
World.content:
The Egyptian national football team faces its South African counterpart Bafana Bafana in a friendly match on Sunday at nine PM at Cairo International Stadium.

This match concludes a training camp during which the Pharaohs played two games: a goalless draw against Angola and a resounding five to zero victory over South Sudan.

Sunday’s showdown is more than just a routine fixture on the Pharaohs’ schedule—despite being a friendly on paper.

The coaching staff, led by Hossam Hassan, is prioritizing tactical insights over the result itself.

Having made significant strides in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, the team now aims to transform its current momentum into a more stable project ahead of the resumption of competitive matches.

The team enters the clash in high spirits, having returned to winning ways in the second round of qualifiers with a dominant five to zero victory over South Sudan—following an opening-round draw with Angola—thereby securing four points and the top spot in their group.

While the five-goal haul served as a clear statement of attacking intent, the match against South Africa will test the team’s form against a stronger, more organized opponent, offering the coaching staff a chance to gauge the players’ ability to maintain their effectiveness against a different caliber of rival.

The coach views the match as an opportunity to recalibrate his plans and experiment with certain personnel, all while preserving the team’s core structure.

Lineup to see limited changes

Indications suggest the head coach intends to make only limited changes to the lineup—potentially introducing Ahmed Sayed “Zizo” and Ali Mahmoud—while keeping Hossam Abdel-Maguid and Ramy Rabia in central defense, with a possibility that Omar Fayed could see action in the second half.

The importance of this match lies in the coaching staff’s search for alternatives capable of maintaining the team’s structure and rhythm when substitutions are made.

The international break offers a rare opportunity to test solutions that would be difficult to trial during competitive matches.

Hassan aims to give more playing time to substitute players while retaining some core members of the squad, particularly given that the match is a friendly and has no bearing on qualification.

The two national teams have met 13 times in their history – South Africa has secured seven victories compared to Egypt’s five, with one match ending in a draw.

This shared history adds extra significance to the match, particularly as Bafana Bafana are no strangers to Egyptian football.

The encounter also marks Pitso Mosimane’s return to Cairo to face the Pharaohs and sets the stage for a new clash with Hossam Hassan, following their previous meetings when Mosimane was at Al Ahly and Hassan was managing Al Ittihad of Alexandria.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Russian drone slams into Kyiv bridge in escalating campaign as Germany’s chancellor arrives to airsirens and explosions
World.content:
A Russian drone struck a major bridge in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv on Sunday as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the city to the sound of air raid sirens, explosions and air defense systems being activated.

Merz is in Kyiv to display support for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky amid Russia’s escalation of strikes on the city.

“Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks,” Merz said.

Highlighting attacks on Ukraine’s towns, residential buildings and energy, he said: “If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn ⁠against us.”

Video footage from Sunday morning’s strike showed the moment the city’s Northern Bridge was attacked, sparking a huge plume of fire and black smoke while cars were still traveling across. Two people were injured, the city’s mayor, Vitaliy Klitschko said.

It is the second time the Northern Bridge has been hit in as many days. On Thursday and Friday, Kyiv’s Southern Bridge, which serves ground transportation and the city’s subway system, was hit five times in less than 24 hours.

Ukrainian officials have said that Russian strikes on the capital’s infrastructure are attempting to cut the capital into two, as Kyiv is split along the Dnipro River, with businesses offices and government institutions on the right back, and the left bank mostly residential.

Kyiv plans to start building several alternative crossings over the Dnipro in case the attacks on the bridges continue, the minister of infrastructure said Sunday.

Russia’s Ministry of Defense has claimed the bridge is used to move Ukrainian troops and military supplies, and on Saturday said that it also targeted a logistics center in the Kyiv region.

‘Decisive weeks ahead’

Merz visited Kyiv alongside his Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy, Katarina Reiche, despite warnings from Russia on Saturday that foreign visitors and dignitaries to the Ukrainian capital are not safe amid an onslaught of Russian attacks.

Zelensky and Merz are tying up a significant defense and industrial partnership, which will see the two countries finalize a deal for the production of drones and missiles.

Berlin is also expected to release €1 billion ($1.13 billion) in military aid and €350 million ($390 million) for repairs to Ukraine’s damaged energy infrastructure, German government officials said.

Zelensky has warned that Ukraine’s defensive need is expanding amid Russia’s accelerated air campaign, which has seen Moscow fire high-speed, jet-powered Shahed-type drones that can bypass some of Ukraine’s air defense systems and exploit its lack of interceptors.

Earlier on Sunday, Merz said that Ukraine “is facing decisive weeks ahead.” Writing on X, he said: “I have traveled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.”

Meanwhile, there appears to be no immediate respite for Kyiv’s three million residents, with Moscow on Sunday saying that it will only intensify its strikes targeting the capital and other cities.

“Strikes by the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation against military and military-industrial facilities, as well as associated infrastructure in Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine, will be intensified,” the ministry said.

Russia’s renewed threat follows an interview Zelensky gave to Reuters news on Saturday, where he outlined that he plans to double down on attacks on oil refineries.

“We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners, etc. – what gives money to them for this war,” Zelensky said.

His comments come despite the urging of US President Donald Trump, who recently asked Ukraine to stay away from attacks on Russia’s oil infrastructure, claiming it was sending global oil prices surging.

CNN’s Kara Fox and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.

World.title: How a TV show may have helped save Flight 1073 from disaster
World.content:
One passenger aboard the diverted Flydubai flight has pointed to an unlikely source of inspiration behind his miraculous effort to help subdue the alleged attacker and take control of the plane: a TV show which reconstructs real-life air disasters.

After entering the cockpit, Yaniv Hayoun started “pulling back the handles,” he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday.

The Israeli prime minister asked if he knew how to operate the plane.

“I watch Air Crash Investigation, Mr. Prime Minister — really. The plane started to level out a bit, and then the pilot told me he was taking over the controls from there,” Hayoun said.

The show “Air Crash Investigation” presents a dramatized reconstruction of plane disasters involving fires, hijackings and crashes using aviation experts and eyewitnesses. The name of the show varies across different countries, including “Air Disasters” in the United States.

President Donald Trump marveled at the passenger’s explanation that he knew what to do because he’d watched the TV show, with the US leader saying he doesn’t like to watch the show “because bad things happen.”

“But he said he watches it a lot and he learned from watching that show sort of how to fly,” Trump said. “I think it’s the most amazing stuff.”

World.title: Foreign Ministry issues national ID card services for expats
World.content:
“National identity card issuance teams began work on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at several Egyptian diplomatic and consular missions abroad, including in Jordan, Dubai and Abu Dhabi,” the Foreign Ministry said.

Hundreds of Egyptians living abroad visited the diplomatic and consular missions seeking to issue, renew or update information on their national identity cards.

“The initiative is part of the Foreign Ministry’s efforts to protect the interests of and meet the needs of Egyptian communities abroad, in coordination with the Civil Status Sector at the Interior Ministry,” the Ministry said.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Nader Zaki said the national ID card issuance teams would visit a number of additional countries in the coming period, including Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Lebanon, France, Italy and Greece.

“The visits are intended to meet the needs of Egyptians abroad and implement the outcomes of the seventh edition of the Conference of Egyptians Abroad, held in Cairo in early August,” Zaki said.

He urged members of Egyptian communities in countries where the ID issuance teams are operating to contact the relevant Egyptian embassy or consulate promptly to learn about the required documents and book appointments, allowing the committees to issue cards to the largest possible number of citizens seeking the service.

World.title: PM: Egypt seeks to boost mutual investment opportunities in Tanzania
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly expressed hope that Tanzania’s participation in the “Alamein-Africa Business Forum” would help expand mutual investment opportunities, noting Egypt’s strong interest in increasing Egyptian investments in Tanzania and the readiness of Egyptian companies to expand their presence in the Tanzanian market across various development sectors.

The Prime Minister made his remarks during a meeting with Tanzanian Vice President Dewa Mwakasege Ndejembi and his delegation on the sidelines of the forum, held in New Alamein under the patronage of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

The talks focused on expanding cooperation in several areas, including investment, transport, ports, agriculture and healthcare. Madbouly said that Egypt is ready to share its expertise and support Tanzania in developing its ports and transport system, including the expansion of Dar es Salaam Port.

He also proposed exploring a joint agricultural project to reclaim land in Tanzania and expressed Egypt’s readiness to provide medical support, send medical convoys and train Tanzanian doctors in Egyptian hospitals.

The Prime Minister also outlined Egypt’s position on the Nile water issue, noting that Egypt has supported several development projects in the Nile Basin, including dams in Sudan and Uganda and, most recently, the Julius Nyerere Dam and Power Station in Tanzania. He stressed Egypt’s firm position on safeguarding its water rights.

For his part, the Tanzanian Vice President conveyed President Samia Suluhu’s greetings to President al-Sisi and stressed that Egypt and Tanzania enjoy historic and distinguished relations between their two peoples.

Ndejembi highlighted the Julius Nyerere Dam as one of the major development projects reflecting bilateral cooperation and praised the efforts and professionalism of the Arab Contractors and Elsewedy Electric consortium implementing the project.

He also expressed interest in benefiting from Egypt’s experience in transport and ports, particularly in expanding Dar es Salaam Port, with the Tanzanian transport minister set to visit Egyptian seaports.

The two sides also discussed expanding healthcare cooperation and training Tanzanian doctors in Egypt. Meanwhile, Egypt reaffirmed its support for sustainable development projects in the Nile Basin, stressing the importance of international law and mutual benefit among all basin countries.

World.title: Liberia: Defense Alleges Witness Tampering at AREPT; Taskforce Denies Wrongdoing in Saudi Rice Trial
World.content:
Defense attorney Gbawou Kowou says witnesses who testified for the accused were summoned to AREPT’s headquarters and pressured, while the taskforce says the incident was a misunderstanding and denies attempting to influence the witnesses.

By Jaheim T. Tumu

[email protected]

PAYNESVILLE CITY — A confrontation at the headquarters of the Asset Recovery and Property Retrieval Taskforce (AREPT) has triggered fresh tensions in the ongoing Saudi rice criminal trial, after defense lawyer Gbawou Kowou accused the agency of attempting to intimidate or tamper with witnesses who recently testified for the defense.



AREPT has denied the allegation, saying the individuals at the center of the controversy were not invited for questioning and that its lawyers immediately asked them to leave after discovering that they had recently testified as defense witnesses.

The dispute unfolded Sunday after Kowou went to the AREPT compound and began a livestream in which he alleged that several witnesses who had testified before Criminal Court “C” had been summoned to the agency and were being pressured about their testimony.

Standing outside the facility, Kowou repeatedly demanded access to the compound, claiming that his witnesses were being held inside.

“I’m live at AREPT. Witnesses who testified on our behalf yesterday were brought here and threatened,” Kowou said during the broadcast, describing the alleged conduct as witness tampering.

He later alleged that AREPT officials had locked the facility’s gate to prevent him from entering.

“They have locked the gate. The witnesses are in there,” he said. “If the witnesses are not there, open the gate.”

Kowou specifically accused AREPT Chairman Cllr. Edwin Kla Martin of directing the witnesses to report to the agency after their appearance in court.

The lawyer argued that the witnesses had already completed their testimony and should not have been subjected to further engagement by officials connected to the prosecution.

Kowou Allowed Into Compound

Kowou was later allowed into the AREPT compound, where he confronted officials over the presence of the witnesses.

Speaking to FrontPage Africa afterward, Kowou said the witnesses were members of the Group of 77 and the community of persons living with disabilities who had testified for the defense.

According to Kowou, the witnesses told him they had been threatened or pressured to report to the AREPT office in Paynesville after appearing in court.

He said he subsequently went to the facility to establish why witnesses who had already testified were being summoned by an agency involved in the prosecution.

Kowou was later taken to a police station following the confrontation.

According to the defense lawyer, AREPT subsequently told him that the situation was a misunderstanding.

But Kowou rejected the explanation, maintaining that the circumstances surrounding the witnesses’ presence at AREPT were troubling.

He characterized the move as sinister and argued that attempts to engage or influence witnesses after they had testified could amount to improper interference with the judicial process.

Kowou described the alleged conduct as tantamount to witness tampering, and said the matter should be taken seriously given the ongoing trial.

Heated Exchange at AREPT

Video footage from the scene showed a heated exchange between Kowou, AREPT employees and other individuals gathered outside the facility.

At one point, persons inside the compound instructed Kowou to stop filming and lower his camera. He refused.

“No, I can’t put the camera down so the world will know this kind of criminal act carried on by the prosecution,” Kowou said during the livestream.

As tensions escalated, officers of the Liberia National Police arrived at the scene.

Kowou repeated his allegations to the officers, insisting that a crime was being committed because defense witnesses had allegedly been brought to AREPT after testifying in court.

“A crime is being committed. My witnesses testified before the court yesterday, and they were brought here,” he told the officers.

The livestream ended as Kowou indicated that he would accompany the police inside the compound to further address the matter.

AREPT Rejects Allegation

In a statement issued after the incident, AREPT denied that its officials had threatened, intimidated or attempted to influence any defense witness.

According to AREPT Public Relations Officer Joseph F. Daniels, the controversy arose after a potential witness who had previously provided a statement during the agency’s investigation was asked to appear at AREPT with other individuals familiar with the Saudi rice matter.

AREPT said the potential witness arrived with two people whom he identified as being familiar with the case.

The agency said its lawyers did not initially know that the two individuals had recently appeared before Criminal Court “C” as subpoenaed defense witnesses.

“Upon recognizing them, AREPT lawyers immediately asked the two individuals to leave the premises,” the statement said.

AREPT said the two witnesses were not invited by the agency, were not interviewed and did not provide any additional statements.

The taskforce said it therefore rejects the allegation that its lawyers attempted to influence or intimidate the witnesses.

“If defense counsel has evidence of witness tampering or intimidation, that evidence should be presented to the court, where such allegations can be properly addressed,” AREPT said.

Dispute Comes as Prosecution Prepares Rebuttal

The controversy comes as AREPT prosecutors prepare to present rebuttal witnesses in the high-profile Saudi rice case involving 13 former government officials.

The defendants are facing corruption-related charges stemming from the handling and distribution of Saudi-donated rice during the transition to the Boakai administration.

The trial has attracted public and political attention, with defense lawyers repeatedly challenging aspects of the prosecution’s case and government witnesses providing competing accounts of how the rice was handled.

The latest dispute places the conduct of both the prosecution and defense under renewed scrutiny.

For the defense, the central question is whether witnesses who have already testified were subsequently approached in a manner that could influence their testimony.

For AREPT, the agency maintains that no such engagement occurred and that its lawyers acted to remove the two former defense witnesses from the premises once their status became known.

World.title: SN Brussels Travelers from Liberia, Sierra Leone Face Tougher Scrutiny as Europe Hunts ‘Bolle Jos’
World.content:
MONROVIA – For many Liberian and Sierra Leonean families, the SN Brussels flight is more than a ticket. Brussels Airlines, still called “SN” by most travelers here after the carrier it succeeded in 2007, is the plane that brings a mother home for Christmas, carries a student to a European campus and returns a trader with goods for a Waterside shop.

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

It is also, investigators in Monrovia and Brussels now say, a route drug networks have tried to exploit.



Caught at the carousel

On July 31, Belgian customs officers were checking passengers off a Brussels Airlines flight from Freetown when they stopped a 22-year-old woman from Anderlecht, according to the Halle-Vilvoorde prosecutor’s office and Belgian media. Her two suitcases held 51 kilograms of cocaine.

She had not been on the plane. Investigators believe she was sent only to collect the bags and are still trying to establish how she got into the baggage reclaim hall. A judge later moved her from detention to electronic monitoring.

Weeks earlier at Roberts International Airport (RIA), Liberian security officers flagged six cargo boxes labeled as Maggi cubes and lappa. Inside were 198 compressed plates of cocaine. The Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) said at the time the shipment, valued at US$19.2 million, was bound for Brussels Airlines’ Europe-bound operations. A Justice Ministry charge sheet later listed London as the final destination.

This week, those two scenes met in a single policy fight in Europe. And the people likely to feel it first are not the kingpins, but honest passengers queuing at RIA and Lungi.

‘Chubby Jos’ next door

The man at the center of Europe’s anger lives one border away. Jos Leijdekkers, known in the Netherlands as “Bolle Jos” (Chubby Jos), is that country’s most wanted criminal. Dutch media placed him in Sierra Leone in early 2025.

In the Netherlands he was sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted assassination. In Belgium, his sentences across several cases total more than 100 years, Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported. In May, a court in Dendermonde, Belgium, sentenced him in absentia to eight years for his role in moving 11 tonnes of cocaine from Sierra Leone to the Port of Antwerp in October 2023, hidden in palm kernel meal. Twenty accomplices were also convicted.

The Economist’s 1843 magazine reported on September 18 that he lived in Sierra Leone under the name “Omar Sheriff,” posed as a wealthy investor and kept bodyguards from Ghana and South Africa.

Dutch media have reported that he has a relationship, and a child, with a daughter of President Julius Maada Bio. FrontPageAfrica has not independently confirmed this.

No treaty, no handover

The Netherlands and Sierra Leone have no extradition treaty. The Dutch formally delivered an extradition request anyway, and Freetown has yet to sign off on it. Van Weel said in June that Sierra Leone keeps telling him the procedures are under way.

That patience has run out. On X on Thursday morning, Van Weel announced that “the EU will no longer provide budget support to the authorities of Sierra Leone this year.” He told the Dutch daily De Telegraaf a day earlier that the suspension, about €18 million for 2026, was because Sierra Leone is not cooperating on the extradition. The Netherlands also wants a planned €22.5 million for next year held back.

The freeze hits money paid straight into the state budget. Development and humanitarian aid are excluded, so Europe is aiming at the government, not at Sierra Leoneans in need. Van Weel has called it bizarre that Europe should support a country sheltering one of the world’s biggest drug criminals.

Speaking to NOS in Luxembourg on Thursday, Van Weel welcomed the Commission’s decision. “It sends a very clear signal from the European Commission that Sierra Leone must stop harboring this criminal,” he said.

Asked whether the measure was too harsh on an impoverished country, Van Weel turned the question back on its government. Leijdekkers, he said, causes “immense destruction, including for the people of Sierra Leone.”

“They could resolve this within 24 hours by arresting and extraditing this man,” he said.

If the aid freeze does not work, Van Weel warned, “we will continue to increase the pressure through other channels.” He added: “We are fully committed to bringing this criminal to the Netherlands.”

The Dutch have also worked through Sierra Leone’s neighbors. Van Weel told De Telegraaf in July that Liberia and Ghana are aware of the risks and frustrated by Freetown’s refusal to act.

Ghana has already moved. In September, its Narcotics Control Commission arrested three men accused of representing Leijdekkers’ network there, after French customs seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine in Dunkirk. The drugs, valued at about €225 million, were hidden in a container of plastic waste shipped from Ghana.

The Economist estimates about a third of the cocaine reaching Europe now passes through West Africa. Liberia is on its route map.

Liberia’s own test

Liberia’s record this year shows how close the trade has come to home.

Police charged five men and the cargo firm Global Logistics Services (GLS) on July 4 over the June RIA seizure of about 237.6 kilograms. Among them was Michael U.S. Browne, whose release from prison after a 2024 drug charge the Senate has ordered investigated.

Prosecutors allege GLS operations manager Paul Jamaal King organized the shipment and then tried to recover it after it was flagged, including by offering money to airport security. King has pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent. In July, the Monrovia City Court found probable cause and sent him and six co-defendants to Criminal Court “C” for trial. Days later, the case appeared stalled because certified records had not reached the court.

Investigators followed the airport leads to the VOA community on the RIA Highway. On July 22, joint security forces arrested two foreign nationals and uncovered a suspected cocaine cache officials valued at up to US$50 million.

When the guards are the thieves

On Tuesday, a jury in Kakata convicted two LDEA agents posted at RIA, Special Agent Joe Logan and Agent Lovette Flowers, along with Nigerian national Tony Obi. Judge Roosevelt Z. Willie of the 13th Judicial Circuit sentenced each to 20 years, the maximum.

Prosecutors said the agents took four of 14 seized plates of cocaine and sold them, and that the network paid about US$10,000 in bribes to LDEA officers. The case began in July 2025 with Quita Dolo Kosso, who landed at RIA from Thailand on a Kenya Airways flight with about 3.4 kilograms of cocaine. She pleaded guilty and is serving five years.

The lesson for travelers is uncomfortable. Drugs can be caught at the gate and still leak out the back door. Europe has noticed both.

Brussels takes aim

Van Weel is in Luxembourg, where EU justice and home affairs ministers meet Thursday and Friday. The agenda covers migration, the EU drugs strategic framework and how the geopolitical climate is affecting Europe’s security. He wrote on X that talks would include “the safety of Europe and the EU-sanctions regime for organized crime.”

He is urging ministers to adopt the regime swiftly, Politico Europe’s Playbook reported. He told Playbook the Bolle Jos case calls for measures against all organized criminals Europe cannot immediately detain, “not only against him,” and said he hopes the regime is concluded by year’s end.

An EU diplomat with the Dutch delegation told OCCRP that cross-border networks can be “very effective” when based in a third country whose authorities will not cooperate or extradite. “The standard criminal law approach isn’t achieving the results we want,” the diplomat said. “That is why there is a push to expand that toolkit.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the package in her 2025 State of the Union address, and the EU Council mandated work on it. On July 9, the Commission and the EU’s foreign policy chief proposed a regime covering drug trafficking, migrant smuggling, human and firearms trafficking and money laundering. It would freeze assets, impose trade restrictions and bar listed people from entering or transiting EU states.

It still has to be agreed, and adoption needs the backing of all 27 member states. Earlier efforts stalled because national police feared sanctions could tip off suspects and spoil investigations. Van Weel said support is stronger now.

What it means for SN Brussels passengers

Sanctions target kingpins, their financiers and fixers, not ordinary travelers. But passengers on the Monrovia–Freetown–Brussels line already live with the side effects, and those are likely to grow.

Tighter checks on arrival. The 51-kilogram arrest came during a targeted customs check of passengers off the Freetown flight. Expect more of those, and more bags opened.

Networks recruiting the young. This week, Belgian and French authorities announced 21 arrests in a ring that used Brussels Airport. It recruited “extractors” through social media, bought tickets just to reach baggage halls and paid airport workers to pull drugs from suitcases before they reached the carousel.

Your bag, someone else’s crime.

The RIA cases show cargo and luggage can be tampered with by insiders. Lock and label bags, and refuse parcels from anyone, even relatives, without seeing what is inside.

Travel bans for facilitators. Once adopted, the EU regime could bar listed people from entering or passing through Europe. Anyone working for a front company, freight forwarder or fixer tied to a listed network risks being swept up.

A reputation tax. Every bust adds to the suspicion attached to a Liberian or Sierra Leonean passport at a European counter. Honest travelers pay that bill in delays and questions.

For now, the man Europe most wants sits a short flight from Monrovia, beyond reach. Van Weel insists Freetown could change that in a day. The question for Liberia is whether it is seen as part of the problem or part of the fix. The 20-year sentences handed down in Kakata this week were a start. The next test is the US$19.2 million trial.
