“A meeting of the Seed Cane and Sugarcane Variety Approval Sub-Committee was held recently, discussions regarding the release of new sugarcane varieties took place during the meeting, attended by sub-committee officials, Director UPCSR, scientists from the UP Council of Sugarcane Research (Shahjahanpur) and the Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (Lucknow). Data concerning the yield and sugar content of new sugarcane varieties—proposed by the U.P. Council of Sugarcane Research, Shahjahanpur, were presented,” told Ministhy S., Uttar Pradesh Cane Commissioner and Managing Director State Sugar Corporation Limited, to The Hindu.

“According to the data, the average yield of the plant crop for the early-maturing variety CoS.23232 was 95.56 tons/hectare, which is 9.44% higher than that of the standard variety Co.0238. This variety is resistant to Red Rot disease and exhibits good ratoon performance. Following deliberations, the sugarcane variety is being cultivated, as it was found to be superior to the popular variety Co.0238 on both parameters of yield and sugar recovery. They would prove to be the best alternative for farmers and would contribute to increasing both sugarcane and sugar production,” she added.

Abhishek Anand, Additional Cane Commissioner and Director UPCSR added, “Furthermore, the sub-committee considered the release of the early-maturing sugarcane variety developed by the Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR), Lucknow. In the meeting of the sub-committee, a decision was made, keeping farmers’ interests in mind to declare six older sugarcane varieties as unsuitable due to their unpopularity and negligible cultivation area; these sugarcane varieties will be phased out over the next two years.”

“With the approval of new, high-yielding and high-sugar-recovery sugarcane varieties, farmers will have a wide basket of varieties for the cultivation; this will lead to increased sugarcane yield and greater economic prosperity for the state’s farmers, while the sugar industry will also benefit from the improved sugar recovery. Director UPCSR said that this will boost the sugarcane farmer’s income and go a long way in doubling the farmer’s income. It is a great testament to progress and research done by scientists of UPCSR Shahjahanpur,” he said.

World.title: The right to more than a room and roof
World.content:
For 35 years, Balunkeswar Paikray has travelled hundreds of kilometres, knocked on the doors of every authority he could think of. He even reachedout to the Prime Minister of India, and, touched the feet of local government officials in the hope that someone would listen. The 55-year-old visually impaired man in Odisha’s Khordha district, says, “I am not asking for charity. I am fighting for a rightful share in my ancestral property.”

Paikray says his share among the three siblings would amount to 40,000 square feet of paternal property in Khordha’s Kadab village. “Now, I live in less than 300 square feet,” he says, of his room, bathroom, and backyard.

Paikray’s long struggle has given him a painful insight into how the world treats those who cannot see, walk, or behave in what is considered regular. His battle has revealed how a disability, whether present from birth or caused by an accident, can deepen a person’s vulnerability, strip away social standing and, in the maze of bureaucracy and family disputes, reduce an individual to almost a non-entity.

In August this year the Odisha government formulated a comprehensive set of guidelines to safeguard the property and inheritance rights of Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016. Paikray and lakhs of others saw hope.

The move has also been welcomed by those working in the disability sector, who see it as a significant step towards protecting PwDs from discrimination in matters of property, including ancestral, inherited, and self-acquired.

The three-page guidelines suggested that the Revenue and Disaster Management Department examine the feasibility of issuing comprehensive guidelines and instructions to all revenue authorities to safeguard the land and property rights of PwDs.

One of the key proposals is to maintain a register of complaints relating to the property rights of PwDs at the tehsil and Sub-Collector levels, with periodic monitoring by the District Collector. Activists pointed out that while revenue laws provide safeguards for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities — including prior permission for transfer of their land or property to persons from the general category—PwDs remain more vulnerable and require similar protection.

Safeguarding the differently-abled

In August this year, the Odisha government’s Suresh Kumar Vashishth wrote to Arabinda Kumar Padhee to issue comprehensive guidelines that would protect all PwDs’ rights over inherited and self-acquired property. Vashishth is principal secretary to the Department of Social Security and Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (SSEPD); Padhee is additional chief secretary, Revenue and Disaster Management Department, under which property is registered.

The guidelines were formulated based on the RPwD Act, particularly Sections 12, 13, 84, and 85. These cast an obligation upon the government to ensure protection of the rights, property, legal capacity, and the interests of PwDs and to prevent all forms of abuse, violence, exploitation, and discrimination.

“Persons with disabilities are often subjected to unlawful deprivation of their paternal, ancestral and self-acquired properties due to their physical, sensory, intellectual or psychosocial disabilities,” Vashishth wrote. He also observed that numerous instances had come to the department’s notice where vulnerable PwDs were “coerced, deceived or unduly influenced into transferring their immovable properties, are unlawfully deprived of their legitimate inheritance, or their lands are wrongfully occupied, cultivated or alienated by others”. This resulted in economic exploitation and violation of constitutional and legal rights.

He suggested including the establishment of a regulatory mechanism for protection of paternal, ancestral, inherited, and self-acquired immovable properties of PwDs.

Vashishth called for directions to all revenue officers to ensure that PwDs and their lawful heirs are not deprived of their legitimate share in ancestral property through fraud or coercion.

The State Commission for Persons with Disabilities, along with district- and block-level officers, provides a forum for PwDs to seek redressal of their grievances.

Vashishth suggested immediate and expeditious inquiry upon receipt of complaints relating to illegal occupation, encroachment, cultivation, mutation, or alienation of lands belonging to PwDs and strict monitoring of these properties.

The principal secretary suggested capacity building and sensitisation of revenue officers regarding the rights of persons with disabilities under the RPwD Act, and the need for adopting disability-sensitive procedures.

Bratati Harichandan, State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, says this is an inter-departmental effort. “We have requested the Panchayati Raj Department to sensitise officials at the grassroots level so that persons with disabilities are accommodated under government housing schemes and are assured of a roof over their heads, particularly when they are forced out of their own homes,” Harichandan says.

The struggle

Milan Kumar Das, 45, his brother Chandan, and sister Mamata, from Bhadrak district, all of whom have 100% locomotor disabilities, are easy targets for those determined to usurp legally inherited property.

Confined to a cramped 100-square-foot room, the siblings and their 80-year-old mother depend on each other for survival. Together, they receive about ₹14,000 a month in disability and other pensions, while subsidised rice keeps hunger at bay. What weighs on them most is not poverty, but the loss of property that they say should have been theirs.

“Our father was an employee of Indian Oil Corporation. He had purchased land and built a house here [in Nadigaon village in Bhadrak district]. After his death, we were driven out by other members of the joint family. Only after a police intervention, were we given a tiny room as shelter,” Milan says.

For nearly 10 years, Milan says he and his siblings have appealed to the Bhadrak district administration and police, seeking justice. “Had we not been physically challenged, no one could have mustered the courage to deprive us of our parental property,” he says.

In Jajpur district, Prakash Mohapatra, 48, who is visually impaired, worries about his future. “Now I live with my mother and brother in the village,” he says, fearing the situation will change with time. “My repeated applications for a house under the Prime Minister Awas Yojana (PMAY) havenot led anywhere, and the application is stuck in some government office,” Mohapatra says.

He had petitioned the Delhi-based Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, in a letter, to include all persons with physical disabilities in welfare schemes. “I could not follow up the case for its logical conclusion,” says Mohapatra.

The State Commission for Persons with Disabilities (SCPD) is flooded with requests to facilitate houses under the PMAY to PwDs. Following the Commission’s intervention, 19,000 PMAY houses were sanctioned in Odisha for PwDs in 2024-25, according to the State Commission for Persons with Disabilities.

Manjulata Panda, 49, Odisha’s first visually impaired woman to earn a PhD and now a lecturer in a college in Sambalpur district, is fighting to get the family property registered in her and her brother’s names. He too is visually impaired and is a teacher in a government primary school.

“Since both of us have good jobs, we don’t struggle for food or survival. But our ancestral properties are entangled in a procedural mess, we are not able to record it in our name,” Panda says. In Panda’s case, no one else has claimed the land, but she says there are “procedural hurdles” that the government must help with.

Larger concerns

The Odisha government’s move came after Dr. Arabinda Mohanty, a paediatrician by profession and an activist on disability for more than three decades, highlighted the plight of people with physical and intellectual disabilities. In 2025, he wrote to the State Commission for Persons with Disabilities (SCPD) to take up the issue with the government, insisting on the need for such guidelines.

“I have come across numerous cases of discrimination against intellectually challenged and physically challenged persons. Invariably, they don’t get the rightful share of their ancestral property,” says Mohanty. He adds that parents of children with intellectual disabilities worry about their children’s lives after their time.

Harichandan concurs: “Discrimination often begins at home. When parental property is divided, sons and daughters with no physical or intellectual disabilities often get the best rooms and enjoy the finest facilities created by their parents. Children with disabilities, on the other hand, are frequently pushed into a corner — an annexe or a poorly maintained portion of the house. In fact, children with disabilities are the ones who deserve the best part of their parents’ homes.”

For PwDs, life is often marked by layers of uncertainty, emotional trauma, and betrayal. A child born with a disability is sometimes disowned by parents. The issue of property transfer comes later. The child is often treated as a burden that no one wants to shoulder.

“Discrimination often begins at home. When parental property is divided, sons and daughters with no physical or intellectual disabilities often get the best rooms and enjoy the finest facilities created by their parents. Children with disabilities, on the other hand, are frequently pushed into a corner — an annexe or a poorly maintained portion of the house. In fact, children with disabilities are the ones who deserve the best part of their parents’ homes”Bratati Harichandan,State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities

The Odisha government has established MANODAYA, a residential facility in Bhubaneswarthat provides psychological and neuropsychological assessments, evidence-based psychotherapy, cognitive rehabilitation, and support across the lifespan of those living with disability.

Children with disabilities are often brought to the centre by their mothers, many of whom receive little moral or financial support from their spouses. These mothers carry the additional responsibility of caring for their children with intellectual disabilities, while also dealing with their own emotional and personal challenges.

Redressal of grievances

The RPwD Act provides for the establishment of special courts in every district to deal with offences against PwDs. “If the police themselves are unaware of the provisions of the RPwD Act, 2016, how will they register cases under its relevant provisions? And how will such cases eventually reach the special courts?” Harichandan says.

The Supreme Court in 2025 revised its case-listing priorities, placing cases involving PwDs seventh in the order of priority.

Shruti Mohapatra, 63,a disability rights activist who is herself is a person with orthopaedic disability, says those with intellectual disabilities are among the most vulnerable when it comes to the transfer and protection of property rights. “To some extent, those with visual, hearing, and orthopaedic disabilities can raise their voices against discrimination or injustice. But persons with intellectual disabilities are largely dependent on their parents or trusted legal guardians,” she says.

Mohapatra also points to the lack of disability-friendly facilities in the justice system. The absence of interpreters and accessible court proceedings, including documents in Braille for persons with visual disabilities, further compounds their helplessness, she says.

“While society often ignores and disowns persons with intellectual disabilities, the government has also failed to ensure adequate employment opportunities for them. What use is immovable property if it does not provide a person with an income and help improve their quality of life?” asks Kartik Chandra Pandab, secretary of Rourkela-based voluntary organisation Shradha Foundation, which works in the disability sector.

Firoz Alam, a gold medallist at the Paralympics and Special Olympics, also rues what he describes as the government’s neglect of PwDs. Working at a tea stall in Rourkela for a monthly wage of ₹5,000, Firoz says that, alongside safeguarding their property rights, the government must take concrete steps to protect the livelihoods and lives of PwDs by ensuring that they receive their rightful share of employment opportunities.

Meanwhile, Paikray hopes the government’s guidelines will finally help him claim his share of property before he dies.

World.title: Kerala High Court orders CBI probe into soldier’s disappearance 14 years ago
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to investigate a 14-year-old missing case of a soldier, who was a rifleman with the Tripura State Rifles, a paramilitary force.

Justice G. Girish issued the order on a petition by the soldier’s father seeking a CBI investigation to find out what happened to his son. The peaceful sleep enjoyed by a civilian was “at the cost of sleepless nights, vigilance and sacrifice of the soldier,” and civil society owed a responsibility to stand by the soldier who protects them if he faced a personal crisis, the court stated.

Subash Chandra Bose, a native of Vengoor in Ernakulam, went missing on April 4, 2012, while returning from leave in Kerala to Guwahati by train. His father last saw him at the Ernakulam railway station on April 3, 2012. The father received a phone call from his son the next day, from an unfamiliar mobile number, to inform him that the train had reached Visakhapatnam and that he was not feeling well. However, on April 10, 2012, the Commandant of Tripura State Rifles informed the father that his son had not reported back to the office after the leave period.

The State government stated that it had no objection to handing over the case to the CBI. However, the CBI contended that the court did not have territorial jurisdiction, since Mr. Bose had gone missing somewhere between Visakhapatnam and Guwahati. It also contended that there was only a very rare possibility of tracing the missing person after a lapse of 14 years.

The court held that, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, if an offence is committed during a journey, a court with local jurisdiction in the places forming part of the journey may order an inquiry. The court observed that a premier investigating agency like the CBI was not expected to take a pessimistic view in a case like this. The court recognised that the golden hours in a missing persons case were 48 to 72 hours. Yet, it stated that in cases where a paramilitary Jawan who guarded the nation’s borders went missing without leads, the court could not shut its doors against him when a CBI investigation is sought as a last resort.

World.title: 'We are not yes-men': CM Afridi launches PTI long march to Islamabad, convoy enters Karak district
World.content:
PESHAWAR/LAKKI MARWAT/DI KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad from Lakki Marwat, saying the party would “not accept” any policy that was against the interests of the people of KP.

The PTI has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government, which has vowed to prevent any violent gatherings in the capital. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.

By late Sunday night, the convoy led by the KP chief minister had entered Karak district and reached Hamidan Chowk.

In a post shortly before 11pm, PTI said Afridi’s convoy was en route to Karak after the KP CM addressed supporters at a roundabout located at the border between Bannu and Karak districts.

Earlier in the day, Afridi reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead his party’s long march, which was launched from Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Indus Highway.

In Lakki Marwat, an AFP journalist saw thousands of people take to the streets. Many of the demonstrators carried red and green flags of the PTI, and a huge billboard affixed on the side of a truck read “release Imran Khan” and featured a picture of the beaming former prime minister.

Addressing thousands of participants in Lakki Marwat, Afridi urged the public to step out of their homes for the sake of Pakistan, saying Imran, along with his wife and sisters, was in prison and they should show the world that they were the “true owners” of the country.

He said the “PTI’s negotiating committee had gone to Islamabad to lower the political temperature, but those making decisions behind closed doors had sabotaged the talks.

“They wanted their will to prevail in KP, but I declared that only Imran Khan’s vision and policies would be implemented here. We do not accept any policy that is not in the interest of the people of KP and the Pashtuns,” he maintained.

The chief minister declared: “We are not ‘yes-men’; we are soldiers of Imran Khan, and we will carry forward his policies.”

He repeatedly asked the crowd whether it supported a military operation, asking those opposed to it to raise their hands.

He questioned the policy being followed to tackle terrorism, saying: “What kind of policy is this, where terrorism has persisted for 22 years?”

KP CM insisted there had been peace during Imran’s government because his policies were sound, but following the “regime change operation”, terrorists were resettled, leading to “infinite terrorism”.

In 2023, after his ouster, Imran had defended his government’s plan to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

“We will eradicate terrorism, and if our policy is implemented, we will restore peace within 100 days,” he claimed.

He said the long march was being launched from Gandi Chowk and would conclude at another chowk. At this, the crowd shouted: “D-Chowk.”

“We are a political force and a party, and those who dream of the demise of the PTI can never succeed,” he added.

Afridi said the participants would leave from Gandi Chowk and their next stop would be Karak.

PTI workers had started gathering at Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Highway on Sunday afternoon to participate in the long march. Strict security measures were in place, with a large police contingent deployed at the site along with armoured personnel carriers and bomb disposal squads.

Afridi assailed for using ‘state helicopter’

A special helipad was prepared near Maidadkhel for Afridi and a video shared on social media platforms earlier showed a crowd of PTI workers gathered around it as KP’s chief executive touched down.

A video shared by the PTI on its X account showed Afridi’s convoy surrounded by a large crowd of party workers and supporters.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar criticised Afridi for using a “state helicopter for a political march”.

Calling the use of the helicopter a “violation of the Islamabad High Court’s orders”, he wrote on X, referring to a recent ruling that directed provincial governments to ensure that no government resources or machinery was used to facilitate any march or gathering.

“Terrorism is spreading in the province and Nero is playing his flute,” Tarar quipped.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said the use of the helicopter amounted to contempt of court by violating the IHC order.

“When the chief minister himself does not uphold the court’s orders and uses state resources for political activities, what expectation can there be for his workers to abide by the law?” Kundi wrote on X.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also made a sarcastic post on X, sharing the video and saying, “Sohail Afridi sahib’s Heli ride today from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat must have been for official work, possibly related to the security situation and counterterrorism efforts.”

Special Assistant to the KP CM for Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saad earlier told journalists at his residence that convoys from the southern KP districts would join the “peaceful long” march at Gandi Chowk.

“If workers from some southern districts, especially Tank and Waziristan, could not attend the long march today due to law and order-related curfew and other restrictions, they would join the movement on the way to Peshawar the next day,” he said.

Gandapur convoy returns to DI Khan

Earlier, PTI workers and supporters, led by former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, set out from Dera Ismail Khan to join the party’s long march at Lakki Marwat.

However, according to Gandapur, they were forced to return from Yarik on their way because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation.

The former KP CM insisted that the decision was taken to avoid exposing party workers to unnecessary risk, after the convoy remained stranded at Yarik for several hours.

Addressing the workers at Yarik, Gandapur noted that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days and that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation.

Gandapur told the workers that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision based on the prevailing circumstances, the safety of the workers and the instructions of the party leadership.

He said the workers could again set out to join the long march if the situation improved or the party leadership issued fresh instructions. The PTI leader contended that if the party leadership called him again, he could reach the long march within two hours.

He emphasised that the law and order situation did not warrant keeping a large number of workers at the site overnight.

The former KP CM also told the workers that they could remain at Yarik if they wanted to, but he could not violate the instructions issued by the party leadership.

He stressed that the decision taken by the senior leadership was not merely a personal decision, but one that he regarded as being in line with Imran’s instructions.

However, during the address, some workers expressed disagreement with the decision to take the convoy back. They said they wanted to remain at Yarik and continue their participation in the protest for as long as the movement continued.

Gandapur expressed displeasure over their position and urged them to take the practical situation on the ground into account. “TikTok-type talk” should not be made here, he told the workers, stressing that decisions had to be based on the situation on the ground.

The former KP CM subsequently persuaded the workers to return, following which the convoy left Yarik for DI Khan.

Before departing from DI Khan, the ex-CM stressed that the protest should remain peaceful and urged the participants to maintain discipline and refrain from violence, vandalism and confrontation with law enforcement personnel.

He said the party would follow a policy of “live and let live” during the protest and directed workers not to take the law into their hands.

“Those who block roads or engage in confrontation are not our workers,” Gandapur said, asking the participants to remain peaceful throughout the march.

He further urged the participants to avoid any activity that could lead to clashes or damage to public or private property.

The PTI’s march, being carried out to demand the release of its jailed founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan, is the latest bone of contention between the two sides.

In August, the PTI announced the long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4 (today).

Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken.

After weekend talks, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah has further warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad.

Plan for the march

According to the plan for the march shared by the KP CM on X, PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan and Bannu will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk on Oct 4.

The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat.

Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani.

The caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” the KP CM said.

They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.

Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.”

Ahead of the march, movement on several roads on KP has been banned under Section 144.

Section 144 imposed in several KP districts

Section 144 has been imposed in several districts of KP through notifications issued by the respective deputy commissioners, with restrictions on the movement of people and vehicles along specified routes, citing security and public safety concerns.

In DI Khan, the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on specified roads and routes has been banned between 6am and 6pm from Oct 4 to Oct 6, citing the prevailing law-and-order situation and public safety concerns.

In Upper South Waziristan, Section 144 has been imposed from Oct 3 to Oct 5, banning the movement of cargo vehicles, rickshaws and dumpers over a possible VBSB/VBIED threat in adjoining areas.

In Lower South Waziristan, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 1 to Oct 10, banning the movement of loader rickshaws, single- and double-cabin cargo vehicles, Shahzore vehicles, Mazdas, Suzuki loaders and dumpers in Wana and Azam Warsak. The notification cited security and public safety concerns.

In District Tank, restrictions on the movement of individuals and all types of traffic along specified routes have been imposed under Section 144 from 9pm on Oct 3 until noon on Oct 5. The notification cited the prevailing law-and-order situation, public safety concerns and the need to ensure the safe movement of law enforcement personnel.

In Hangu, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 3 to Oct 6, banning the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on six routes, including the Hangu-Kohat, Hangu-Thall, Hangu Bypass and Hangu-Sumari roads.

The restrictions do not apply to law enforcement agencies and emergency services, while exemptions may be granted by the district police officer or security forces.

World.title: PTI terms access to Imran 'principal point of deadlock', claims Centre refused to include it in agreement
World.content:
The PTI on Sunday asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of its talks with the Centre was that the latter refused to incorporate terms regarding access to incarcerated party founder Imran Khan into a proposed agreement.

Hours-long negotiations yesterday between an opposition delegation comprising the PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP, ended in a deadlock.

While the federal government blamed the PTI for the failure of negotiations, the main opposition party denied the allegations and claimed that the federal government was responsible for all that happened on Saturday night.

In a press release posted on social media, the PTI expressed regret that the negotiations concluded without substantive progress, despite “serious efforts” to address concerns including political instability, access to the PTI founder as well as his medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in the country, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The statement said that the “principal point of the deadlock” was the party’s demand for immediate access to Imran, so that its leadership could consult him on matters of “national and political importance”.

According to the statement, the government agreed to restore meetings between Imran and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but did not agree to the additional measures concerning his medical assessment and treatment.

“In an effort to facilitate progress, the negotiating team conveyed that other demands could be set aside if the government agreed to this single request. However, according to PTI, the government declined to make access to Imran Khan part of the proposed agreement,” the PTI said.

“PTI welcomed the resumption of family and legal meetings but stressed that such access cannot substitute for proper medical examination and necessary treatment,” the statement read, adding that the party called for Imran’s health to be addressed with “seriousness, transparency and humanitarian consideration”.

The party stressed that just as leaders of other political parties remained central to decision-making and policy, the PTI must also be allowed to consult its chairman; restricting such consultation limited the scope for meaningful political engagement, it added.

Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

Despite an order by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowing him twice-a-week meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays with his family, lawyers and other associates, Imran has been restricted from meeting visitors for several months.

His health has deteriorated over the course of his prison sentence, prompting outcry from members of the party.

According to the PTI, Imran’s health and medical treatment were also raised as a matter of fundamental importance in the talks, with the negotiating team seeking immediate access to him, his transfer to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for treatment, and the constitution of an “appropriate” medical board — including his personal physician — to ensure his proper examination, diagnosis and treatment.

After his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January, Imran has been provided with treatment at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

In mid-August, the Supreme Court ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment. However, the government later revealed that Imran was instead taken to Pims, prompting a strong reaction from his family and party.

Security situation in KP

The security situation in KP also featured prominently in the discussions, with the PTI saying it stressed that the concerns of the public must remain central to counterterrorism policies.

According to the statement, the Centre sought the provincial government’s “unconditional support” for its counterterrorism measures and operations as well as support for imposing emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged districts and adjoining areas.

“The PTI reiterated its unequivocal condemnation of terrorism and stressed that eliminating terrorism, protecting citizens and restoring lasting peace must remain a national priority,” it said, adding that the party paid tribute to the officers and personnel of the authorities that have sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism and expressed solidarity with civilians and families who had suffered from terrorist violence.

“Terrorism cannot be defeated through force alone or through unilateral measures that could expose innocent civilians to further loss of life, property or displacement,” the party maintained, calling for a strategy that combined “firm action against terrorism with protection of civilian populations and sensitivity to local realities”.

Accordingly, it proposed a meeting within 72 hours of authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments to develop a mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism. It also proposed consultation with political parties represented in the KP Assembly, elected representatives, tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders in order for the policy to enjoy public confidence and be implemented effectively.

PTI also rejected attempts to characterise the position of KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as political obstinacy, arguing that “had access to Imran Khan been facilitated, the chief minister could have consulted the PTI chairman directly on security and counterterrorism policy, potentially helping to bridge differences and create greater consensus”.

Responding to the press conference held by federal ministers after the talks ended without result, PTI said the government should address the substantive issues that prevented progress instead of seeking to place the responsibility on the opposition.

It called for an explanation as to why immediate access to Imran was considered unacceptable, why requests regarding his medical care were not accommodated, and why the proposed broader consultative approach was not accepted for developing a sustainable security strategy in KP.

The party reiterated that it remains “prepared to engage in political dialogue, constitutional processes, meaningful consultation and national consensus to address Imran Khan’s health and treatment, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, political stability, terrorism and the wider challenges confronting Pakistan”.

The party stressed, however, that “meaningful negotiations” could not succeed through predetermined positions or demands for unconditional endorsement.

“Serious dialogue requires flexibility, mutual confidence, consultation and a genuine willingness to translate discussions into practical progress,” the statement added.

‘Three fundamental red lines’

Separately, Opposition Chief Whip Malik Aamir Dogar stated that the talks had fallen through on “three fundamental red lines”: meetings with Imran, his medical treatment, and KP’s terrorism policy.

“We made it clear that the authority to call off the long march rests solely with Imran Khan sahib, so a meeting with him is essential,” he said in a post on X.

The MNA added that, when the government was unwilling to do this, an alternative demand for Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas’s meeting with Imran was also put forward, but similarly rejected.

On the PTI founder’s health, Dogar said that the opposition’s minimum demand had been the inclusion of his personal physicians in his treatment to dispel “doubts and suspicions” about his health. This, too, was not agreed to, which heightened the opposition’s concerns.

The third “red line”, he said, was that the opposition demanded that “no decision be made unilaterally” regarding KP’s security and terrorism policy, but rather that all relevant stakeholders be taken into confidence.

“Instead of broad consultations on this matter, the government sought hasty decisions within 72 hours,” he said.

As a result of the government’s refusal of these demands and the party’s refusal to back down from them, he added, the negotiations ended in a deadlock.

Salman Akram notes Centre’s ‘insistence on unilateral’ CT measures

Earlier, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of talks with the Centre was the latter’s insistence on “unilateral” counter-terrorism measures in KP.

In a post on X, Raja wrote that the “primary reason for the failure of the talks around 3am this morning” was that the “PTI-TTAP team stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions in KPK would be based on agreement between the federal government and the KPK government”.

He said the opposition wanted those actions to be “framed on the basis of consultation with, and the buy-in of, the different political parties represented” in the KP Assembly.

“This was not acceptable to the government team, that insisted that all actions unilaterally initiated by it would have to be owned by the provincial government,” Raja asserted.

“The PTI-TTAP team was clear that we have zero tolerance for terrorism and are committed to rooting it out. We also have a clear position against so-called collateral damage in the form of innocent lives and internal displacement of the local population.”

Raja noted that counterterrorism policies require support from the local population and ground intelligence.

“The wisdom provided by the jirga held in the KP assembly of all the political and tribal notables of the province, including the merged districts, must be heeded.

“This was not acceptable to the federal government,” he wrote.

In November last year, a peace jirga held at the KP Assembly, also attended by the governor, demanded that the Centre consult the KP government over Afghan policy.

Tarar accuses KP govt of ‘supporting’ terrorism

On the other hand, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar responded to Raja in a lengthy post on X, questioning why the KP government has not taken action against terrorism.

“It is only now, when your KP government is politically weak, [that] you have started responding to the federal government’s calls for [a] joint mechanism to fight terrorism, that too only as a strategy to save your political capital in KP,” the minister alleged.

“This is an old strategy of PTI, that when under pressure, they start talking of consultations and joint actions, but on [the] ground they do the exact opposite.”

Accusing the KP government of “double standards and hypocrisy”, Tarar contended that while it said it was taking steps to fight terrorism, its “narrative on terrorism is in favour of terrorists”.

“KPK government’s policy only encourages and supports [the] spread of terrorism in the province,” the PML-N leader alleged.

Tarar questioned why the KP government had not taken steps against terrorism or convened the provincial apex committee for meetings and why it had not condemned the “TTA regime for sponsoring terrorism inside Pakistan and conduct of cross-border attacks on the posts and drone attacks by them”.

“Why hasn’t the KPK Government not implemented NAP as per which clear action is required against illegal spectrum, illegal Afghan immigrants, measures for capacity enhancement of Police and [Counter-Terrorism Department]?” he added.

He asked why PTI leaders did not visit checkposts of security forces and police to express their support, and whether they had taken interest in the governance and development of esrtwhile Fata.

The minister urged the PTI to “stop selling this false narrative of collective consultations, jirgas or any other method, as this means nothing on [the] ground other than delaying tactics”.

Tarar reiterated his comments in a televised video statement, slamming the PTI for failing to abandon “double standards and hypocrisy”, which he said resulted in deadly terrorist attacks in KP.

“We were considering that they may go back on their word, and I had been saying it for the past two and a half weeks: if we are going to talk, then who should we talk to? And if we talk, what guarantee do we have that they will honour their word?” the minister asked.

He accused the PTI of taking U-turns and “expressing pride in them”, as well as failing to maintain a steady stance on the issue of protecting the lives and property of KP’s residents.

“Now different statements are emerging: Salman Akram Raja is saying one thing; [Adviser to KP Chief Minister on Information] Shafi Jan is saying that they want to change the policy on terrorism,” he added. “What is your policy? Does it even exist?”

Tarar alleged: “The only policy you have is deliberately supporting terrorism. Your policy is how you can elevate terrorists, how you can build a political terror-crime nexus and how you can spread terrorism across the province.

“I said earlier that you have to decide whether you stand with Pakistan or Afghanistan. You take the benefits of Pakistan, but are in favour of Afghanistan.”

“The policy change they are talking about is to give terrorists cover and protection,” Tarar further claimed.

He said people of KP were being killed in terrorist incidents because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi “wants to free one prisoner”.

“Lives have been wasted and people have been martyred because the province’s CM prioritises the release of one convicted prisoner,” he insisted. “This is why I say they (PTI) are TTP’s (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) B-team and TTA’s (Afghan Taliban) C-team,” the PML-N leader alleged.

The minister further accused the KP government of having a “pro-terrorism mindset”, which he contended had contributed to a failure to prevent terrorist attacks and cross-border firing from Afghanistan.

“Because their mindset is pro-terrorism, then they don’t care that security forces, armed forces, police, and thousands of officers and troops have been martyred,” Tarar claimed.

“They cannot even honour their martyrs … They burned the Chagai monument in Peshawar. This is a terrorist mindset; can they stop terrorism with this mindset in govt? No, they never will,” the minister asserted.

The minister continued denouncing the PTI, accusing it of not building a forensic lab or creating a Counter-Terrorism Department, failing to install Safe City cameras and being unable to fortify police check posts.

“You’ll be surprised to know that since they took power, they have received over Rs700 billion for counter-terrorism under the NFC Award,” Tarar claimed, adding that it is “extra”.

“This year, if you look at the figures, they have earmarked Rs45bn for police capacity building and counter-terrorism, but only released Rs1.5bn. The rest is for salaries and expenses. Is this how the war on terrorism will be fought?” he asked.

Earlier on Sunday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that the weekend talks collapsed as the PTI had initiated its long march, accusing KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations.

“Their team was reasonable. I am repeating that I will not blame anyone else for all of this collapsing. There is only one person responsible for the entire collapse, and that is the KP chief minister,” the interior minister declared.

He further said that Afridi was to be responsible “if there is any loss of life”. He said those supporting the PTI leader should “realise that they will be committing contempt of court, and we will take legal action against them to every possible extent”.

World.title: Yemen presidency announces military drive to retake all territory seized by Houthis
World.content:
Yemen’s leader announced on Sunday the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the group made fresh gains on the ground, effectively encircling a government-held city.

The announcement sets an ambitious goal for the embattled government, which recently lost swathes of the country’s Red Sea coastline and areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait — a chokepoint for international shipping — after a lightning offensive by Houthis.

Yemen’s government has struggled to roll back the surge, even with the military support of Saudi Arabia, where the Houthis said they had attacked oil infrastructure in the capital yet again on Sunday.

“I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory,” Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement.

Alimi called on all the armed forces “to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia”.

The statement came just hours after the Houthis cut a vital supply route linking the besieged city of Taiz with the government’s interim capital Aden, according to four security sources.

The Houthi advance followed days of heavy fighting in and around Taiz, where dozens of combatants were reported killed on Friday.

The battle for Taiz is taking place on several fronts, including highlands overlooking coastal areas recently seized by the Houthis. Taiz is Yemen’s third-largest city after Sanaa and Aden.

“We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station,” a police source in the area told AFP.

Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and the supply route, with traffic along the road halted and the group now surrounding Taiz city.

The military sources added that fighting in the area was ongoing.

Sources from both sides told AFP on Sunday that fighting in and around the western province of Taiz has killed more than 70 people over the past day.

Sources from the internationally recognised government reported that 34 government troops were killed — 20 on the edge of Taiz province in neighbouring Lahj — while Houthi military sources said 39 of their fighters were killed in fighting across Taiz and in border areas with Lahj.

Taiz city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen’s long-running civil war.

“They’ve achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven’t fully taken control of it,” Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP.

Muslimi also downplayed expectations over what the coming government offensive might accomplish. “In my opinion, it’s meaningless,” he added.

But Taiz residents vowed to resist any Houthi advance.

“We will defeat and crush anyone who enters the city of Taiz. We will not abandon Taiz,” resident Zakaria Al-Dhubhani said.

“This is a message to the Houthis: I swear to God, we will not allow you to advance a single inch into the city.”

Saudi attacks

Following several years of relative calm, Yemen’s civil war reignited in July against the backdrop of the wider conflict in the Middle East.

It has also drawn in Saudi Arabia — leader of an anti-Houthi military coalition since 2015 — with the group regularly claiming attacks on the kingdom’s territory in recent weeks and declaring a blockade of its ships in the Red Sea.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree on Sunday said the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi energy giant Aramco’s sites in Riyadh and in the oil-rich Khurais area in the east.

“The strikes were precise, causing large fires at the targeted sites,” Saree said on X.

Saudi oil exports were already under pressure thanks to Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.

The Houthis’ Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes on Sunday in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.

They came a day after Yemen’s government said its forces struck Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group’s positions near Taiz in the southwest.

The Yemeni government’s air capabilities, however, are limited, and the Saudi-led coalition has long been the primary force carrying out airstrikes against the Houthis.

Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes as well.

Yemen is one of the poorest countries in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis that has unspooled since the civil war broke out in 2014.

That year the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-led government, before going on to take control of much of the country’s north, with Riyadh’s international coalition intervening the following year.

Hunger warning

Hostilities between the Houthis and Yemen’s government had reignited after four years of a fragile truce when Iran sent a plane to Sanaa carrying a Houthi delegation.

The flight did not seek authorisation from Saudi Arabia, contravening a practice in place for a decade.

Riyadh retaliated with strikes on Sanaa airport, and in response the Houthis attacked Saudi territory for the first time since 2022.

Since then, fighting has intensified with the Houthis launching a lightning offensive in which they seized control of coastal regions along the Bab al-Mandab strait.

They have also struck multiple Saudi targets including oil infrastructure and the capital Riyadh while also announcing a naval blockade on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea.

The renewed fighting has worsened a humanitarian crisis sweeping Yemen, with the World Food Programme warning on Friday that three-quarters of the population was unable to meet its basic food needs.

World.title: Naqvi says talks with opposition have collapsed, accuses KP CM of 'sabotaging' negotiations
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Sunday that the talks between the federal government and the opposition had collapsed as the PTI had initiated its long march, accusing Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi of “sabotaging” the negotiations.

Naqvi was addressing a press conference in Lahore after an hours-long second round of talks between the two sides ended without yielding any results.

“Their team was reasonable. I am repeating that I will not blame anyone else for all of this collapsing. There is only one person responsible for the entire collapse, and that is the KP chief minister,” the interior minister declared.

He further said that Afridi was to be responsible “if there is any loss of life”. He said those supporting the PTI leader should “realise that they will be committing contempt of court, and we will take legal action against them to every possible extent”.

He warned that no one would be allowed to violate the Islamabad High Court’s order regarding protest. The IHC order, issued on Sept 14, ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”.

Notably, Naqvi stressed that there “had been no request from our side for the long march to be postponed”.

“When we had the first meeting, we told them that the long march was not an issue for us. However, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto had already given an indication and had also given a date. A day earlier, he had said that the PPP wanted the long march to be postponed and for the temperature to be brought down,” he added.

Naqvi explained that the PTI was given the option to hold a protest but would not allow an attempt to “create a disturbance”.

“We gave them this option. Now, if they violate the orders, whether they are workers or politicians, whether they are protesting within KP or outside KP, we will pursue them one by one. This time, we want to ensure that this repeated episode of creating a disturbance in Islamabad comes to an end,” he asserted.

According to the interior minister, there were two agreements to be reached — one was a “main agreement” that would cover whatever was being decided with the opposition parties, and the other was regarding counterterrorism.

“If we had known that no one in this committee was authorised to give a commitment on behalf of the KP government, or that the KP government would veto all these things, we would not have held the negotiations in this form in the first place,” he remarked.

The minister said the two sides had agreed “100 per cent on political things” so that the KP government could come on board with the Centre on the counterterrorism issues.

“It is not appropriate that there is a war going on in one province and the ministers there are giving statements against the army, are not coming to funerals, and at the local level, somewhere or the other, terrorists are also being given support,” he added.

“If there is a military operation, would you tell the army which gun to use or which drone to use? This happens nowhere in the world,” he said.

Naqvi detailed Saturday’s developments: “I requested CM Afridi to onboard the KP government because, definitely, the problems we are facing are coming from the KP government. He said, ‘Okay, I am going now,’ so we postponed the meeting until tomorrow. All members agreed to the postponement.

“They (opposition team) held negotiations with CM Afridi for four hours. The KP CM gave them his feedback and gave them the mandate that whatever they finalise with him, they should proceed with it.”

The interior minister accused Afridi of changing the draft of the agreement despite what had been agreed to earlier.

“When I forwarded the draft to the KP chief minister, around 9pm he became active. Once the draft is finalised, he asks for changes once and then asks again, and by 12am or 12:30am at night, he brings an entirely new draft. And in that, he changed the things that we had locked after discussing them,” Naqvi asserted.

In an apparent jibe at the KP CM, Naqvi noted that placing “immature and inexperienced people in positions of authority had consequences for the country”.

“You have seen in the past how chief ministers came to this province and the country continued to suffer the consequences. Similarly, if an immature boy sits in a position of authority, has no experience and has not seen politics, then definitely he will call himself a representative of the people, but he will make decisions in the same way as my team and I witnessed yesterday.”

Commending the government’s delegation, the minister said: “They worked non-stop for 12 hours and, even before that, made sincere efforts to resolve the issue. I will give them credit for the fact that at no point did they say no. They remained focused on resolving the matter. From the smallest issue to the major ones, all the members made a sincere effort to resolve them in a good manner.”

Naqvi meets Kundi at Governor House

Naqvi then went to Peshawar, where he met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.

According to a statement issued by the Governor House, both leaders expressed concerns over the “risk of facilitating terrorists to safely cross security checkposts” during the PTI’s Islamabad march.

They agreed that whenever the president and the prime minister deemed it necessary to impose governor’s rule or emergency to “save the province from terrorism and destruction, the Governor’s House will play a full Constitutional role”.

The interior minister and the governor discussed important matters at the provincial level, including growing unrest in the province, the political scenario, and the situation arising from the Islamabad march.

The statement read that the KP government’s attitude during the negotiation regarding counterterrorism actions was tantamount to enmity toward the people and the province.

Naqvi and Kundi also termed the use of helicopters and other government resources by Afridi and the provincial ministers for the march as a “blatant violation” of the IHC verdict.

Other matters of mutual interest were also discussed in the meeting, and consultations were held on numerous issues, according to the statement.

Kundi said in his own statement that KP Inspector General of Police Zulfikar Hameed was also present at the meeting, which revolved around the prevailing security situation in the province.

“The security of our people remains our foremost priority. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has sacrificed enough, and every institution must work together to protect our people and defeat terrorism,” the governor said.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visited Naqvi’s residence to offer condolences over the death of his maternal uncle, Akmal Hussain Naqvi.

According to the PM Office, the interior minister also briefed PM Shehbaz in detail on the “key negotiations held last night and the progress made” so far.

PM Shehbaz also met with PML-N President Nawaz Sharif to discuss the “overall political situation in the country”, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported.

Matters of international importance were also discussed during the meeting, which was attended by Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz as well, the report added.

Conditions and demands

Earlier in the day, Naqvi also claimed on X that the KP government had agreed to sign a written agreement and submit an implementation plan within 72 hours, mainly covering counterterrorism initiatives, during the talks held over the weekend, but then backtracked.

According to Naqvi, the PTI had agreed to:

Reconsider the Police Act 2026 in light of the security situation and the need to protect security matters from political interference

Prevent terrorists from operating freely or finding safe havens in the province

Unequivocal condemnation of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and all other terrorist groups

Support the national policy on Afghan refugees, including repatriation and dismantling Afghan camps in KP

No contact with the interim Afghan government

Substantial funding for counterterrorism operations and the police

Full provincial ownership of counterterrorism measures and stronger cooperation with the armed forces

Decisions on counterterrorism in the former Fata and merged districts

Implementation of the National Action Plan

“Last night, during the final phase of negotiations, the KP government backed out of these commitments. Security must not be politicised while the province is at war,” he said.

The meeting between the opposition and federal government at Parliament House began after 4pm on Saturday, with discussions focusing on the PTI’s planned Oct 4 march to Islamabad. The talks extended into the early hours of Sunday without yielding any results.

However, shortly before 3am on Sunday, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who was part of the opposition delegation, told the media that the talks had not resulted in a breakthrough.

He went on to say that the deadlock was over jailed PTI founder Imran Khan’s meeting with his personal physicians, and how to address terrorism in KP.

But Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, who was part of the government’s delegation, said the talks failed primarily because the “KP government could not assure whether they would cooperate in the fight against terrorism in the future”. He alleged that the PTI’s provincial government in KP did not want to implement the NAP and that the PTI delegation that participated in the talks had also left the venue “disappointed because the KP government did not cooperate on terrorism”.

Following these allegations, CM Afridi posted on X that he was sharing the text of the draft he sent to the opposition’s negotiating team, saying that “no even one demand in there was unconstitutional or illegal”.

He then went on to list the demands, calling for:

Arrangements for meetings between the prime minister and the leaders of the opposition in both houses of Parliament to discuss important political, national, constitutional, legal, and democratic issues, particularly those facing delays. “The two sides shall be bound to ensure effective and feasible progress within two months towards resolving the aforementioned matters through mutual consultation and negotiations.”

The prime minister to form a joint political negotiating committee comprising representatives from the ruling coalition, the PPP and opposition parties. “This committee shall engage in continuous negotiations with the opposition on national and political matters, points of disagreement, and other important issues, and shall seek feasible solutions through mutual consensus. The committee shall ensure significant progress on negotiations and resolutions within one month of its formation and shall present its recommendations to the relevant leadership.”

Ensuring all legal, human and medical rights for Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, in accordance with the jail manual, Constitution and prevailing laws. “Where legally applicable, necessary medical facilities and treatment shall be provided to them, taking into account the opinion, instructions and advice of their personal or nominated physicians.”

Allowing Imran and Bushra Bibi to meet their family members, lawyers and other associates, in accordance with the jail manual and relevant laws. “Such meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the law and jail rules and regulations. However, the facility of meetings will not be used by any party for political or other purposes prohibited by law.”

The process of taking up appeals filed by prisoners against their sentences to be initiated or completed within 10 days, where legally possible, in accordance with the Constitution and law. “All cases shall be decided by the relevant courts and legal forums in accordance with the Constitution, law, transparent judicial procedures and principles of justice, without undue delay. And women who are political prisoners, including Yasmin Rashid and Bushra Bibi, should be released expeditiously on humanitarian grounds.”

Effective, continuous and meaningful consultation between the federal and provincial governments to eradicate terrorism, protect the lives and property of the people and establish lasting peace in KP. “Existing policies and measures should be reviewed and amended as needed.”

Authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments shall convene regular meetings within 72 hours and, through mutual consultation, formulate a clear, comprehensive and feasible strategy for peace and security. The implementation of this strategy, within the scope of the Constitution and law, shall be the joint responsibility of the federal and provincial governments.”

The KP CM said that PTI would announce the cancellation of the long march upon receiving a written assurance from the federal government for the effective implementation of the aforementioned assurances and agreed actions.

“However, if the federal government violates the agreed assurances, the negotiation process, or constitutional and legal requirements, or causes undue disruption to the negotiation process, PTI shall reserve the right to peaceful, democratic and lawful protest in accordance with the Constitution and law”, he added.

Responding to Afridi on X, Naqvi said the “negotiating teams finalised a separate draft with us, which both sides agreed to, in addition to the KP Terrorism Related Implementation Plan”.

Commenting on that, KP Information Minister Shafiullah Jan said the PTI’s negotiating committee “came with a full mandate that we would endorse every decision they made, however they deemed fit”.

“The provincial government’s mandate lies with the chief minister. The KP government’s policy cannot go against Imran Khan’s ideology. Your intent is not to end terrorism but to end PTI,” Jan asserted.

“The blood of our innocent Pakhtuns is not so cheap that, under your misguided policies, we would sacrifice another 80,000 lives. Terrorism has been forcibly imposed on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Those who start the fire can never put it out,” he claimed.

The provincial minister stressed that a policy shift regarding counterterrorism was necessary as “relying solely on the policy of guns and batons will not work”.

“A few self-proclaimed wise men sitting in closed rooms will not decide our future,” Jan said.

PPP says KP govt ‘began dictating terms’

PPP Senator Sherry Rehman, who was part of the talks, also blamed the KP chief minister, saying the talks “collapsed on the KP government’s unilateral refusal to sign the afternoon’s pre-agreed draft on counterterrorism cooperation with the Centre”.

In a post on X, she emphasised that the idea behind the agreement was to bring the province on board on all counterterrorism actions.

The PPP leader said the government’s team had repeatedly asked for the provincial government of KP to be in the talks as well, but the chief minister or cabinet representatives did not turn up. “If they had a viable draft, they should have shown up themselves or communicated it to their committee over the two days, without constant reversals”, she added.

“No point presenting new drafts on social media after refusing to show up or sabotaging their own teams by broadcasting messages that subvert the process,” Rehman stated.

The senior politician went on to say: “I have never in my 25 years in parliament seen such a reckless squandering of an opening to begin political CBMs (confidence-building measures), and to bring stability to Pakistan after years of bitter political division.”

Rehman regretted that instead of “taking the opportunity the PPP-govt team offered them to unlock the blind alley they have taken themselves into, their Peshawar government began dictating terms after 8:30pm when all but final agreements had been signed”.

“We really went more than halfway. The rest could have followed.”

World.title: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's links to the country, police say
World.content:
A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating links to Australia of the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, who allegedly stabbed his captain and then attempted to hijack the plane, a police spokesperson said on Sunday.

The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team — which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency — was “investigating the man’s links to Australia”, the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said.

Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, the capital of the Australian state of Victoria. A third source said he studied at RMIT University around a decade ago. RMIT declined to comment.

The co-pilot of the flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a “terrorist attack”.

Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a “vertical roller coaster” when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.

Co-pilot in UAE custody

Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hamami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman. UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot’s identity.

Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hamami, who is in UAE custody, for comment. The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel.

Oman has not commented on the incident.

Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane.

Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals.

A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday.

The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited “mosques and extremist websites” while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation. Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to FT.

Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours.

Netanyahu orders security review of flights

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a security review of international flights to Israel after the incident.

Netanyahu “has instructed the Head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel”, a statement from the premier’s office said.

Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also claimed pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

Calls have mounted in Israel for an investigation into the security lapse.

Transport Minister Miri Regev rejected responsibility for the failure, saying security oversight for flights operated by foreign airlines falls under the remit of the Mossad and Shin Bet, Israel’s foreign and domestic intelligence agencies.

A 2024 report by the state comptroller found there was no clear division of responsibility for the security of foreign airlines operating in Israel, and recommended that the government address the issue.

Israeli media has reported that pilots from countries hostile to Israel have repeatedly flown into the country in recent years.

Opposition leader Yair Lapid dismissed Netanyahu’s announcement of a security review as a “sham investigation”.

“The chain of failures that preceded the incident could have led to a disaster of historic proportions, and this is how an Israeli prime minister responds?” Lapid wrote on X.

“Just as Netanyahu escaped an investigation into the October 7 massacre, he is now running away again,” he added.

Gadi Eisenkot, a leading challenger to Netanyahu ahead of the October 27 election, wrote on X that “in a proper and functioning government, the minister of transportation would have submitted a letter of resignation last night”.

World.title: UK's Green Party adopts 'Zionism is racism' policy
World.content:
The UK’s left-wing Green Party on Sunday voted to define Zionism as racism at the party’s annual get-together, drawing sharp backlash from British Jewish groups and the Israeli government.

Members of the Greens, which has five members in Britain’s 650-seat parliament and which enjoyed a boost in recent local and special elections, backed the motion at the party’s conference, with 1,022 votes in favour and 813 against.

According to the motion, Zionism would be “treated as any other form of racism”, and the party supports the establishment of a “single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine”.

“This has been a serious and deeply felt debate within our membership,” a Green spokesperson said.

Later, the party issued a joint statement by Leader Zack Polanski, its co-deputy leaders and five MPs noting that it will not tolerate discrimination.

“We will continue to stand in opposition to genocide, ethnic cleansing, apartheid and the illegal occupation,” the statement reads. “We will continue to call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government, and we will continue to work to ensure that the Green Party is an anti-racist party in every way.

It adds, “We know there is no conflict between supporting the rights of Palestinians and the rights of Jewish people.”

The Greens have enjoyed a surge in popularity under Polanski’s charismatic leadership, attracting voters dissatisfied with the centre-left Labour government’s stance on Israel’s military campaign in Gaza. However, Polanski’s popularity has taken a hit in recent months, polls show, following several missteps.

“This motion would make the Green Party the first electorally significant UK political party in living memory to adopt what appears to be an overtly antisemitic political platform,” three Jewish community groups said in a letter to the party ahead of the vote.

“We also emphasised the implications for the safety and welfare of all British Jews,” the heads of the Board of Deputies, Community Security Trust and Jewish Leadership Council warned.

Israel’s foreign ministry said the policy went “far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate”.

“Every political party in Britain, first and foremost the governing Labour Party, must unequivocally reject this twisted resolution,” it said.

The motion laid bare divisions in the party, with Polanski — who is currently running to become an MP in former prime minister Keir Starmer’s London constituency — skipping the vote.

Despite at least three out of five Green MPs opposing the motion, Polanski said earlier this week that the “displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people” was “clearly racism”.

United Nations investigators have accused Israel of committing “genocide” in the war in Gaza, a finding that Israel has rejected.

World.title: 4 injured Pakistanis rescued from vessel hijacked in Somalia arrive in Karachi with remains of 3 colleagues
World.content:
The four Pakistanis who were injured during a security operation to recover a hijacked oil tanker off the coast of Somalia, along with the remains of three others who lost their lives in the episode, arrived in Karachi on Sunday evening.

The crew members of MT Honour 25 reached Karachi after departing from Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa via Ethiopian Airlines flight ET 694.

Sindh Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Labour Minister Saeed Ghani, PPP Senator Waqar Mehdi, MQM-P MNA Farooq Sattar and others welcomed the rescued seamen upon their arrival at Jinnah International Airport.

Shah said the loss of lives and injuries was an “extremely regrettable incident” and extended his condolences to the bereaved families.

The minister said all expenses for the treatment and care of the injured will be borne by the Sindh government, with the wounded to be taken to Aga Khan Hospital.

Pakistan’s ambassadors to Djibouti and Ethiopia had seen off the four injured Pakistani crew members — Usman Ghani, Aqeel Khan, Ameen bin Shams and Yasir Khan — along with the mortal remains of Rafiullah Khan, Syed Kashif Umer and Mahmood Ahmad Ansari from Addis Ababa.

The seven were among 10 Pakistanis aboard MT Honour 25, which was hijacked by Somali pirates in April. Apart from Pakistanis, the vessel’s crew also included seven Indonesians, an Indian and a Sri Lankan.

For around five months, there had been no progress either in negotiations or in the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for the recovery of the hostages, despite concerns abounding about their declining health.

Since the hijacking, the crew made several emotional videos and audio appeals , reporting that they ran out of clean water, food and medicine.

For its part, FO maintained that it remained “actively engaged” to secure the release of the sailors.

On Sept 29, Somali maritime police recovered the Palau-flagged oil tanker amid reports of casualties among the crew.

During the operation, it said, 21 suspected pirates were apprehended, while operations to locate the remaining members continue.

“Before the operation [had] begun, the pirates on board the ship killed five of the crew. Among those killed were three from Pakistan, one from Myanmar and one from India,” it said.

Advocate Quratulain of the Ansar Burney Trust, however, gave a separate account of the events, saying the pirates had brought the hostages onto the deck when they realised Puntland forces were approaching.

“They tied their hands and warned to kill them if the police force came anywhere near them without paying them the ransom,” she said, adding that the ransom demand had by then been reduced from an initial $3 million to $1m.

She said the pirates opened fire on the hostages as the security forces proceeded with the operation, killing three Pakistanis, one Indian and one Myanmar national.

World.title: US Marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of murder
World.content:
A US Marine stationed on Japan’s southern island of Okinawa was arrested on suspicion of the murder of a Japanese woman, police said on Sunday.

Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday and taking her wallet and backpack, ​police said. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-run and drunk-driving accidents by US personnel have long sparked protests on Okinawa, which bears a disproportionate burden of hosting about 70 per cent of US military facilities in Japan.

US Ambassador George Glass posted on social media that he had spoken with Japan’s foreign ministry and Okinawa’s governor, offering “our sincere condolences and pledging full cooperation as the investigation continues”.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan had lodged a protest with US authorities and called the crime “exceptionally brutal and vicious”.

The government has urged the US “to provide maximum cooperation with the investigation, enforce stricter discipline among US military personnel, and take thorough measures to prevent the recurrence of similar crimes,” Takaichi said in a post on X.
